title: Surface an actionable error when the Connect server URL redirects
description:
## Context

#4262 was closed as wontfix: Publisher will not follow HTTP redirects with credentials across origin changes, and #4315 fixes the common case (http→https upgrade) by resolving redirects once at credential-creation time and storing the post-redirect URL.

That leaves stale credentials — created before #4315 lands, or pointing at servers that later add an `[HTTPRedirect]` config or migrate to a new host. When such a credential is used to publish, the failure messages are misleading:

- **Host change** (e.g. server migration): axios's `follow-redirects` transport strips `Authorization` when the redirect crosses to a different, non-subdomain host, so the first publish request (`GET /__api__/v1/user`) follows the redirect unauthenticated and gets a 401. The user sees "authorization failed," which is misleading — their API key is fine; their credential URL is stale.
- **http→https upgrade on the same host**: `follow-redirects` preserves `Authorization` on an https upgrade, so every preflight request silently succeeds, and the publish fails at the bundle upload (the one request with `maxRedirects: 0`) with `Unexpected response from the server (302: ...)` — no hint that a redirect occurred or where it pointed.

## Proposal

Detect 3xx responses and surface an actionable error, e.g.:

> Your server URL redirects to `https://…`. Update your credential's server URL and try again.

At minimum this should cover:

- `testAuthentication` (catches host-change redirects before auth is stripped mid-flight — a 3xx with `maxRedirects: 0` on this probe, or inspection of the final URL, would reveal the redirect)
- `uploadBundle` in `@posit-dev/connect-api`, where a 3xx currently falls into the generic "Unexpected response" branch of `classifyDeploymentError`

No redirect should be followed with credentials attached; the goal is purely a better error message pointing the user at the fix.

title: Cannot create a credential for a Connect server that redirects http to https
description:
## Problem

With a Connect server configured with `[HTTPRedirect]` (http://host:3939 redirects to https://host:3443), Add Credential fails no matter how the URL is entered when **Verify TLS Certificates** is disabled:

- `http://host:3939` → `Error: Invalid URL (unable to validate connectivity with Server URL - Protocol "http:" not supported. Expected "https:".)`
- `host:3939` → `Error: Invalid URL (unable to validate connectivity with Server URL - Unable to reach the server. ...)` (Publisher defaults to https, and a TLS handshake against the plain-HTTP port fails; this is expected — type the scheme explicitly)

## Causes

1. When certificate verification is disabled, the custom transport in `@posit-dev/connect-api` hard-codes `https.request`, so any `http:` URL fails with Node's `ERR_INVALID_PROTOCOL`. This also breaks **all** plain-http Connect servers when verification is disabled, redirect or not.
2. That transport also does not follow redirects, so the http→https upgrade redirect can never be followed in insecure mode.
3. Even in secure mode, where axios follows the redirect, the post-redirect URL is discarded — the credential is stored with the typed `http://` URL, so every subsequent request (including ones carrying `Authorization` headers) first goes out over plaintext http.

## Fix

- Dispatch the insecure transport on the request protocol (`http.request` vs `https.request`).
- Resolve redirects once, unauthenticated, while validating the server URL, and store the resolved (https) URL in the credential.

title: R version in deployment.toml should take precedence over renv.lock constraint
description:
*Problem*

When a user explicitly sets an R version in `deployment.toml` (e.g., `4.5.2`), but the `renv.lock` file contains a different R version (e.g., `4.4.0`), Publisher derives a `RequiresRVersion` constraint from the renv.lock (`~=4.4.0`) and then fails deployment with:

> Cannot find compatible environment: no compatible Local environment with R version 4.5.2 (~=4.4.0) and Quarto version 1.8.26.

*Expected Behavior*

1. The R version explicitly set in `deployment.toml` should take precedence over the version recorded in `renv.lock` for the `RequiresRVersion` constraint
2. Publisher should detect this conflict earlier and provide actionable guidance (e.g., "Your deployment.toml specifies R 4.5.2 but your renv.lock was created with R 4.4.0 — run `renv::snapshot()` with R 4.5.2 to update it")
3. The error message should make it clear which file is the source of the conflicting constraint

*Steps to Reproduce*

1. Have an R project with `renv.lock` created under R 4.4.x
2. Update `deployment.toml` to specify R version `4.5.2`
3. Attempt to publish

*Context*

Related (but different): #2648

title: correctly handle redirects on bundle upload
description:
To support streaming of large bundles, we had to disable Axios' automatic following of redirects. (#4249)

I believe prior to 2.0.0, publisher did not handle redirects (#18, #2372), and as far as I know we have not done specific testing of redirect handling with 2.x. However, this is still arguably a regression.

Other Connect clients have added custom redirect handling:

- https://github.com/posit-dev/posit-sdk-py/issues/385
- https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/674
- https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/1297

We should investigate whether something similar would work here.

For bundle uploads specifically, we should start a new stream from disk every time we make an upload request; we must not buffer the bundle in memory nor drop the POST body on retry.

title: downloadBundle buffers entire bundle in memory — large bundles fail to open
description:
## Problem statement

`ConnectAPI.downloadBundle` (`packages/connect-api/src/client.ts`) fetches a deployed bundle by reading the whole HTTP response into memory as an `ArrayBuffer` and returning a single `Uint8Array`:

```ts
async downloadBundle(contentId, bundleId, signal?): Promise<Uint8Array> {
  const { data } = await this.client.get<ArrayBuffer>(
    `/__api__/v1/content/${contentId}/bundles/${bundleId}/download`,
    { responseType: "arraybuffer", signal },
  );
  return new Uint8Array(data);
}
```

This is the same in-memory ceiling that #4249 fixed for the *upload* path, but on the *download/browse* path. The only caller is `connect_content_fs.ts` (`extractBundleTree(bundleBytes)`), which backs the "open Connect content bundle" file-system browsing feature. For a multi-GiB deployed bundle, buffering the full archive (plus the typed-array copy) will exhaust memory in the extension host and fail to open the content — and the tar extraction in `extractBundleTree` is also fully in-memory.

This was noted as a follow-up while fixing #4249 (streaming bundle upload). Upload now streams to/from a temp file; download was left out of scope.

## Expected behavior

Opening/browsing a large deployed bundle should not be limited by available memory.

## Suggested approach

Mirror the #4249 upload fix on the download side:

- Stream the download response (`responseType: "stream"`) to a temp file on disk instead of buffering it.
- Have `extractBundleTree` (or the `connect_content_fs.ts` caller) read entries from the on-disk tar.gz via a streaming extractor rather than from an in-memory `Uint8Array`.
- Clean up the temp file when the cached content root is evicted / no longer needed.

## Notes

- Affected: `packages/connect-api/src/client.ts` (`downloadBundle`), `extensions/vscode/src/connect_content_fs.ts` (`extractBundleTree` and the bundle fetch/cache path).
- Related: #4249 (streaming bundle upload).

title: When Publisher creates a `renv` and `renv.lock` it is then treated as the source of truth
description:
If a user that isn't using `renv` for a project deploys using Publisher, a `renv` folder and `renv.lock` are created.

This can be re-created with the `shinyapp` we have in `test/sample-content` by deleting the `renv` and `renv.lock` (if you have one) and deploying.

Once that `renv.lock` is created Publisher treats that as the source of truth on re-deploys which is a problem for users who expecting to not use `renv` at all.

Their `renv.lock` never gets updated by Publisher (since it was already made and is now being used without being re-made).

This causes a problem if you then add a new `library(...)` call. The `renv.lock` wont have that new library, so the re-deploy with fail.

title: bug: Publisher missing dependencies when using `::` operator in Shiny R directory
description:
If a user is not using `renv` and is using a library without a `library(...)` command the library won't be discovered when publishing.

Connect will complain about missing `connectapi`, for example.

Ideally Publisher is better respecting the double-colon operator `::`

## Use Case

This specifically came from using Shiny which uses [the `R/` directory](https://shiny.posit.co/r/articles/build/app-formats/#the-r-directory). It sources all files in the R directory automatically which included a `connectapi::` reference in this case.

Publisher doesn't see the `::` dependencies that are in the R directory, but `library()` references work.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a hello world shiny app.
2. Create an R directory in the same folder as the `app.R` file.
3. Create `autosource.R` in the R directory as follows

```
# library(connectapi)
print("IN AUTOSOURCED R FILE")
print(connectapi::set_environment_all)
```

Uncommenting out the `library(connectapi)` call and it works. Otherwise it fails.

### References

- https://shiny.posit.co/r/articles/build/app-formats/#the-r-directory
- https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-intro.html#Namespaces-1
- https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-intro.html#Packages-1

title: Snowflake: PRIVATE_KEY_PATH env override ignored when TOML has no private_key_file
description:
## Summary

In `extensions/vscode/src/snowflake/connections.ts`, `listConnections()` runs `normalizeKeyPaths()` **before** `applyEnvVarOverrides()`:

```ts
normalizeKeyPaths(conns);     // line 232
applyEnvVarOverrides(conns);  // line 233
```

`normalizeKeyPaths()` collapses `private_key_path` into `private_key_file` and then deletes the `private_key_path` field. Because env-var overrides are applied *after* this step, a `SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_<NAME>_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` override is written into `private_key_path` on a connection that has already been normalized — so it is never folded into `private_key_file`.

Downstream (`CredentialsService.createSnowflakeConnection`) only reads `private_key_file`, so the override is silently ignored and JWT auth fails with `private_key_file is required for snowflake_jwt`.

## Reproduction

1. A `connections.toml` connection using `snowflake_jwt` with **no** `private_key_file` / `private_key_path` set in the file.
2. Set `SNOWFLAKE_CONNECTIONS_<NAME>_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH=/path/to/key.p8` in the environment.
3. Attempt Snowflake discovery / token fetch for that connection.

**Expected:** the env-provided key path is used for JWT auth.
**Actual:** the override lands in `private_key_path`, is never normalized to `private_key_file`, and the connection errors as if no key were provided.

(The TOML-only and `PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` env paths are unaffected.)

## Suggested fix

Reorder so normalization runs after env overrides:

```ts
applyEnvVarOverrides(conns);
normalizeKeyPaths(conns);
```

Add a unit test covering a `PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` env override with no key field in the TOML.

## Notes

Pre-existing; surfaced during review of the snowflake-sdk consolidation branch (`chris/snowflake-sdk-consolidation`). Not introduced by that change.

title: cache/memoize snowflake connections
description:
Follow-up to #4207.

We call https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/bd358d592d7e53ed7ec5a3b86b69e6f76b719527/extensions/vscode/src/credentials/service.ts#L51 to convert a stored credential into `ConnectAPIOptions`. This is a cheap transformation except in the case of Snowflake credentials. In that case it involves filesystem reads (to [look up the connection info](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/bd358d592d7e53ed7ec5a3b86b69e6f76b719527/extensions/vscode/src/credentials/service.ts#L98)) followed by API calls to Snowflake (to [get a token](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/bd358d592d7e53ed7ec5a3b86b69e6f76b719527/extensions/vscode/src/credentials/service.ts#L109)). This happens multiple times at extension launch and multiple times during a deployment. We should refactor this code to reduce the number of times we have to get a new token for sure, and ideally also reduce the number of filesystem reads.

This might also be a good opportunity to consolidate all of the snowflake auth options to use snowflake-sdk (like the externalbrowser option does), but that is technically separate work.

title: Show status indication when Publisher initiates background auth/API calls on startup
description:
When Publisher opens, it immediately begins loading credentials and making API calls (fetching available integrations, env vars for existing deployments, etc.) without the user explicitly initiating a deployment. With browser-based auth, this is particularly jarring because it can trigger a browser auth flow the user didn't expect.

## Problem

- Users see unexpected browser popups for auth without understanding why
- If there's no internet connection, the sidebar may be inaccurate with no explanation
- No indication that Publisher is "doing something" in the background

## Proposed solution

Show a status message or notification indicating that Publisher is performing setup/fetching server details. Some considerations:

- Showing a notification on every startup might be too noisy
- Could potentially show it only when browser-based auth is triggered
- VS Code has precedents for this (status bar messages, progress notifications)
- Need to balance informing users vs. being annoying

## Open questions

- Should this only appear when browser auth is involved, or always?
- Status bar vs. notification vs. sidebar loading state?
- Should there be a way to defer/cancel the initial fetch?

title: feat: remove token/key choice in new credential flow
description:
Now that token authentication works everywhere[^1], it would be simpler and less confusing to remove the "Token auth or API Key" choice in the new credential flow and just default to token. We have heard that customers are sometimes confused by the choice and think we don't support token auth, even though it is present as a choice and just works.

We need to continue to support API Key credentials that already exist.

We may want to consider having some way to still make a new API Key credential as a fallback in case somebody finds a situation where Token auth is not working. Maybe a separate command they can invoke from the command palette?

[^1]: We think. Verify that this is true! Search for open issues. We have tested and proved it works in Snowflake and Workbench. Try it with a proxy setup.

title: Support setting `metrics_collection_enabled` during deployment
description:
## Summary

When deploying content to Posit Connect via Publisher, there is currently no way to configure `metrics_collection_enabled` for the content item. This means users must manually enable resource metrics collection after deployment via the Connect Dashboard or API.

## Problem

Connect supports per-content resource metrics (CPU, memory, connection counts) via the `metrics_collection_enabled` field on content items. This can be set at creation time via `POST /v1/content` or updated afterward via `PATCH /v1/content/{guid}`. However, Publisher's configuration files (in `.posit/publish/`) don't expose this setting, so users deploying via Publisher cannot enable metrics collection as part of their deployment workflow.

## Proposed Solution

Add support for a configuration option (e.g., in the `.posit/publish/*.toml` configuration file) that maps to the `metrics_collection_enabled` field in the Connect API. When deploying, Publisher would include this field in the content creation/update API call.

Example configuration:

```toml
[connect.runtime]
metrics_collection_enabled = true
```

## Workarounds

- Set `Applications.MetricsCollectionEnabled = true` server-wide in `rstudio-connect.gcfg`
- Manually call `PATCH /v1/content/{guid}` after deployment
- Use the Connect Dashboard to enable metrics after deployment

## References

- [Connect API: Create content](https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/index.html#post-/v1/content-request-body)
- [Connect Admin Guide: Per-content job metrics](https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/operational-metrics/index.html#per-content-job-metrics)

title: Failed to Add Credentials in VS Code after Posit Connect Upgrade - "secretStorageKeys" API Error
description:
## Problem statement
When attempting to add Posit Connect credentials to the Posit Publisher extension in Visual Studio Code, the process fails. This issue started occurring immediately after our Posit Connect server was upgraded from version 2025.05 to 2026.04. The VS Code logs show a persistent warning that the extension cannot use the `secretStorageKeys` API, preventing it from saving credentials.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Go to the Posit Publisher extension sidebar in Visual Studio Code.
2. Click on the '+' icon to add a new server.
3. Enter the URL for our Posit Connect server and press Enter.
4. When prompted, select to add a new account and enter the credentials for that account.

**Expected behavior:** 
The Posit Publisher extension should successfully save the credentials, add the account, and connect to the Posit Connect server, allowing me to see my published content and deploy new content.

**Actual behavior:** 
The process fails after entering credentials. The account is not added to the extension. The VS Code logs show a `Failed to read credentials from SecretStorage` warning, and I am unable to publish content.

## System Details

- **Posit Publisher Version**: 2.6.0
- **Platform**: win32 x64
- **IDE**: Visual Studio Code 1.103.2

## Publishing information

- **Content type:** 
- All content types are affected as the issue is with adding the account itself, not publishing specific content.

**Connect version:** 2026.04

## Publisher output and logs

The key warning from the Visual Studio Code logs is as follows:

`[warning] Failed to read credentials from SecretStorage: Error: Extension 'posit.publisher' CANNOT use API proposal: secretStorageKeys. Its package.json#enabledApiProposals-property declares: [] but NOT secretStorageKeys. The missing proposal MUST be added and you must start in extension development mode or use the following command line switch: --enable-proposed-api posit.publisher`

I have already performed several troubleshooting steps, including:
*   Updating and reinstalling the Posit Publisher extension.
*   Launching VS Code with the `--enable-proposed-api posit.publisher` flag.
*   Checking the Windows Credential Manager for conflicting entries.

None of these steps have resolved the issue.

title: CI: @cypress/grep filter in e2e.yaml has been silently inert since v6 bump
description:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/e2e.yaml:230` invokes Cypress with `--env grepFilterSpecs=true,grepOmitFiltered=true,grepTags=-@uses-posit-connect-cloud` to exclude Connect-Cloud-tagged tests from the non-`release` Connect Server matrix entries. That filter hasn't been doing anything since the bump to `@cypress/grep` v6.0.0 in #3526.

## Root cause

`@cypress/grep` v5→v6 deprecated `Cypress.env()` for plugin configuration and moved to `Cypress.expose()`. The README's "From v5 to v6" migration section says the CLI must change from `--env grepTags="..."` to `--expose grepTags="..."`. #3526 updated the v4→v5 import API in `cypress.config.js` and `support/index.js` but missed this v5→v6 CLI step.

## Impact

The `@uses-posit-connect-cloud`-tagged tests run on all of the Connect Server matrix entries (`preview`, `2025.03.0`, `2023.03.0`, `release`) instead of just `release`. They pass because `PCC_USER_CCQA3` is also forwarded to every matrix entry via `pull-request.yaml:140-145`, so credentials are available wherever the tests run.

Net effect: the Connect Cloud tests run 3x more often than expected or needed.

## Fix

Change `--env` to `--expose` on `.github/workflows/e2e.yaml:230` (the non-`release` branch of the `if`).

## Related

- Dependency bump: #3526
- Tag rename PR: #4189

## Context

Part of #4115 — updating GitHub Actions that use deprecated Node.js 20.

`HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension@v2` still uses Node 20 and there is no newer release with Node 24 support. This action is used in `publish.yaml` for publishing to both the VS Marketplace and Open VSX Registry.

## Action needed

- Monitor https://github.com/HaaLeo/publish-vscode-extension for a new release that uses Node 24.
- Once available, update the two usages in `.github/workflows/publish.yaml` (lines 41 and 69).

## Deadline

GitHub will force Node.js 24 starting **June 16, 2026**. Node.js 20 will be removed from runners on **September 16, 2026**.

## Alternatives if upstream doesn't update in time

- Replace with direct `vsce publish` and `ovsx publish` CLI commands.
- Set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24=true` env var as a temporary workaround.


## UPDATE (6/3/26): 

The way forward I think is to produce a common GH action owned by posit to publish to the vsix registries. 

https://github.com/posit-dev/posit-gh-actions/pull/2

The actual code needed to implement the publish is really minimal - there's no need for anything beyond direct command line invocations, the action itself can just be tens of lines.

title: fix: list Node.js entrypoints in the Create a New Deployment quick picker
description:
## What happens

When a Node.js file (e.g. `app.ts`, `app.js`) is open in the editor:

- ✅ The editor-bar **Deploy with Posit Publisher** button shows up.
- ❌ The same file is **not** listed when you click **Add Deployment** → "Create a New Deployment".

Both should treat Node.js entrypoints the same way.

## Why

The "Create a New Deployment" picker filters open files by a static extension list that was never updated when Node.js support landed. The editor-bar button takes a different path — it runs the actual detector chain — so it doesn't have this problem.

## Fix

Add `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts` to the `ENTRYPOINT_FILE_EXTENSIONS` array in `extensions/vscode/src/constants.ts`. The Node.js detector already declares this exact set; the constants array just hasn't been kept in sync.

## How to verify

- Open `app.ts` in a Node.js project; click **Add Deployment**; confirm `app.ts` appears under "Open Files" in the picker.
- Repeat for `app.js`, `index.mjs`, `server.cjs`, etc.
- Confirm the existing Python/R/Quarto/HTML extensions still appear (no regression).

## Related

- #3964 — parent Node.js feature.
- #3997 — Node.js project detector (where the constants update was missed).
- #4001 / #4167 — publishing-flow PR that exposed this during manual testing.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

### Current state of the constant

`extensions/vscode/src/constants.ts:18-28`:

```ts
export const ENTRYPOINT_FILE_EXTENSIONS = [
  ".htm",
  ".html",
  ".ipynb",
  ".py",
  ".qmd",
  ".r",
  ".rmd",
  ".yml",
  ".yaml",
];
```

Node.js extensions are absent.

### The two code paths

**Editor-bar button** (`extensions/vscode/package.json:273-279`):

```jsonc
"editor/title": [
  {
    "command": "posit.publisher.deployWithEntrypoint",
    "when": "posit.publish.activeFileEntrypoint == true && isWorkspaceTrusted"
  }
]
```

`posit.publish.activeFileEntrypoint` is set by `extensions/vscode/src/entrypointTracker.ts:40 isEntrypoint()`, which calls `inspectProject(...)` — the full detector chain. `NodejsAppDetector` matches `.js`/`.ts`, the context flips `true`, the button appears. ✅

**Quick picker** (`extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newDeployment.ts:286-289`):

```ts
const filteredOpenFileList = vscodeOpenFiles().filter((openFilePath) => {
  const parsedPath = path.parse(openFilePath);
  return ENTRYPOINT_FILE_EXTENSIONS.includes(parsedPath.ext.toLowerCase());
});
```

Static extension list — no detector chain. `.js`/`.ts` get filtered out before the user sees them. ❌

### Canonical set from the detector

`extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectors/nodejs.ts:8-15`:

```ts
const VALID_EXTENSIONS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  ".js",
  ".mjs",
  ".cjs",
  ".ts",
  ".mts",
  ".cts",
]);
```

These are the six entries to add to `ENTRYPOINT_FILE_EXTENSIONS`.

### Scope of the change

`ENTRYPOINT_FILE_EXTENSIONS` has exactly two references in the codebase:

- `extensions/vscode/src/constants.ts:18` (definition)
- `extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newDeployment.ts:288` (only consumer)

So the fix is a one-array-extension change with no other call sites to update.

</details>

title: test(mock-connect): add Node.js server_settings fixture
description:
## Context

#4000 added `getNodejsSettings()` to the `connect-api` client, but the corresponding mock-connect fixture, route, and fixture-map entry were deferred because the validator was still pinned to Swagger 2.0 — and `/v1/server_settings/nodejs` only exists in Connect's OpenAPI 3.0 spec.

Once the validator migration in #4161 lands, the Node.js fixture can be added and validated like the other server-settings fixtures.

## Goal

Add a `server-settings-nodejs.json` fixture to mock-connect, wire up the route, and register it in the fixture map so it's validated by `just validate-fixtures`.

## Approach

1. **Fixture** `test/mock-connect/fixtures/connect-responses/server-settings-nodejs.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "installations": [
       { "version": "22.11.0", "cluster_name": "", "image_name": "" }
     ],
     "enabled": true
   }
   ```

2. **Route** in `test/mock-connect/src/mock-connect-server.ts`:
   ```ts
   [
     "GET",
     /^\/__api__\/v1\/server_settings\/nodejs$/,
     200,
     loadFixture("server-settings-nodejs.json"),
   ],
   ```

3. **Fixture map** in `test/mock-connect/src/validation/fixture-map.ts`:
   ```ts
   {
     fixture: "server-settings-nodejs.json",
     path: "/v1/server_settings/nodejs",
     method: "get",
     status: 200,
     description: "GET /server_settings/nodejs — Node.js installations",
   },
   ```

## Testing considerations

- `just validate-fixtures` passes, including the new fixture validating against the OpenAPI 3.0 schema.
- Connect API contract tests covering `getNodejsSettings()` exercise the new route.

## Dependencies

Depends on #4161 (OpenAPI 3.0 validator migration) — the fixture references a path that only exists in `openapi.json`.

Deferred from #4000.

title: test(mock-connect): migrate fixture validator from Swagger 2.0 to OpenAPI 3.0
description:
## Context

`test/mock-connect/src/validation/swagger-helpers.ts` validates response fixtures against the Connect public spec. It currently fetches the **legacy** Swagger 2.0 document at `https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/swagger.json` and is hardwired to Swagger 2.0 internals:

- Reads `definitions` (Swagger 2.0) instead of `components.schemas` (OpenAPI 3.0).
- Resolves `$ref` against `#/definitions/...` instead of `#/components/schemas/...`.
- Reads `response.schema` directly instead of `response.content["application/json"].schema`.

The Connect docs site now publishes both `swagger.json` (Swagger 2.0, legacy) and `openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.0). The Swagger 2.0 file is no longer kept fully in sync with Connect source — for example, `/v1/server_settings/nodejs` exists in `openapi.json` but not in `swagger.json` as of 2026-05-12.

## Goal

Migrate `swagger-helpers.ts` to consume `https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.0) so fixture validation runs against the spec Connect actually maintains.

## Approach

Update `test/mock-connect/src/validation/swagger-helpers.ts`:

- `SWAGGER_URL` → `https://docs.posit.co/connect/api/openapi.json`
- Rename types (`SwaggerSpec` → `OpenAPISpec`, etc.) or keep the names but update structure.
- Replace `definitions: Record<string, JsonSchema>` with `components: { schemas: Record<string, JsonSchema> }`.
- Update `dereferenceSchema` to resolve `#/components/schemas/...`.
- Update `getResponseSchema` to read `response.content["application/json"].schema`.
- Keep the cache file (`.cache/swagger.json`) but bump cache key/path or clear on first run to avoid mixing specs.
- `x-nullable` transform may no longer be needed (OpenAPI 3.0 uses `nullable: true`); audit fixtures.

Consider renaming `swagger-helpers.ts` → `openapi-helpers.ts` and updating imports.

## Testing considerations

- `just validate-fixtures` passes for all existing fixtures after the migration.
- Connect API contract tests (`test/connect-api-contracts/`) still pass against the updated mock server.

## Out of scope

- New fixtures for endpoints absent from Swagger 2.0 (e.g., `/v1/server_settings/nodejs`) — tracked separately.
- Any changes to `@posit-dev/connect-api` client code.

title: Standardize detector construction in detectorRunner.ts
description:
## Context

`extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectorRunner.ts` mixes two construction styles for the detectors it instantiates:

```ts
return [
  new PlumberDetector(),
  new RMarkdownDetector(),
  new NotebookDetector(),
  new QuartoDetector(),
  new RShinyDetector(),
  new PyShinyDetector(),
  newFastAPIDetector(),       // factory fn
  newFlaskDetector(),         // factory fn
  newDashDetector(),          // factory fn
  newGradioDetector(),        // factory fn
  newPanelDetector(),         // factory fn
  newStreamlitDetector(),     // factory fn
  newBokehDetector(),         // factory fn
  new NodejsAppDetector(),
  new StaticHTMLDetector(),
];
```

The Python detectors use factory functions for a real reason — `PythonAppDetector` is a single class parameterized by `(contentType, imports[])`, and the factory functions in `pythonApp.ts` capture each framework's specific import list. Everything else is a plain class.

The asymmetry showed up in [PR #4129 review](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/4129#discussion_r3209828285) — flagged by @zackverham, agreed by @dotNomad as a follow-up cleanup.

## Proposed direction

Pick one of:

1. **Subclass + `new` everywhere.** Keep `PythonAppDetector` as a base class, replace each `newFooDetector()` factory with a `class FooDetector extends PythonAppDetector { … }` and instantiate uniformly. Slightly more code, fully consistent call site.
2. **Factory function everywhere.** Add `newPlumberDetector()`, `newNodejsAppDetector()`, etc., and have `detectorRunner.ts` call only factories. Smallest call site change, but creates trivial wrappers for stateless classes.
3. **Document and accept the split** — factories are reserved for parameterized detectors, `new` for stateless ones.

(1) is the most consistent. (3) is the cheapest. The team should pick a convention and apply it consistently across `extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectors/`.

## Acceptance

- `detectorRunner.ts` uses a single construction style, OR a brief note in `extensions/vscode/CLAUDE.md` documents when each is used.
- No behavior change.

## Scope

Small. Single file (`detectorRunner.ts`) plus possibly the per-detector files depending on direction chosen. No tests should need to change beyond import updates.

title: docs: add preview deployments for PRs
description:
## Summary

When a PR includes documentation changes, we should deploy a preview of the rendered docs so reviewers can see the changes without building locally.

## Approach

Use [rossjrw/pr-preview-action](https://github.com/rossjrw/pr-preview-action) to deploy per-PR previews to subdirectories on the `gh-pages` branch (e.g., `pr-preview/pr-123/`). The action also posts a comment on the PR with the preview URL.

## Manual steps required

After merging, update the GitHub Pages source in repo settings:

1. Go to **Settings → Pages**
2. Change source from "GitHub Actions" to **"Deploy from a branch"**
3. Select branch: `gh-pages`, folder: `/ (root)`
4. Save

This is needed because the preview action pushes directly to the `gh-pages` branch, and both the main deploy and PR previews need to use the same mechanism.

Evaluate removing package listing given Positron's built-in package analysis
description:
## Context

With Package Manager's package analysis now baked into Positron, the R/Python package listing in Publisher may be duplicating what Positron already provides. This is worth exploring to determine if we can simplify Publisher by removing this functionality.

## Considerations

- From a UX perspective, displaying the same package information in two places in Positron is confusing
- If we can remove package listing from Publisher, we wouldn't need to add it for Node either
- We'd likely still want a fallback available for VS Code users (non-Positron)
- Need to understand how much overlap there is between what Publisher's package listing provides vs. what's needed

## Outcome

Determine whether Publisher's package listing can be removed (or made optional/fallback-only) given Positron's native package analysis capabilities.

title: docs: add nodejs content type to configuration documentation and CHANGELOG
description:
The final piece of the #3964 Node.js epic: update user-facing docs and the CHANGELOG now that everything ships.

## `docs/configuration.md`

1. Under `#### type`, add `nodejs` to the bullet list, alphabetically between `jupyter-voila` and `python-bokeh`.

2. Add a new `## Node.js settings` section after `## Quarto settings`, parallel in style to `## Python settings` / `## R settings`, covering:

   - **There is no `[node]` TOML section.** `type = "nodejs"` is the only marker — Node.js content has no user-configurable Publisher-side settings. This was a deliberate decision in #3996; don't introduce one here.
   - Both `package.json` and `package-lock.json` must be present in the project and included in `files`. Connect installs with `npm ci`, so a missing lock file is a hard failure — run `npm install` to generate one.
   - If `engines.node` is set in `package.json`, Connect uses it to pick the runtime version; otherwise Connect uses its default.
   - **Server gating:** requires Connect with an Advanced or Evaluation license, and the admin must enable Node.js support. Publisher's preflight surfaces a Node.js-specific error when the server reports `nodejs.enabled = false`.
   - **Connect Cloud is not supported** — `type = "nodejs"` with `product_type = "connect_cloud"` is rejected at load time.

   Example snippet (note: no `[node]` line):

   ```toml
   type = "nodejs"
   entrypoint = "index.js"
   files = ["*.js", "package.json", "package-lock.json"]
   ```

## `CHANGELOG.md` (root)

Under `## [Unreleased]`, add an `### Added` subsection above the existing `### Fixed`:

> - Support for deploying Node.js applications (Express, Fastify, Hono, etc.) to Posit Connect. (#3964)

Reference the epic (#3964), not the implementation sub-issues. Edit only the root `CHANGELOG.md` — leave `extensions/vscode/CHANGELOG.md` alone.

title: Refactor quarto shiny detection to iterate over all formats dynamically
description:
## Problem

The Quarto content detector hardcodes specific output format names (`html`, `revealjs`, `dashboard`) in multiple places:

1. **Shiny detection** (`extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectors/quarto.ts:154-158`) — checks `htmlMetadata`, `revealjsMetadata`, and `dashboardMetadata` separately.
2. **Title extraction** (`extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectors/quartoInspectOutput.ts:194-205`) — checks each format's title in sequence.
3. **Type definition** (`extensions/vscode/src/inspect/detectors/quartoInspectOutput.ts:49-68`) — each format has its own named interface entry.

Every time Quarto adds a new output format that supports `server: shiny`, we need to update all of these locations. This was the root cause of #3991 (dashboard format was missing).

## Proposed improvement

Refactor the `formats` field in `QuartoInspectData` to use a generic index signature (e.g., `Record<string, QuartoFormatEntry>`) instead of listing each format name explicitly. Then:

- **Shiny detection** can iterate over all format entries and check for shiny metadata in any of them.
- **Title extraction** can iterate over all format entries to find the first valid title.
- New Quarto output formats would be automatically supported without code changes.

### Considerations

- Some output formats are not supported for rendering on Connect (e.g., Word docs). The refactored code may need a filter or allowlist for formats that are valid Connect deployment targets, or it may be acceptable to detect shiny/extract titles from any format and let Connect handle unsupported formats at deploy time.
- The priority order for title extraction (currently html → revealjs → dashboard → website → project) may need to be preserved or reconsidered.

## Context

This came up during review of #4099, which added `dashboard` to the hardcoded list as a targeted fix for #3991.

title: Automate patch releases of older release lines
description:
## Background

Today's release tooling (`scripts/prepare-release.py`, `.github/workflows/prepare-release.yaml`, `tag-on-release-merge.yaml`, `nightly-prerelease.yaml`) is built around two flows:

1. **Production releases** — operator dispatches `prepare-release.yaml` with an even-minor version; the workflow branches off `main`, runs the script, opens a PR; merge triggers tag + release/publish.
2. **Nightly pre-releases** — daily cron picks the highest semver tag, computes the next odd-minor pre-release, commits the version bump to `main`, tags it.

Patch releases of an older release line (e.g. `2.0.1` while `2.1.x` pre-releases are in flight) don't fit either flow. As surfaced during prep for #4090:

- The release branch ends up cut from `main`, which contains everything since the last release — not just the targeted fix. We got lucky with `2.0.1` (only docs + nightly bumps + the fix), but the system doesn't enforce the "only the fix" guarantee.
- `prepare-release.py` would silently set `package.json` from `2.1.1` down to `2.0.1`. PR #4093 adds a `--allow-downgrade` guard, but that only catches the symptom.
- A maintainer doing a patch today has to manually: cut a branch from the prior tag, cherry-pick the fix, run `prepare-release.py` locally, push, merge, etc.

## Proposal

A new manually dispatched workflow, `prepare-patch-release.yaml`, that automates the mechanical parts:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:        # e.g. "2.0.1" — must be even minor
      base_tag:       # optional; defaults to highest v{major}.{minor}.* tag
      pr_numbers:     # comma-separated, e.g. "4082,4087"
```

Steps it would take:

1. **Validate** — version format + even minor; `base_tag` exists; `release/v$VERSION` branch and `v$VERSION` tag don't already exist.
2. **Derive `base_tag` if omitted** — from `2.0.1`, look up the highest tag matching `v2.0.*`. Saves an input and prevents off-by-one mistakes.
3. **Branch** — `git checkout -b release/v$VERSION $base_tag`.
4. **Cherry-pick each PR** — for each PR number, resolve to its squash-merge SHA on `main` (`gh pr view N --json mergeCommit -q .mergeCommit.oid`) and `git cherry-pick` it. PR numbers are friendlier than raw SHAs and let the workflow render a nice "Backports: #4082, #4087" line in the release PR body.
5. **Run `prepare-release.py $VERSION --allow-downgrade`** — same script, same CHANGELOG/`package.json` rewrite. The `--allow-downgrade` flag (added in #4093) is required because the patch version is necessarily lower than current `main`'s `package.json`.
6. **Push branch + open PR** — same as today; PR body lists the backported PRs and the base tag.

Steps 1, 5, and 6 are nearly identical to the existing `prepare-release.yaml`; only steps 2–4 are new. A lot of the workflow body can be lifted directly.

Once the PR merges to `main`, the existing `tag-on-release-merge.yaml` already handles the rest: it extracts `v$VERSION` from the branch name and tags the merge commit, which triggers `release.yaml` and `publish.yaml`. `verify-tag-ancestry` is satisfied because the tag's commit is reachable from `main`. No further changes needed downstream.

## Design decision: cherry-pick conflicts

CHANGELOG cherry-picks will conflict frequently — the fix's CHANGELOG line was originally added next to entries that don't exist on the older base. Three options:

- **Auto-resolve with `git cherry-pick -X theirs` on `CHANGELOG.md`.** Brittle; can silently drop context.
- **Bail and let the operator finish locally.** On conflict, push the half-resolved branch and open a *draft* PR with a comment containing the failing SHA and `git status` output. Operator does `git fetch && git checkout release/v$VERSION`, runs `git cherry-pick --continue` after fixing, pushes, marks PR ready.
- **Skip the script's CHANGELOG edits when cherry-picking.** Add a `--from-cherry-pick` flag to `prepare-release.py` so it leaves the CHANGELOG body alone (since the cherry-picked commits already brought their entries) and only inserts the `## [X.Y.Z]` header. Removes the most common conflict source.

Recommended combination: **#3 + #2.** Trust cherry-picked CHANGELOG entries (skip the script's CHANGELOG body work), and bail-to-draft on any other conflict. Handles ~90% of cases automatically and the rest with a clear path.

## Out of scope

- A label-driven backport bot (e.g. `korthout/backport-action`) that opens backport PRs onto long-lived `release/vX.Y` maintenance branches when a PR is labeled `backport/...`. That's worth doing only if patch releases become frequent (multiple per release line per year). For now, manual dispatch is fine.
- Loosening `verify-tag-ancestry` to accept tags reachable from non-`main` branches. Not needed for the dispatch-time approach above, since the patch release PR still merges to `main`.

## Effort

Estimate: ~half a day to write `prepare-patch-release.yaml` and the `--from-cherry-pick` flag in the script, plus a CONTRIBUTING.md section documenting when to use which workflow. Hardest part is testing without polluting the tag namespace — recommend running it against a throwaway fork or a dummy `v0.0.x` baseline first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `prepare-patch-release.yaml` workflow with `version`, `base_tag` (optional), `pr_numbers` inputs.

title: Publishing to Connect Cloud deletes secrets by sending `secrets: []` on PATCH
description:
## Bug Description

When publishing a new version of content to Posit Connect Cloud, all secrets on the content are deleted. This happens because the PATCH request payload always includes a `secrets` field, even when secrets haven't changed.

## Root Cause

In [`extensions/vscode/src/publish/cloudContentRequest.ts` at line 407](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/d8215f91774ab8a00bab9b214b2894afa50986d5/extensions/vscode/src/publish/cloudContentRequest.ts#L407), a value for `secrets` is always included in the request payload. If the user made no changes to secrets, it sends `secrets: []`, which tells Connect Cloud to remove all secrets from the content.

Connect Cloud update endpoints are all PATCH — if a value is not changing, it should **not** be included in the payload. Sending `secrets: []` is interpreted as "there should be no secrets on this content."

## Expected Behavior

If secrets have not been modified by the user, the `secrets` field should be omitted from the PATCH payload entirely, so existing secrets are preserved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Deploy content to Connect Cloud with secrets configured
2. Publish a new version of the content via Posit Publisher without modifying secrets
3. Observe that all secrets are deleted from the content on Connect Cloud

title: Skip Claude review on release PRs opened by bots
description:
## Problem

Claude currently attempts to review release PRs, but these PRs are opened by a bot account. This causes the review to fail because the "was this opened by a collaborator" check rejects bot-authored PRs.

## Expected behavior

Claude should not attempt to review release PRs. The workflow should detect that the PR was opened by a bot (or is a release PR) and skip the review step.

## Suggested fix

Add a condition to the Claude review workflow to skip PRs that are:
- Opened by bot accounts (e.g., check the `actor` type), or
- Tagged as release PRs, or
- Match the release PR title/branch pattern

title: Auto-label externally-opened issues with `community` label
description:
## Summary

Update `external-issue-notify.yaml` to automatically apply a `community` label to issues opened by non-Posit users. This builds on the existing external issue notification workflow so we can:

- Easily filter and triage community-reported issues
- Track open/unresolved external issues via a Project board
- Ensure timely follow-ups and close the loop when fixes land

## Proposed change

In `.github/workflows/external-issue-notify.yaml`, after detecting that an issue was opened by an external user, add a step to apply the `community` label:

```yaml
- name: Add community label
  if: steps.check-org.outputs.is-member == 'false'
  uses: actions/github-script@v7
  with:
    script: |
      await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
        owner: context.repo.owner,
        repo: context.repo.repo,
        issue_number: context.issue.number,
        labels: ['community']
      });
```

## Prerequisites

- Create the `community` label in the repo if it doesn't already exist

title: Reduce brittleness of quarto command assertions in smoke tests
description:
## Context

In #4048, @jonkeane [noted](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/4048#discussion_r3120054684) that the "command construction smoke test" suite in `quartoProjectHelper.smoke.test.ts` duplicates assertions already covered by the unit tests in `quartoProjectHelper.test.ts`. @zackverham agreed the command-capture approach is brittle, though the tests do serve a purpose: verifying that `QuartoProjectHelper` successfully invokes the mocked terminal with a render command when given real filesystem inputs.

## Current state

**Unit tests** (`quartoProjectHelper.test.ts`):
- Mock both `runTerminalCommand` and `fileExistsAt`
- Assert the exact command string passed to `runTerminalCommand` (e.g., `quarto render "."`)
- Cover project vs. document rendering, multi-level workspaces, and error cases

**Smoke tests** (`quartoProjectHelper.smoke.test.ts`, "command construction" suite):
- Use the real filesystem (create temp dirs with `_quarto.yml`) but mock `runTerminalCommand`
- Capture the command string and assert the exact same `quarto render "..."` pattern
- Overlap significantly with unit tests — the assertions are nearly identical

## Problem

The smoke test command assertions are brittle because they test the exact command string, which is an implementation detail. If we change how the command is constructed (e.g., add flags, change quoting), both the unit tests *and* the smoke tests break, creating unnecessary maintenance burden.

The smoke tests' real value is in verifying the filesystem-to-render-mode integration: given a real directory with/without `_quarto.yml`, does `render()` invoke the terminal at all and pick the right rendering mode (project vs. document)?

## Suggested improvements

1. **Relax exact command matching in smoke tests** — Instead of asserting the full command string, assert that:
   - `runTerminalCommand` was called (i.e., a render was attempted)
   - The command starts with `quarto render`
   - For project mode: the command contains the project directory path (not a specific `.qmd` file)
   - For document mode: the command contains the source file path

   Example:
   ```typescript
   expect(capturedCommand).toBeDefined();
   expect(capturedCommand).toMatch(/^quarto render /);
   expect(capturedCommand).toContain(tmpDir); // project mode
   ```

2. **Keep exact command assertions only in unit tests** — `quartoProjectHelper.test.ts` already covers the precise command construction with controlled mocks; that's the right place for those assertions.

3. **Consider whether the command construction smoke tests are needed at all** — The "real Quarto render" tests (which actually execute `quarto render`) already validate end-to-end behavior. The command construction smoke tests occupy a middle ground that may not add enough value over the unit tests + real render tests.

## Related

- PR #4048 (the change that surfaced this discussion)
- #4021 (original issue about `--to html` breaking revealjs)

title: Warn when Quarto project uses non-web-servable output formats (pdf, docx, etc.)
description:
## Context

In #4021 we removed the `--to html` flag from the "Render Your Project" command, which was silently overriding per-file format declarations (breaking `format: revealjs`, etc.). This was fixed in #4048.

With that fix, `quarto render` now respects all declared formats — including non-web-servable ones like `format: pdf` or `format: docx`. These formats aren't valid for Posit Connect deployment, and the current pipeline will fail or produce broken content downstream when it can't find the expected `.html` output.

## Proposal

Add a warning in the inspection layer (`QuartoDetector` / `QuartoInspectOutput`) when unsupported output formats are detected. The `formats` field from `quarto inspect` output already surfaces this information.

Possible approaches:
- Warn at inspection time if the only declared format is non-HTML (pdf, docx, etc.)
- Warn at render time if `quarto inspect` reveals formats that won't produce web-deployable output
- Surface the warning in the UI so the user understands why their content may not deploy correctly

## Current state

- `QuartoInspectOutput.formats` only types `html` and `revealjs` — other format keys are silently ignored
- The static alternative builder (`buildStaticAlternative`) assumes HTML output throughout
- There is no validation or user-facing warning for unsupported formats

## Related

- #4021 — original bug report (revealjs rendered as HTML)
- #4048 — fix removing `--to html`

title: Separate raw TOML config from computed interpreter defaults in PublisherState
description:
## Summary

`PublisherState.configurations` stores config objects that blend two concerns: the raw TOML configuration read from disk and computed interpreter defaults (e.g. `r.version`, `python.version`) that are resolved asynchronously by spawning R/Python subprocesses. This creates a race window where cached configs may lack interpreter fields if consumed between the file watcher's disk read and the async `UpdateConfigWithDefaults` hydration.

## Background

PR #4027 fixes the immediate symptom — deploying R Shiny apps intermittently fails with "Invalid manifest.json" because `r.version` is empty in the manifest. The fix re-applies `UpdateConfigWithDefaults` at deploy time, which is safe (synchronous, idempotent, in-memory only) but is a point fix rather than a structural solution.

This race was introduced during the Go-to-TypeScript migration. The Go backend loaded configs independently from disk on each API call, so the cached JS config object's lifecycle never mattered. Now that TS orchestrators consume the cached config directly for manifest building, the hydration gap is observable.

## Current state

- `refreshConfigurations()` loads all configs from disk, then hydrates each with `UpdateConfigWithDefaults` (async — spawns subprocesses)
- `findValidConfig()` returns whatever is in the cache, which may be un-hydrated
- `getSelectedConfiguration()` hydrates on cache miss but returns un-hydrated configs on cache hit
- `initiateDeployment()` (after #4027) re-applies defaults as a safety net before publishing

## Proposed approach

Separate raw TOML config from computed interpreter defaults:

1. **Store raw configs only** — `PublisherState.configurations` holds configs exactly as read from TOML, with no interpreter version fields filled in
2. **Resolve defaults at point of use** — callers that need interpreter fields (publish, manifest building) call an async method like `getHydratedConfig(name, projectDir)` that applies `UpdateConfigWithDefaults` on demand
3. **Cache computed defaults separately** (optional optimization) — maintain a parallel cache of resolved defaults, invalidated when the raw config or detected interpreters change

### Benefits

- Eliminates the race structurally — no caller can accidentally get a half-hydrated config
- Makes the contract explicit — raw config vs. computed config are different types
- Simplifies `refreshConfigurations()` — no need for the async hydration loop during refresh
- Tree views and other read-only consumers that don't need interpreter fields get simpler, faster access

### Considerations

- Callers that currently use `findValidConfig()` and don't need interpreter fields (tree views, UI display) would continue working unchanged with the raw config
- Only the publish path and manifest building actually need hydrated configs
- `getInterpreterDefaults()` is async (subprocess spawning) so the hydration point must be in an async context, which `initiateDeployment()` already is

## Related

- #4027 — immediate fix for the deploy-time race condition

Audit what E2E actually needs from the local build and rewrite.

title: Drop platform-specific VSIX packaging (vsce --target)
description:
Sub-issue of #3713.

Now that the Go binary is gone (#3818 et al.) and the extension is pure JavaScript/TypeScript, there's no reason to publish a separate VSIX per platform. We should drop `vsce --target` and ship a single universal `.vsix` that works on every platform VS Code runs on.

## Why it existed

The extension previously bundled `bin/publisher` — a Go binary built per platform (`darwin-amd64`, `darwin-arm64`, `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, `win32-x64`, `win32-arm64`). `vsce --target` was required so each VSIX would contain only the matching binary.

## Why it's no longer needed

Per the [VS Code extension docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension#platform-specific-extensions):

> Platform-specific extensions are useful if your extension has platform-specific libraries or dependencies, so you can control the exact binaries that are included in a platform package. A common use case is the use of **native node modules**.

All of our runtime dependencies are now pure JavaScript:

- `@posit-dev/connect-api`, `@posit-dev/connect-cloud-api`
- `@vscode/codicons`
- `ajv`, `ajv-formats`
- `async-mutex`, `axios`, `debounce`, `filenamify`, `js-yaml`, `jsonwebtoken`, `picomatch`, `retry`, `smol-toml`, `tar-stream`, `vscode-uri`

No `.node` bindings are included in the built VSIX. The only native modules in `node_modules` (`rollup`, `fsevents`, `ttf2woff2`) are dev-only and never bundled by esbuild into `dist/extension.js`.

## Cleanup

### `extensions/vscode/Justfile`
- Delete `_os`, `_arch`, `package-target-platform` helper recipes.
- Simplify `default`, `install`, `package`, `package-name` to take no `os`/`arch` arguments.
- `package-name` becomes `$name-$version.vsix` (drop the `-{os}-{arch}` suffix).
- `package` recipe: drop the `-t "$target_platform"` arg from the `vsce package` invocation.

### `.github/workflows/package.yaml`
- Collapse the 6-cell `(darwin|linux|windows) × (amd64|arm64)` matrix into a single job.
- Delete the `merge-artifacts` job — a single `dist/` upload is all downstream consumers need.

### `.github/workflows/publish.yaml`
- Simplify to publish one VSIX instead of iterating over platform-specific files.

### `.github/workflows/release.yaml`
- Attach a single `.vsix` to the release artifacts instead of six.

### Verification
- VSIX installs and activates on darwin-arm64 (local smoke test).
- CI package job produces one VSIX.
- `vsce publish` from a dry-run or pre-release flow succeeds with a single file.

This feels like overkill for a normal, non-error situation. It would be nice to suppress this, or maybe the answer is to not try to scan .py files as Quarto inputs?

title: Fail early when renv.lock is missing packages needed by project
description:
## Problem

When using `packages_from_library = true`, if a package is removed from `renv.lock` (but is still used by the project code), the deployment succeeds but the content fails to execute on Connect because the missing package isn't included in the manifest.

This happens because both the Go and TypeScript library mappers iterate over `lockfile.Packages` to build the manifest — if a package isn't in the lockfile, it's silently omitted.

- **Go implementation:** [`internal/inspect/dependencies/renv/manifest_packages.go#L221-L292`](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/internal/inspect/dependencies/renv/manifest_packages.go#L221-L292)
- **TypeScript implementation:** `extensions/vscode/src/publish/rLibraryMapper.ts` (`libraryToManifestPackages`)

## Expected behavior

Publisher should detect that the lockfile is missing packages the project depends on and fail early with a clear error message, rather than allowing a deployment that will fail at runtime.

## Notes

- This applies to both the `packages_from_library` (library mapper) and standard lockfile paths, since both use `renv.lock` as the source of truth for which packages to include.
- `renv::status()` already detects this kind of drift — we could either shell out to R for validation or compare lockfile packages against a dependency scan.

Found during smoke testing of #3980.

title: Cloud SSO refresh is not implemented
description:
Posit Connect Cloud credentials have automatic refresh logic for the OAuth token. However, for SSO-enabled accounts, refreshing the token is not enough. We need to detect SSO claim expiration and direct the user to their browser to log in again.

```
{"error":"Unauthenticated.","error_type":"sso_required","error_args":{"idp":"lucid-auth:idps:01961b78-bf9a-fd78-b8df-082da083ddce","logged_in":true}}
```

title: Cloud publish should auto-detect Python version when not in TOML config
description:
## Problem

When deploying Python content to Connect Cloud, the deploy can fail if `python.version` is not set in the config file, which it is not by default.

```toml
[python]
```

This causes a validation failure:

```
422: {"error":"Field `body.revision_overrides.python_version` error: Input should be '3.9', '3.10', '3.11', '3.12' or '3.13'","error_type":"request_validation","error_args":null}
```

Which can be resolved by manually entering a python version:

```toml
[python]
version = '3.13'
```

When deploying to Connect, it just works without the manual intervention. It would be nice if the Cloud flow was as seamless.

The bundle we send to Connect has a python version in the manifest.json even though it was not in the config. I don't know if this is the case for the bundle we send to Cloud (might need to add some debugging code to save the bundle aside for inspection, as I don't see a way to download the bundle from Cloud.) Judging from the error message, we probably need to set a reasonable default on the content request body revision.

title: cloud: send domain_id alongside vanity_name
description:
It's possible to set a `vanity_name` in your deployment config: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/2bf9c9b63f0fb28eea6cb9cf3c5a42c939a7c705/docs/configuration.md#connect-cloud-specific-settings

However, this no longer works as a `domain_id` is now required when you send a `vanity_name`:

```
{"error":"Field `body` error: Value error, If 'vanity_name' is set then 'domain_id' must also be set.","error_type":"request_validation","error_args":null}
```

From the Cloud team:

> If there is no custom domain then `domain_id` should be passed as `null`.

At a minimum we should include `domain_id: null` when `vanity_name` is set. For full support we should add `domain_id` to the schema as a valid field (a UUID string) and allow setting it in configs.

title: feat: Node Packages view in sidebar
description:
> [!WARNING]

## Context
