title: feat: support Snowflake session auth (browser-based) for publishing to SPCS
description:
Publishing from desktop Positron/RStudio to Connect running in Snowflake SPCS currently requires keypair auth — the user must generate a public/private key pair, register the public key with Snowflake, and configure the private key path locally. This has high friction and security concerns (private key material on disk).

Snowflake's SPCS ingress supports a **session auth** flow ([Option 3 in the docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/developer-guide/snowpark-container-services/tutorials/advanced/tutorial-8-access-public-endpoint-programmatically)) that supports all Snowflake auth types — including **browser-based auth**, which is the ideal desktop UX:

1. Publisher opens a browser tab to Snowflake's auth endpoint
2. User authenticates in the browser (SSO, MFA, etc.)
3. Snowflake calls back to a localhost server with a session token
4. Publisher uses that token for SPCS ingress requests (~1 hour lifetime, refreshable)

This dramatically reduces friction: no key management, no config files for the common desktop case. CI/headless environments can still use PAT or keypair auth through the same mechanism.

### How it works

The session auth flow produces a Snowflake token that authenticates requests through the SPCS ingress proxy. Connect still requires its own auth, so this builds on the dual-header pattern from #3465:

| Header | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | Snowflake session token | Authenticates to the Snowflake ingress proxy |
| `X-RSC-Authorization` | Connect API key or token | Authenticates to Connect behind the proxy |

### What needs to happen

1. **Implement Snowflake session auth flow in TypeScript.** The flow involves:
   - Reading Snowflake connection config from `~/.snowflake/connections.toml` (Python connector format — Posit Team standard)
   - For browser auth: spinning up a localhost HTTP server, opening the Snowflake auth URL in the browser, capturing the callback token
   - For PAT/keypair: constructing the appropriate JWT
   - Exchanging the auth for a session token usable on SPCS ingress
2. **Token lifecycle management.** Session tokens last ~1 hour. Implement refresh so long publish operations or repeated publishes don't fail mid-session.
3. **Credential UX.** When the user targets a `*.snowflakecomputing.app` URL, offer auth method choices appropriate to the environment:
   - Desktop: browser-based (recommended), keypair, PAT
   - CI/headless: keypair, PAT
4. **Wire into dual-header requests** (building on #3465's `Authorization` + `X-RSC-Authorization` pattern).

### Reference implementations

- **[posit-dev/snowflakeauth](https://github.com/posit-dev/snowflakeauth/blob/main/R/externalbrowser.R)** — R implementation of Snowflake session auth with browser-based flow. Clean, no heavy dependencies. Per the Snowflake team, this is the best reference for porting to TypeScript.
- **[Snowflake Go database driver](https://github.com/rstudio/partnership-snowflake/blob/main/native-apps/go/snowflake/auth/session/session.go)** — Go implementation of Snowflake session auth, but heavier dependency. The `snowflake-auth` repo is preferred as a reference.
- **[Snowflake JS driver](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-nodejs)** — exists but hasn't been evaluated. Worth checking whether it could simplify the implementation or is too heavy.

### Testing

- Dogfood SPCS instance: see https://connect.posit.it/snowflake/demo.html for the current address. Stick with this dev environment (updated within a day if needed).
- Test from desktop Positron publishing to the dogfood Connect instance.
- Verify browser auth flow, token refresh, and fallback to PAT/keypair.

### Dependencies

- #3465 (dual-header auth foundation) should land first or concurrently.

### Relationship to other issues

- Builds on #3465 (dual-header auth with API key)
- Related to #3226 (Token Auth UX in SPCS)
- Supersedes the original Snowflake support from #2632

title: feat: fix dual auth for Snowflake SPCS (Connect API key + Snowflake token, and Connect token + Snowflake token)
description:
## Background

When publishing to Connect running in Snowflake SPCS, requests route through the Snowflake ingress proxy at `*.snowflakecomputing.app`. The proxy requires a Snowflake auth header. Connect itself also requires auth — and since Connect no longer trusts Snowflake headers for user identity (switched to OIDC), every request needs **two** auth headers.

## Current state (broken)

The `SnowflakeAuth` variant in `ConnectAPIOptions` (`packages/connect-api/src/types.ts`) sends only:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Snowflake Token="<snowflake-token>"` |

No Connect credential is attached. Requests pass the ingress proxy but fail at Connect with 401. The credential creation wizard (`newConnectCredential.ts`) only collects a Snowflake connection name for Snowflake URLs — no Connect auth is gathered. `CredentialsService.create()` actively rejects Snowflake credentials that have an API key or token, making it impossible to store dual-auth credentials.

## Scope

Two dual-auth combinations need to work:

### 1. Snowflake token + Connect API key

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Snowflake Token="<snowflake-token>"` |
| `X-RSC-Authorization` | `Key <connect-api-key>` |

### 2. Snowflake token + Connect token (RSA keypair signing)

The token auth signing headers from `signRequest()` (`packages/connect-api/src/auth.ts`) do **not** use `Authorization` — they use `X-Auth-Token`, `X-Auth-Signature`, `X-Content-Checksum`, and `Date`. These can coexist with the Snowflake `Authorization` header, so:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Snowflake Token="<snowflake-token>"` |
| `X-Auth-Token` | `<connect-token-id>` |
| `X-Auth-Signature` | `<per-request RSA-SHA1 signature>` |
| `X-Content-Checksum` | `<MD5 of request body>` |
| `Date` | `<request date>` |

## What needs to change

### 1. `packages/connect-api/src/types.ts`

Replace the current `SnowflakeAuth` interface (which has no Connect auth) with two new discriminated union variants:

```typescript
interface SnowflakeApiKeyAuth extends ConnectAPIBaseOptions {
  snowflakeToken: string;
  apiKey: string;          // Connect API key → X-RSC-Authorization: Key <apiKey>
  token?: never;
  privateKey?: never;
}

interface SnowflakeTokenAuth extends ConnectAPIBaseOptions {
  snowflakeToken: string;
  token: string;           // Connect token ID → X-Auth-Token
  privateKey: string;      // RSA private key → per-request signature
  apiKey?: never;
}
```

Update `ConnectAPIOptions` to include these instead of the current `SnowflakeAuth`.

### 2. `packages/connect-api/src/client.ts`

Update the constructor to handle both new variants:
- `SnowflakeApiKeyAuth`: set both `Authorization: Snowflake Token="..."` and `X-RSC-Authorization: Key <apiKey>` as static headers.
- `SnowflakeTokenAuth`: set `Authorization: Snowflake Token="..."` as a static header, and attach the same request-signing interceptor used today for `TokenAuth` (which calls `signRequest()` to add `X-Auth-Token`, `X-Auth-Signature`, etc. per request).

### 3. `extensions/vscode/src/credentials/service.ts`

Two functions need updating:

**`CredentialsService.create()`** — Loosen the `ServerType.SNOWFLAKE` validation. Currently it rejects any credential with `apiKey` or `token+privateKey`. Instead, require that **exactly one** Connect auth method is present alongside `snowflakeConnection`:
```
snowflakePresent && (connectPresent XOR tokenAuthPresent) && !connectCloudPresent
```

**`buildSnowflakeOptions()`** — After generating `snowflakeToken`, check whether the credential has `apiKey` or `token+privateKey`, and return the appropriate `SnowflakeApiKeyAuth` or `SnowflakeTokenAuth` options. The function currently reads from `Pick<Credential, "url" | "snowflakeConnection">` — widen that to also accept `apiKey`, `token`, and `privateKey`.

### 4. `extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newConnectCredential.ts`

The Snowflake flow currently branches from URL entry straight to Snowflake connection selection, then to credential naming — skipping Connect auth entirely. After the user picks a Snowflake connection, add a step to select the Connect auth method (API key or Token), then collect the relevant credential (reuse the existing `inputAPIKey` and `inputToken` steps). Update `isValidSnowflakeAuth()` to also require either an API key or token+privateKey.

## Files not expected to need changes

- `extensions/vscode/src/api/types/credentials.ts` — `Credential` already has `snowflakeConnection`, `apiKey`, `token`, and `privateKey` fields.
- `extensions/vscode/src/credentials/storage.ts` — No schema changes needed.
- `packages/connect-api/src/auth.ts` — `signRequest()` is already correct.

## Prior work

- PR #3268: Go implementation of Snowflake + API key dual-header auth, validated against the dogfood instance. Use for reference.
- `rsconnect-python` PR posit-dev/rsconnect-python#715: same dual-header pattern.
- `rstudio/snowflake-auth`: Snowflake auth Go code, clean implementation with no heavy dependencies.

## Testing

- Dogfood SPCS instance: see https://connect.posit.it/snowflake/demo.html for the current address.
- Test from desktop Positron publishing to the dogfood Connect instance.
- Verify both API key and token auth methods work end-to-end.

## Relationship to other issues

- Prerequisite for #3466 (session/browser auth builds on top of this dual-header foundation)
- Related to #3226 (Token Auth recommendation doesn't work in SPCS — this issue provides the correct alternative)
- Supersedes the Snowflake support added in #2632 (which relied on header-trust that no longer exists)

title: Integration Requests 'Add' action hidden due to server settings fetch failure
description:
## Description

The "Add Integration Request" action in the Integration Requests section is not displayed because the server settings fetch fails for certain content types.

## Root Cause

Commit c7584d857 from PR #3267 changed `AppModeFromType` to return `AppMode(t)` (the raw content type string) instead of `UnknownMode` for unknown content types.

In `capabilities.go`, this causes the scheduler settings API path to include the raw content type string:

```go
appMode := clienttypes.AppModeFromType(cfg.Type)
if !appMode.IsStaticContent() {
    schedulerPath = "/" + string(appMode)
}
err = c.client.Get("/__api__/server_settings/scheduler"+schedulerPath, &settings.scheduler, log)
```

**Before the change:**
- Unknown content types → `UnknownMode` (empty string)
- API call: `/__api__/server_settings/scheduler/` ✓

**After the change:**
- Unknown content types → raw content type string (e.g., `"unknown-type"`)
- API call: `/__api__/server_settings/scheduler/unknown-type` ✗ (fails)

This causes `GetSettings` to fail, which causes `refreshConnectServerSettings` in `homeView.ts` to fail silently, leaving `serverSettings` undefined in the webview store. The `IntegrationRequests.vue` component checks `isOAuthIntegrationsSupported` which requires `serverSettings` to be defined, hiding the "Add Integration Request" action.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Selecta deployment in the Publisher extension
2. Observe that the "Add Integration Request" action is missing
3. Check console for `Failed to fetch server-settings for...` error

## Affected Versions

Introduced in v1.25.0 (commit c7584d857)
Last working version: v1.24.0

title: follow same R repository configuration as positron in auto mode
description:
This is what positron does:
- check for repos.conf in XDG config paths (~/.config/rstudio/, ~/.config/positron/, /etc/)
- use custom PPM URL if packageManagerRepository setting is configured
- default to PPM in web mode (Workbench)
- therwise let Ark handle it (Ark then respects .Rprofile and options(repos))

~Since positron has already done the above I think publisher should be able to just look up what's configured and use that.~ with the way publisher runs R for this, I'm not sure that's the case, I think we do need to replicate the logic.

title: use local R packages if available for renv snapshot
description: When snapshotting dependencies, publisher currently does not assume any dependencies are installed on the local machine and creates a fresh, isolated environment where it installs all the packages before deploying. This is helpful in environments where not all packages are installed, but makes deploys unnecessarily slow from user machines where all the dependencies _are_ installed. We should update this so that we try to use existing packages (as rsconnect does) if present, but fall back to installing everything if not.

What if I could highlight the `app` variable there and then run/click "create an ASGI API based on this function" and then publisher _just did the rest_. title: Investigate R package repository defaults and pre-deployment package installation behavior
description:
publisher's ephemeral renv setup has some behaviors worth investigating and potentially improving:

1. Default repository selection: publisher defaults to `cloud.r-project.org` (CRAN) for R package installation during dependency scanning
2. Pre-deployment package installation: publisher installs packages locally (even ones already installed on the system) before deploying

## Questions to investigate

- [x] understand why we default to cloud.r-project.org/whether defaulting to P3M is possible instead
  -  Comments suggest that the behavior is the way is it for compatibility with positron's defaults: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/1d4ffb23f518e094b1672c7330ef37a31cd4c790/internal/inspect/dependencies/renv/project_dependencies.go#L149-L150
  - However I think [positron's behavior](https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/blob/0c4b3dabbce385212ab9ea039079286a6b5bea04/extensions/positron-r/src/kernel-spec.ts#L413-L431) is a little different. Notably it defaults to `posit-ppm` when running in web mode (i.e. Workbench), which makes sense since on linux we most likely want PPM. For the same reason we may want publisher to default to PPM as well, because whatever we choose here will make it into the lockfile that gets sent to Connect, which is running on linux.
  - I think we can and should change this to default to package manager
  - [x] is it possible to actually look up what's configured for the user? look at what positron does/how it interacts with .Rprofile & `options(repos)`. ideally publisher behaves the same
    - this is what positron does:
      - check for repos.conf in XDG config paths (~/.config/rstudio/, ~/.config/positron/, /etc/)-
      - use custom PPM URL if `packageManagerRepository` setting is configured 
      - default to PPM in web mode (Workbench) 
      - otherwise let Ark handle it (Ark then respects `.Rprofile` and `options(repos)`)
    - since positron has already done the above I _think_ publisher should be able to just look up what's configured and use that.
- [x] why does publisher install packages before deploying? is this necessary? (compare to rsconnect, which does not do this)
  - the answer here is that rsconnect does a snapshot from the user's current library. this is fast & doesn't require installation of all the packages because they're already installed, _however_ it fails if any of the packages are not installed. publisher on the other hand creates an isolated renv project and installs packages into it, which works even if the user does not have the packages installed locally.

title: Credential creation fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')" for on-prem Connect server
description:
## Summary
When attempting to create a new deployment credential for an on-premises Posit Connect server in the Publisher pane, the credential creation fails immediately with an "Invalid URL" error before prompting for an API key.

## Error Message
```
Error: Invalid URL (unable to validate connectivity with server URL - Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status'))
```

A second error also appears:
```
Unable to query existing credentials. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'status')
```

## Environment
- Positron: 2026.01
- OS: Windows 11
- Connect server: On-premises, HTTP on port 80
- Connect authentication provider: single-user password
- Posit Publisher: Use Key Chain Credential Storage = Unchecked

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Positron
3. Open the Publisher pane
4. Click to add a new credential
5. Enter a valid Connect server URL (e.g., `http://my-connect-server.local`)
6. Error appears immediately — no prompt for API key
## Expected Behavior
Publisher should either:
- Prompt for an API key after entering the URL, or
- Open a browser for SSO authentication (as RStudio IDE does)

## Actual Behavior
The credential creation fails with a JavaScript null reference error before any authentication step.

## Additional Context
- The same Connect server works correctly with RStudio IDE (which opens a browser for SSO login)
- `curl -v http://my-connect-server/__ping__` returns HTTP 200
- The server is accessible in the browser and via VPN

## Workaround
Manually create `~/.connect-credentials` with the following format:
```toml
[credentials.my-server]
url = "http://my-connect-server.local"
api_key = "your-api-key-here"
```

This bypasses the broken credential creation UI and allows deployments to proceed.

title: Revisit `ForceProductTypeCompliance()` to minimize differences between schemas
description:
In `config/types.go`, the method `ForceProductTypeCompliance()` overrides a few deployment configuration fields so that the config complies with the schema spec for Connect or Cloud.

It was the case for issue #3356 that overriding `R.PackageFile` and setting it to an empty value had side-effects for the deployment workflow to Connect Cloud, an empty `PackageFile` was used erroneously as a signal to ignore the user's existing `renv.lock` file.

The less overrides to the deployment config would help to avoid surprising side-effects, for that, revisiting `ForceProductTypeCompliance()` with the mindset of avoiding overrides or having a more transparent flow of deployment configuration updates would help greatly.

title: Python version capability check defeats `requires-python` specification
description:
In our capabilities checking we check the python version (and critically not the `requires-python` version range if it is present) https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/34458b36a57e078043ead4ad07fa82f1ba25ecbc/internal/clients/connect/capabilities.go#L175-L188

This means that if there isn't a matching major/minor on the server for the interpreter you have you are unable to deploy to that server (even if you have a python requirement specification that works!). For example: if my server has python 3.11 and 3.12, my local interpreter is python 3.9 and the content I'm trying to deploy uses `pyproject.toml` to set `requires-python = ">= 3.8"` since the item is compatible with anything 3.8 and over. We fail at the capabilities step. 

I uncovered this while working on end to end tests. We weren't running into this because we matched the exact python version in the image with the item being deployed.

title: Poor experience trying to deploy a python module/following `uv` conventions
description:
It's not uncommon for Python modules to have a `__main__.py` that defines an entrypoint for invoking it. And that's a totally reasonable way to start an API--or more specifically what I was trying to do, an MCP server, because you can easily specify `uvx <module>` for how it is run. But this goes really badly for Publisher.

I recently forked an MCP server (https://github.com/nealrichardson/zendesk-mcp-server), and I wanted to deploy it to Connect so that I can securely give it access to the Zendesk API without passing around those credentials.  Since Connect can't run a node.js app, I asked Claude to port it to Python so it could be run with `uvx` instead of `npx`. Then I tried to deploy it. Here's all of the things I ran into, many familiar to us based on past issue reports, some not.

* Publisher could not find an entrypoint. The function in `__main__.py` starts the API server itself, but that's not how Connect needs it. So I had to refactor the Python code so that the Starlette app was available for Connect. Told Claude I needed to be able to `uvicorn.run(app)` where app is the starlette app. It did, and said you can run the app with `uvicorn zendesk_mcp.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`. (Not long ago, having to do this would have probably been a deal breaker, but with LLMs these days, this was the easy part.) Note that this entrypoint is not its own standalone file, and it is inside the `zendesk_mcp` package.
* Once that was done, when I clicked new deployment, Publisher discovered that I could use the server.py file as an entrypoint. But it was type = 'unknown'. (#2833)
* The help message suggested e.g. "python-shiny" so I tried "python-fastapi". That failed with an error about invalid type. Clicking the troubleshooting link, and then the link to the schema (https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/docs/configuration.md#type), I found that "python-fastapi" is indeed a valid type. The actual problem was that I needed to add `[python]` at the end of the file. I never would have guessed that if I hadn't flailed around here before. That was not in the troubleshooting docs. (#2666)
* After declaring Python, then it failed with "Missing dependency file requirements.txt. This file must be included in the deployment." Because uv/Claude had set me up with pyproject.toml. Ok fine. So I did `uv pip compile python/pyproject.toml -o python/requirements.txt` to generate requirements.txt from pyproject.toml. (#2824, #2205)
* But the file isn't available because it's in the parent directory, because Publisher put the config at the same level as the file with the entrypoint. But that's part of the python package. That also means that the app wouldn't have run on Connect anyway because all of the imports from the package would have failed. (#2832, #2868)
* So I moved the publish directory up a level. Now the toml file is out of sync, it references files that are no longer in the same directory. So I had to fix all those paths. (#3063)
* Then I had to know to set the entrypoint to `zendesk_mcp.server:app` instead of `server.py`. (#2178)
* Then deployment failed because `.python-version` specifed Python 3.13, but the Connect environment only has up to 3.11. The error message pointed me to edit the toml file, but IDK how I would specify the version, and which version specification wins if there are multiple. I tried excluding the file but that didn't work either. I edited `.python-version` to say `>=3.11` and that didn't work. (#971) I tried including `pyproject.toml` too, which also specifies Python version, and that didn't help either. I tried adding `version = '3.11'` under `[python]` in the toml file, and that said "invalid version"!  (#3028)

title: Deployment fails with renv.lock due to missing shiny package
description:
<!-- Please provide the following information to help us diagnose the issue, removing any sections that are not applicable. Thank you for your help! -->

## Problem statement

Publisher fails to deploy a Shiny application when a valid project-level `renv.lock` is present. During deployment, Publisher generates or uses a different `renv.lock` under `.posit/publish/deployments/`, which omits required packages (including `shiny`). This results in an incomplete R environment and a startup failure, despite `renv.lock` existing at the repository root and a manifest file being generated as documented.

## Steps to reproduce

Using publisher, I went through the process of deploying the app.

I also followed instructions [here](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/rsconnect.html) to generate a manifest file to use.

**Expected behavior:** App deployment.

Publisher should:
- Respect the project-level `renv.lock`, or
- Use the provided manifest consistently, and
- Install all required packages listed there, including `shiny`.

**Actual behavior:** Did not deploy.

- Publisher generates or uses a different `renv.lock` at `.posit/publish/deployments/renv.lock`.
- This generated lockfile does **not** match the project-level `renv.lock`.
- The resulting environment omits required packages.

## System Details

## Publishing information

```text

Code - OSS Version: 1.103.0

Date: 2025-08-29T18:31:52.943Z (3 mos ago)

title: feat(connect): include git repo metadata with bundle
description:
## Description

The upcoming 2025.12.0 Connect release will allow including extra metadata fields with bundle uploads, including fields for source control (previously only used by Connect's "git-backed publishing" feature). We should include that metadata from Publisher when publishing to Connect, if the Connect server version is sufficient (see https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/pull/736 for reference). 

Do we need to shell out to `git` or can we tap into a vscode/positron extension API to get it? Any other considerations?

title: An existing and outdated renv.lock file causing failed deployments
description:
Taking the following quarto doc as example:
```qmd
---
title: Quarto Document
format:
  html:
    echo: false
---

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a
finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.
```

Calling `renv::init()` on the project generates an almost empty `renv.lock`.

After changing things on the doc and adding a code block to it, e.g:
```
```{r}
print(mtcars) 
```
... the `renv.lock` now will be missing dependencies such as `knitr`. 

For users without much experience handling `renv` environments this can be frustrating since the project deploys but fails to render and Publisher does not provide feedback that the existing `renv.lock` looks to be out of sync or incomplete.

title: During deployment, allow standalone URL to work Content URL
description: When setting up a deployment for content already on Connect, the standalone URL throws an error if input as the Posit Connect Content URL. It would be nice if it expected the standalone URL (since that URL is listed under URL in Connect settings Panel) and could deal with that different URL. Potentially, could a publisher also use the GUID or other easy to grab identifiers. Including @jonkeane since he was part of this discussion and might have additional thoughts.

title: feat: support adding `package_repository_resolution` to manifests
Upgrade e2e to the latest Cypress
description:
e2e is currently using Cypress 14.x and should be upgraded to the latest.

Additionally, we should ensure Dependabot is maintaining future upgrades for us if it is not already.

We should investigate whether this upgrade fixes the issue we currently have with the Workbench e2e tests silently failing and restarting due to us overriding the baseUrl. This is documented in this PR https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2984  [Overriding the baseUrl is a documented config feature](https://docs.cypress.io/app/references/configuration#Test-specific-Configuration) so it should work without issue. If it continues to fail after upgrading Cypress we should reach out to Cypress support for assistance.

title: Improve e2e Workbench Positron test isolation
description:
The initial e2e Workbench Positron automation was merged via: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2984

The tests current reuse the same default rstudio user, and this requires some amount of manual cleanup and full container restart which has the following concerns:
- The manual cleanup is tightly tied to Workbench implementation which is planned to change at some point in the future
- The container restart is very slow

The Workbench team suggested using ssh to create new users for each test, and simply cleanup the users. This should provide easier test isolation and not require restarting the container.

title: feat: Publish scripts as Quarto documents
description:
## Description

Connect supports rendering scripts (`.py` and `.R`) files as Quarto documents, see https://docs.posit.co/connect/user/scripts/. There's some front-matter that needs to be added that makes Quarto recognize them as renderable, see https://quarto.org/docs/computations/render-scripts.html#syntax and the scripts are renders using Jupyter or Knitr. However, the Publisher extension does not know how to handle these types of files. For example, if I try to publish the following R script

```R
#' ---
#' title: "R script file"
#' ---

# Randomly generate data that acts as 30-day trailing unit sales.
today <- Sys.Date()
data <- data.frame(
  Date = today - 1:30,
  Sales = sample(75:100, 30, replace = TRUE)
)

# Write a CSV for downstream use.
write.csv(data, "sales.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#' Download [CSV](sales.csv)
```

Publisher generates the following configuration

```toml
# Configuration file generated by Posit Publisher.
# Please review and modify as needed. See the documentation for more options:
# https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/docs/configuration.md
product_type = 'connect'
'$schema' = 'https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json'
type = 'unknown'
entrypoint = 'rscript.R'
validate = true
files = [
  '/rscript.R',
  '/renv.lock',
  '/.posit/publish/render-rscript-reprex-545N.toml',
  '/.posit/publish/deployments/deployment-OVT9.toml'
]
title = 'render-rscript-reprex'
```

Where the `type` config should be `quarto-static`, and an `[r]` and `[quarto]` block are missing. 

### Note

It does appear that Publisher knows how to handle `.py` handles rendered with Jupyter.

```py
# %% [markdown]
# ---
# title: "Python script file"
# ---

# %%
import datetime
import pandas as pd
import random

# Randomly generate data that acts as 30-day trailing unit sales.
today = datetime.date.today()
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Date': pd.date_range(
        today - datetime.timedelta(days=30),
        today - datetime.timedelta(days=1),
    ),
    'Sales': [random.randint(75, 100) for _ in range(1, 31)],
})


# Write a CSV for downstream use.
data.to_csv("sales.csv", index=False)

# %% [markdown]
# Download [CSV](sales.csv)
```

Publisher generates the configuration


```toml
# Configuration file generated by Posit Publisher.
# Please review and modify as needed. See the documentation for more options:
# https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/docs/configuration.md
product_type = 'connect'
'$schema' = 'https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json'
type = 'quarto-static'
entrypoint = 'pyscript.py'
validate = true
files = [
  '/pyscript.py',
  '/requirements.txt',
  '/renv.lock',
  '/.posit/publish/Python script file-HT68.toml',
  '/.posit/publish/deployments/deployment-GDCC.toml'
]
title = 'Python script file'

[python]

[quarto]
version = '1.7.32'
engines = ['jupyter']
```

title: Upgrade to Vite 7

title: bug: Cancelling a re-deploy can change the deployment record
description: Cancelling at a certain point during a re-deployment can change the `id` of a deployment record causing the publisher to create a new a content item and start pointing at it instead of the original content item.

title: Investigate updated esbuild + TypeScript setup
description:
With the work to upgrade Vitest to version 4 in #3303 there was a workaround needed to handle sub-path imports. This makes me think there is a better way to handle our `tsconfig` setup alongside `esbuild`. Ideally our dependencies shouldn't cause TypeScript errors that become irrelevant with our `esbuild` bundler setup.

Some things that will be helpful:
- [investigate the latest VS Code extension template created with `yo`](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/get-started/your-first-extension)
- [investigate the latest `esbuild` and `webview` VS Code extension examples](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-extension-samples)

title: Upgrade `vitest` to 4
description:
We are currently on `vitest` `3.2.4` in both `extensions/vscode` and `extensions/vscode/webviews/homeView`. Vitest has a version 4 available.

There is [a migration document](https://vitest.dev/guide/migration.html).

title: bug: Publisher shows toasts on save in multi-folder workspaces in Workbench
description:
To Reproduce:
1. Create a VS Code / Positron session in Workbench
2. Create a multi-folder workspace by doing "File > Add Folder to Workspace..." on two folders
3. Save a file

Notice that a `entrypoint not found` (the only one that I saw, but @MariaSemple saw `project directory not found`) toast appears.

title: Add Panel app support
description:
With addition of Panel apps in Connect, we want to add the panel apps to deployments with Publisher. Currently, we see "the specified app mode is not valid".



### Related Issues 

- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2474

### Related PRs

- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2541
- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2418

title: add support for quarto-shiny on connect cloud
description:
Connect Cloud is adding support for Quarto Shiny content, but Publisher today will prevent content with that app mode from being deployed. We need to specifically add support for this content type.

Note that this functionality hasn't been released yet in production. I'll comment here once it goes live.

title: Stop populating certain fields for Connect Cloud
description: The fields `r_version` and `app_mode` aren't required to be sent on the content create/update request. We'd like to remove them from the request format for the API, so publisher should stop populating them.

title: Ability to infer or store recurring secrets
description:
## Feature Request

I oftentimes have the same environment variables I want to send up alongside my deployment. It is tedious to type them in every time, especially when you are passing 10-15 environment variables with each deployment. 

I would love if there was a feature that would **allow to either grab the existing system environment variables in the session** and give me the option to add them to my `SECRETS` tab in the deployment **_or_ a way to import credentials from a file** (e.g. allowing me to import secrets from my `.Renviron` or `.env` file).

title: chore: Remove older bats Nightly jobs and scripts
description:
There was bats tests running nightly, removal of these tests happened here:
- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/commit/4b93639ab459028d8e254510e00c7951f8f807bd
- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/commit/cf57d940515f88949165d05ff2dcd2285532207d

Some remnants left to spin up the infra for those tests still exists in CI and [have been failing for about a week](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/actions/runs/19126550433/job/54707736547) due to SSH key revocation in fuzzbucket.

We don't need to fix these. Now that we have Cypress e2e tests, running as `e2e` also within the `nightly.yaml` CI jobs, we can remove these older vestiges of bats tests and the associated artifacts and scripts.

title: Ensure that Connect Cloud supports specifying python versions in standard locations.
description:
With #2617, a Python version constraint can be specified with `.python-version`, `pyproject.toml`, and `setup.cfg`.

We noticed in #3249 this didn't seem to work with Connect Cloud. We should circle back and make sure that those are supported in Publisher with Connect Cloud so the experience is as similar as possible.

title: Write out TOML configuration files with commented-out fields and documentation
description: With the ability to maintain comments within TOML configuration files, we should then be able to produce our configuration files with all fields available within the schema, with documentation, but unused or defaults being commented out. This should improve the ability of users to interact with the configuration file, while reducing our immediate need to provide an editor for the files.

title: Maintain comments in TOML configuration files
description: A different TOML go package will need to either be found or written. This is done within several popular Python libraries, so perhaps we could port one of those from Python?

title: Add the ability to save the generated manifest.json file
description: This would help in both debugging as well as providing the ability to deploy using APIs.

title: Provide the ability to import an existing manifest.json file
description: This opens up additional workflows.

title: Provide the ability to edit credentials
description:
Should have the ability to edit existing credentials, without changing the GUID.

If allow to change the name, then will need to also update references within existing deployment files.

title: Expand the publisher log section with an error when deployment fails
description:
When the deployment fails, the log section in which the error occurred should be expanded, with the active visible line being shown as the last line of that section (or the specific error if we can find it).

Related issue (which won't be needed when this is completed):
https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/3192

title: Activate/Display publisher log upon start of deployment
description: Upon initiating the operation, the publisher log view should be shown.

title: Add automatic file scanning for HTML projects
description: See PR https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/3149 for the base implementation for Quarto, but the created scanner included support for HTML assets. Needs to be integrated and tested.

title: Add automatic file scanning for RMarkdown projects
description: See PR https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/3149 for the base implementation for Quarto, but the created scanner included support for RMarkdown assets. Needs to be integrated and tested.

title: Deployment Summary View: Add advanced edit link
description:
Which will bring up the configuration.TOML file for editing.
Perhaps also consider having link to bring up schema file (as a source of documentation)?

title: Deployment Summary View: add renv.lock status
description: Show location of renv.lock file, allow selection or use of default

title: Feature: Deployment Summary View
description:
This view displays a friendly summary of the deployment parameters and common/effective settings (read/only to start).

The information displayed initially will be the same details as those displayed by the configuration button’s tooltip.

It is automatically displayed upon activation of a deployment.

This replaces the default opening of the configuration TOML file for a better user experience.

title: Deployment Summary View - Allow add or removal of interpreter dependencies
description: Within the view, add a summary of the interpreters that are in use as well as the ones that are not in use. Allow the user to indicate whether the interpreter is needed or not needed for this deployment, and update the configuration.TOML file accordingly.

title: Deployment Summary View - Show active values (default or set) for interpreter versions
description:
Show the active values (default or set) for interpreter versions, as will be inserted into the manifest once the next deployment operation is initiated. 

Allow changing of the versions of an interpreter, and perform the operation for the user. 

For example, the user should be able to activate an action to set a specific version of the python version, in which they would be prompted for the version, and that version would be updated within the active configuration.TOML file for the user. 

They should also be able to set the option not to use the default (which should display the current value used in their active environment), prompting them with that active value already filled out, and update the toml file accordingly.

Consider supporting the minimum versions syntax as well as the single version specifier.

This should be available for Quarto, Python, R, and TensorFlow.

title: Remove Token Auth method when URL is Snowflake endpoint
description:
When creating a New Deployment in the Publishing Client, there's an option for `Token Authentication Recommended`, however that will not work when publishing to Connect inside Snowflake.  API Key is the only method that will work there.  

Is it possible to either detect when the target url is a Snowflake endpoint and entirely omit the Token Auth option, or at least remove the `Recommended` text?

title: missing dependencies in generated renv.lock file
description:
<!-- Please provide the following information to help us diagnose the issue, removing any sections that are not applicable. Thank you for your help! -->

## Problem statement

When I try to deploy an application, publisher generates an renv.lock file but it is missing dependencies.

## Steps to reproduce

Attempt to deploy the following application. Note that `shinychat` is a dependency but not actually used (was trying to use this app to test #3194).

```r
library("shiny")
library("shinychat")

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    numericInput("n", "n", 1),
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$plot <- renderPlot( plot(head(cars, input$n)) )
  }
)

shinyAppDir(system.file("examples/01_hello", package="shiny"))


# The object can be passed to runApp()
app <- shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    numericInput("n", "n", 1),
    plotOutput("plot")
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$plot <- renderPlot( plot(head(cars, input$n)) )
  }
)

runApp(app)
```

**Expected behavior:** <!-- What should have happened? -->

I would expect that with the currently released publisher, the generated renv.lock would contain both shiny and shinychat. Running the application on Connect would fail (because shinychat is installed from a subdirectory).  When using the version of publisher on the branch for #3194 I would expect the deployment to succeed and the application to run.

title: panic when deploying R content without an existing renv.lock file
description:
<!-- Please provide the following information to help us diagnose the issue, removing any sections that are not applicable. Thank you for your help! -->

## Problem statement

When I attempt to deploy an R shiny application without an existing renv.lock file, Publisher panics when trying to generate the lockfile.

## Steps to reproduce

Attempt to deploy this application:

```r
library("shiny")
library("bslib")
library("emoji")

ui <- page_fillable(
  layout_columns(
    card(
      card_header("Emoji selection"),
      selectizeInput(
        inputId = "name",
        label = "Emoji Name",
        choices = NULL
      ),
      textOutput(outputId = "emoji")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  updateSelectizeInput(
    session,
    "name",
    choices = names(emoji_name),
    server = TRUE
  )
  output$emoji <- renderText({
    req(input$name)
    emoji_name[[input$name]]
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

**Expected behavior:** <!-- What should have happened? -->

Application deploys to Connect

**Actual behavior:** <!-- What actually happened? -->

Publisher appears to hang. Output logs show a panic.

title: Extension contributes a button on Positron Data Explorer in v1.23.15
description: ## Problem statement Positron has support for viewing data in our [Data Explorer](https://positron.posit.co/data-explorer.html), and the Publisher extension is contributing its button on these tabs. ## Steps to reproduce 1. In Positron, run `View(mtcars)` in the R console 2. Notice that the Publisher extension contributes its button there, even though there is nothing that can be published there. **Expected behavior:** The extension should not contribute its button on these tabs. **Actual behavior:** The extension does contribute right now. ## System Details I've got v1.23.15 of the extension, and I think this is a new bug.

title: Consider changing behavior of View Publishing Logs button
description: ## Description Just noting that I found the experience when clicking the View Publishing Logs button (screenshot) surprising, and sent me down a path of struggling a bit to actually find the logs that would tell me why my app failed to publish. I think that button should go directly to the logs most users will be interested in, the ones that describe what went wrong / what they need to fix, which is usually not the information generated by the publisher extension but rather the logs generated on the server.

title: Render never finishes for quarto doc with R in a sub page
description:
## Problem statement

The Render Your Project button runs forever on a quarto project where R is only defined on a sub page.

## Steps to reproduce

I have a simple quarto site with 3 files where the main file (`index.qmd`) is vanilla markdown but the linked file uses R.

When I use the publisher to deploy this quarto site, I need to deploy rendered content (see #3190 ) so I create a new deployment and choose "Publish Rendered Documents only"

Once the deployment is created I click "Render Your Project" but this never finishes. Contents of my project are below.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d07e3504-5a50-451e-bc26-c015815ed000

`_quarto.yml`
```
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "Quarto Needs R"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: rstuff.qmd
        text: R Stuff

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo

description: ## Problem statement When clicking **‘View Content’** in the **Posit Publisher** tab after publishing a Quarto doc or Shiny dashboard, the user is redirected to a **login page** instead of the publicly deployed content. - This behavior is confusing, because it left me wondering if my content was actually publicly published. - Directing to public link would create a more straightforward, streamlined experience. ## Expected: User should be taken directly to the **publicly shared content** without being prompted to log in again. An example of a publicly shared content would be [this link](https://0199e2ef-65a5-1bde-fde9-ab40f95c1824.share.connect.posit.cloud/). ## Actual: User is redirected to the login page through a link like [this one](https://login.posit.cloud/login?redirect=%2Foauth%2Fauthorize%3Fclient_id%3Dposit-connect-cloud%26redirect_uri%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fconnect.posit.cloud%252Fauth%26response_type%3Dcode%26state%3DeyJyZWRpcmVjdCI6Ii9yb2RyaWdvc2Y2NzIvY29udGVudC8wMTk5ZTJlZi02NWE1LTFiZGUtZmRlOS1hYjQwZjk1YzE4MjQifQ%253D%253D&local=1&google=1&github=1&product=connect_cloud). ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use **Posit Publisher** to publish a Quarto document or Shiny dashboard. 2. After publishing, click **‘View’** (in lower-right notification pop-up) or **‘View Content’** (in Publisher UI tab). 3. Observe that the user is redirected to a login page. 4. Upon logging in, the deployed content is displayed (inside Connect Cloud). **Expected behavior:** The user should be sent **directly** to the publicly shared content, with NO additional authentication prompt. **Actual behavior:** The user is redirected to a login page before being able to access content that’s already public. ## System Details ``` Positron Version: 2025.11.0 build 63 Code - OSS Version: 1.104.0 Commit: 630a0d8b54a787b38feced01712847ba7ed3e931 Date: 2025-10-13T07:11:53.021Z Electron: 37.3.1 Chromium: 138.0.7204.235 Node.js: 22.18.0 V8: 13.8.258.31-electron.0 OS: Darwin arm64 25.0.0 ``` ## Publishing information - **Content type:** Quarto document or Shiny dashboard

title: Permission issues are preventing files from being removed from deployments.
description:
## Problem statement

Permission issues are preventing files from being removed from deployments.

## Steps to reproduce

This was testing by publishing to Connect Cloud from Positron. Its a bit contrived but we have seen at least 1 user run into what we think is a similar issue.

1. create a new project (I tested with a python shiny app)
2. deploy to Connect Cloud
3. create a subdirectory, I called my `.hidden` with a single file in it (`file.txt`)
4. In the Publish Project Files list, check the box to include `.hidden/file.txt` in the deployment
5. Deploy to Connect Cloud
6. `chmod 600 .hidden`
7. Close Positron and reopen it
8. I can no longer expand `.hidden` in the Publish Project Files pane. When i deploy, the bundle always includes an empty `.hidden` folder and I can't get rid of it. (Unless i go fix the permissions, at which point everything is fine.)

**Expected behavior:**
A little unclear, its admittedly contrived, but I think the Publisher should allow me to exclude this folder somehow, or at least exclude the folder that it can't access from the bundle.

**Actual behavior:**
The bundle includes an empty folder

## System Details

## System Information

- **Posit Publisher Version**: 1.23.11
- **Platform**: darwin arm64
- **IDE**: Positron 1.103.0

title: bug: The publisher output stream names are confusing
description: For output streams, qe have two named ones: `Posit Publisher Authentication` and `Posit Publisher Deployment` Practically speaking, the Authentication one has very few lines in it ever (I haven't yet traced what uses it) and the s-called Deployment one has everything in it. title: Missing fields when converting `renv.lock` to `manifest.json`
description:
We aren't fully copying all fields from `renv.lock` and that is hitting errors with packages installed from it sources. 

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/b6626c5dbfaca47ebf23be71cde5c046a23e2bed/internal/inspect/dependencies/renv/lockfile.go#L37-L73 lacks fields like `RemoteHost` and `GithubSHA1` 

This then leads to `archiveUrl` being empty during a packrat restore (with the error `Error in if (!grepl("^http", archiveUrl)) {: argument is of length zero`) https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/blob/b3127db3cea2144b1e3bd9c17de1da277b4776e9/R/github.R#L72-L98

We should enrich our test fixtures to include these (for example, https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/b6626c5dbfaca47ebf23be71cde5c046a23e2bed/internal/inspect/dependencies/renv/testdata/sample-renv.lock doesn't include any git-installed packages) and confirm that the manifest includes all of the fields that are in the `renv.lock` file in the correct places.

title: bug: ephemeral `renv.lock` file creation sometimes doesn't get all of the dependencies when it is listed in `[files]`
description:
This is similar to #3063 when deploying a shiny app, I tried creating renv infrastructure first (publishing) then deleting the `renv.lock` file. Because we don't (yet) remove the `renv.lock` file form the config file's `files` array, it is still there.  I found that this would create the ephemeral lockfile just fine, but the lockfile (and thus the manifest) would be missing critical packages (and most critically shiny itself!) 

I'm attaching the ephemeral lockfiles that show up in .posit/publish/deployments to help show this, but I've been able to recreate it with the steps above very reliably.

The `renv.lock` file when I've deleted the lockfile, but it is still listed in the `files` array: 
[renv.lock-in-files.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22319039/renv.lock-in-files.txt)

The `renv.lock` file when I've deleted the lockfile *and* removed it from the `files` array too:
[renv.lock-not-in-files.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22319042/renv.lock-not-in-files.txt)

This might seem like an edge case, but it is exactly the state that someone would get to if they tried once with renv, and then came back to a project later and weren't able to update the lockfile with renv and so want to start from scratch.

title: feat: sniff + add positron's configured repositories when calling renv (especially `renv::init()`)
description:
Positron, and especially positron on workbench will frequently be configured with Posit Package Manager as the source of packages. This is especially important on Linux systems, since package manager hosts binaries for them, but standard CRAN repositories do not. 

In our current setup, the publisher uses standard R calls, which don't have Positron's set repository injected. For example, calling R like we do in the publisher returns this:

```
$ /opt/R/4.4.3/bin/R -s -e "options('repos')"
WARNING: ignoring environment value of R_HOME
$repos
    CRAN 
"@CRAN@" 
``` 

But from a new positron terminal we see:

```
options('repos')
$repos
                                                         CRAN 
"https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest" 
attr(,"IDE")
[1] TRUE
```

In this state, when we (ephemerally) call `renv::init()`, we end up building every package from source that is necessary to run the item being published, which can take a long time (hours, sometimes!). And will also frequently fail because of misconfigured or missing system dependencies for building packages. 

We need to make sure that when publisher is calling `renv::init()` we try and use the repositories that are set in Positron so we have a higher chance of hitting Posit Package Manager (either our public one or one in a customer environment).

title: bug(connect): Python version confusion
description:
I was trying to deploy an app to Connect (my local dev environment) and was testing out all of the new flows. It's a lot better! Though I still had to skirt around #2823. I pressed the button to make my requirements.txt and pressed deploy, and it failed. The error says: 

> Python 3.9 is not available on the server. Consider editing your configuration to use version 3.11.3.

So I clicked "editing", which opens the toml file. It just says `[python]`, there is no version specified. So (a) why does it think I want Python 3.9, or care about the Python version at all? And (b) how might I specify the Python version? Completely opaque to me. 

I'm guessing this has to do with the manifest.json that gets magically generated for me, and that must be specifying a particular Python version. That's not great but I understand that's where things stand today. But I am a little lost as to what I could possibly do about this. And I'm guessing we can handle this a lot better, even with the current constraints.

I tried adding `version = "3.11"` under `[python]` and that seemed valid (no red squigglies from the TOML extension), but it was rejected as an invalid version. It failed pretty fast so IDK if that was coming from the publisher or from Connect. But "3.11" seems like it should be valid. 

What's further weird is that the virtualenv I have active is Python 3.12. Sounds related to #2825. At least if the python version it was saying I wanted matched what I was actually using, I might have some intuition for how to change it--I could make a venv with whatever version you said I needed.

Right now there's no way to access the non-production environments of Connect Cloud by default. If you want to do so, you have to launch the extension in a development configuration and set `CONNECT_CLOUD_ENV`. It would be nice if there were a way to easily configure this.

Some options:

- Add a command palette item to switch the environment

Ideally this is as invisible as possible to our regular users who don't have access to alternate environments.

title: chore: automate schema updates
description:
We currently have a manual process for schema updates: What could we do to make this automated? Surely we can have GHA push changes to S3 for us when that happens?

As Pull Requests are merged into main, we update (or create in the case of a new
schema) the file on the CDN (in S3). Currently, this is a manual process:

- Log into the AWS console (https://rstudio.awsapps.com/start/#/)
- Select `Posit Connect Production`, then `Power User`.
- Select `View all services`, then `S3`.
- Open the `Posit Publisher` bucket, then the `publisher` folder.
- Click `Upload`, then `Add Folder`.
- Select your local `schemas` folder (`internal/schema/schemas`).
- Click the `Upload` button to complete the upload.
- Verify availability of the updated schema(s) on the CDN. There may be a delay due to caching.
  - https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json
  - https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-record-schema-v3.json

1. new deployment
2. publish content to a free account cred
3. deploy a second time after first one is successful

### Publisher Output and Logs

`Error in update content response: unexpected response from the server (402: {"error":"Account does not have the entitlement to create private content.","error_type":"not_entitled_private_content","error_args":{"account_id":"01991600-039e-79a5-0bef-7a457d353f27"}}). See [Troubleshooting docs](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md) for help.`

title: bug: Accept both `https://connect.company.com/connect` as well as `https://connect.company.com/`
description: It's magical and entirely unclear if someone should supply `https://connect.company.com/connect` or `https://connect.company.com/` as the _correct_ URL when making a credential. We should accept either (we can silently rewrite https://connect.company.com/connect` to `https://connect.company.com/` once we detect that that is the right URL.

title: bug: logs output remembers the collapsed / not state from previous views
description:
If I have a log stage (like "Run Content") open and I re-deploy, that stage will be opened when it gets to that stage. But if it was collapsed before it would stay collapsed. This is confusing (and can sometimes cover up the error).

What if: we always opened a stage when it was running, and auto-folded it when it completed successfully. This way people saw the details of what's going on, but it was folded when it was done. I thought this is how it worked already, but the current behavior of opening if it was previously open feels like a bug (even if it's not technically a bug). 

Came up in user testing with @blairj09

title: feat: Auto-scroll / follow the bottom of the logs viewer
description:
## Description

During a deploy, if someone opens up the publisher logs output, we should auto-scroll to the bottom  / follow the flow (like a terminal does) so that folks see what the most recent steps are.

Came up in user testing with @blairj09

title: feat: Open connect logs in file viewer
description:

The logs viewer is really great in that it curates logs, but it would be nice to be able to open the text of logs in the file viewer itself. This would make searching, copying, pasting, etc. much easier *and* it would let someone use this as input in positron assistant too.

Came up in user testing with @blairj09

description:

We can add items to the right click menu when you click on a file in the file explorer: can we add "publish this file" that does the same flow as the button on top of the file viewer (create a new deployment or take me to the first available one)? 

Requested during user testing with @blairj09

feat: Make a force-deploy option
description:
There are some states where deploying is not going to lead to a correct state #2823 but we also have run into a number of times where our overly protective guards have _prevented_ totally valid states from deploying due to bugs in our guards.

As a compromise, what if we changed the deploy button to a split dropdown where it is disabled as a button if we think things are bad, but there's on option to click the dropdown and then a second option that is like "Deploy anyway". This way folks always have an out and aren't stuck, but have to do slightly more work to override what we believe is a bad state.

description:
Noticed at https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2936#issuecomment-3230076913

It seems we are not validating that the entrypoint in the deployment configuration does exist, which we could do as part of the pre-flight checks to prevent failed deployments sooner.

title: Add utm params to Connect Cloud redirects
description:
## Description

Add utm params to have a sense of traffic coming from Publisher usage to Connect Cloud. 

**Potential params**

* utm_source=publisher _or_ utm_source=publisher-{ide-name}: `positron` _or_ `vs-code`
* utm_medium=ide
* utm_campaign={worklflow-type}: `auth` (anything leading to a sign up/in path) _or_ `content` (anything leading to a content page)

I know have a lot of redirects and open to discuss potential to add the more dynamic options above or keep it simple with a static `?utm_source=publisher&utm_medium=ide` for all Connect Cloud links.

title: Replace html content type with static
description:
Based on a comment from Marcos: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2956#discussion_r2308099159

For both Connect and Connect Cloud, `static` is the proper type for prerendered static content. When we create content on either platform, we end up mapping `html` to `static`. Thus, we should just call this type `static`.

This will require an addition to the `contenttypes.ContentType` type and the JSON schema.

We'll need to remain backwards-compatible with existing `html` content, though. Our mappings should remain, but any new content should be created with the `static` type.

title: fix cloud-related issues in configuration.md
description:
## Description

We should proof-read configuration.md for any mistakes related to Cloud. So far we've identified these problems:
- `connect_cloud` needs to be mentioned as an allowed value for `product_type`
- r and python version fields are valid for connect_cloud

title: Help out on rendering Quarto documents if there are no existing renderings
description:
**Edit:**

The Quarto Extension wasn't really suited for our use case, instead we will have to call `quarto render` directly.

---

**Original:**

For Quarto deployments, when opting to "Publish rendered document only" and there are no renderings, call the Quarto Extension (if available) to pre-render the document so the resulting configuration is accurate with the static files to be deployed.

The available commands from the Quarto Extension that can help with this, depending on the project, are:
- `quarto.renderProject` (If there is a `_quarto.yml` present, we want to render the project)
- `quarto.renderDocument` (No `_quarto.yml`? render the doc passed as entrypoint)

title: Setup automated pre-releases
description:
Positron and VS Code users of the Publisher extension can click "Switch to Pre-Release Version" to get auto-updates for the pre-release version of Publisher. We currently do not frequently release pre-release versions, but doing so would allow us to get feedback quickly on the new things we are building with the expectation that it is a pre-release and may have bugs (even though we attempt to keep `main` release-able) 

We can do this on merges to `main` or if we are worried about the high frequency of releases we could do this nightly if there is a new commit to tag on `main`.

title: Communicate the rendering state for projects
description:
**Last Edit:**

- Disable Deploy Your Project button if the project rendering entrypoint does not exist.
- Use the deployment status message (where we show Not Yet Deployed or Last Deployment Successful) to also communicate more prominently the result of the rendering.
    - Render does not exist
    - _(hits render button)_ Render was successful
    - _(hits render button)_ Cannot render, Quarto not found on the system
    - _(hits render button)_ Render failed

---

**Edit:**

Since we will leverage on the Quarto Extension to try rendering the project if there are no renderings present, the error message is expected to be shown when there are no renderings and it wasn't possible to render (because there is no extension or it failed on rendering).

---

**Original description**

When publishing the rendered document for a Quarto project and there is NO rendered assets, Publisher allows you to deploy with a configuration including the expected assets but the bundle will practically be empty because such renderings are not to be found.

We should present a warning or error when trying to deploy.

_No response_

Positron

examples-quarto-r

### Problem Statement

When you try to add a credential (in this case for PCC) as part of the new deployment workflow, if the deployment fails with an error, the credential does get added, but the UI doesn't refresh to show it automatically.  The user must hit the refresh button to see that it was actually successfully added.

In my case, I tried to add it again thinking it failed along with the deployment failure, but then was prompted that I didn't have any available accounts to use for the credential.  But that was only because my single account for this credential was already added without me knowing it

title: Add new deployment workflow E2E tests for Connect Cloud
description: Setup the happy path e2e flow for both creating a new credential and then deploying a simple project

title: Recover from panics when publishing
description:
We have a middleware set up here to recover from panics:

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/ac93bde519af4835b2be7f0f7dff86cfc171d8ea/internal/services/middleware/panic_recovery.go#L12

Without this code, the agent crashes upon panics. However, we start goroutines ourselves a few times (all initiated under `POST /api/deployments/$NAME`). Panics occurring inside those aren't able to be recovered by our middleware. We should recover those too as a precaution to prevent the agent from crashing.

Alternatively, is it possible to restart the agent from the extension code when it crashes?

title: Confusing messaging when Connect Cloud credential is deleted
description: When we delete a credential used for a Connect Cloud deployment, we show the following messaging: However, this is a little confusing. If "no credential was found for the deployment's server", why do I see a Connect Cloud cred in my list down below? The real reason for the error message is that there wasn't a credential set up for the same _account_ on Connect Cloud. Our messaging here should reflect that. Note that this messaging is still appropriate for Connect, for which only one credential is allowed per server.

title: Consider adding a .gitignore to the .posit/publish directory excluding deployments/
description:
## Description
An enhancement suggestion in consideration of a  user story like this:

As a member of a data science team,
I want to develop my project in git, and deploy it to Connect [Cloud] from Positron

I think in this case, every time I deploy, a file will be generated under .posit/publish/deployments/*, so could be a lot of files over time.

When I want to share a change to the app that I made with my team, I need to figure out what is this new file, does it _need_ to be in git for future deployments made from other machines to work, or can I omit it from my change set / PR to minimize distractions.

We could save folks time by providing guidance about whether these files should be in version control. If they aren't really needed to be shared, we could communicate that guidance by adding a .gitignore file in the .posit or .posit/publish directory to exclude the deployment records from source control by default.

title: Quarto Deployments: Detect the configuration alternative for static/rendered content on project inspection
description:
Provide the configuration alternative for Quarto when `POST inspect` is called by including a new alternatives field on the configuration:
```go
type Config struct {
    //...
    Alternatives      []Config      `toml:"-" json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
```

This new field should be populated by the `QuartoDetector` when there is a possible static version of the content. Such static version configuration should:
1. populate the `Files` attribute with the applicable rendered version of the project files.
2. `Type` should be `ContentTypeHTML` for the rendered version

For this work, it is important to rely heavily on what `quarto inspect` output provides for `output-dir` and `files` (the `files` JSON data is already filtered down by the possible presence of `_quarto.yml#project.render`).

If there is not an `output-dir` stated, an `.html` naming version of files listed under `files` should be used.

title: Quarto Deployments: Prompt deployment type selection (source code or existing renderings)
description: When creating a new deployment, after the inspection is done and before entering a title for the deployment, we want to ask the user to choose between publishing the source code or an existing rendering. **Technical approach:** The `type ConfigurationDetails` can have a new `alternatives?: []ConfigurationDetails` prop to indicate the project has more than one possible configuration for the content type. Just before `step.INPUT_TITLE`, eval if `newDeploymentData.entrypoint.inspectionResult.configuration.alternatives` exists so we need to show the main option for `inspectionResult.configuration` as well as options for `inspectionResult.configuration.alternatives`. We could, rely only on the extension side code to notice if `quarto-static` content type is detected, then show the additional `push rendered content` option. However the inspection step returns the configuration options that, after selected, end up sent to be saved as a file by the agent. So, we need the resulting configurations for the static rendering alternatives up front with the related files listed.

title: app_mode: unknown is a bad experience
description:
If you specify an entrypoint file and Publisher can't infer what "app mode" it should be on Connect, it generates `app-mode: unknown`. Technically you can edit the TOML to change this, but in practice it is not something mortals can do. 

My use case was deploying a Python app that uses a framework based on FastAPI, so we can support it. But it doesn't import FastAPI, so the detection does not work. 

We believe that having a published TOML schema, and using the TOML plugin, you can get hints to help create valid configuration. I tried to lean into that. So, I start trying to type over "unknown", and a red squiggly line appears under it and tells me what the valid values are. Cool. I never would have guessed that it should be "python-fastapi" otherwise. So I type that, and then... the whole TOML file gets red squigglies! On hover, now it says `"python" is a required property` So I start typing `python =` on a new line and the squigglies go away. I guess that this must be the python version, so I type "3.12", but now `python` has a squiggly under it that says `"3.12" is not of type "object"`. Ok, so... what is an object in TOML? I type `python = {}` and the squigglies go away. But surely that can't be right, I haven't specified anything!

The only reasonable workaround I found was to (after deleting all of `.posit`) put a fake import in my entrypoint file (`import fastapi` in this case), running the detection again to get the right `python-fastapi` and other bits in place, and then deleting the fake import. That's not great.

title: Not at all obvious how to specify an entrypoint that is not at the top level
description:
if you pick an entrypoint that is in a subdir, it assumes you are only working within that subdir. That's usually reasonable but not always. But if it is actually what you want, how do you even get there?

What I did, after it created all of the .posit tomls in the subdir: 

* Delete `.posit/**`
* Make a copy of `my_subdir/app.py` to the top level
* Generate the deployment TOMLs off of that
* Delete the top level app.py and select all the right files to include
* Fix `entrypoint`. This part was extra tricky because entrypoint has to be the python import invocation, not the file path. So `my_subdir.app:app`. This of course I only discovered by trying to deploy and interpreting the logs from the failure.

This is not the most pressing use case to support. But it's frustrating because it's one of a few places where the alleged flexibility of the TOMLs turns out to be frustrating--sure, you could technically write the TOMLs yourself to be correct, but how in the world would you know how?

title: A perceptible pause when creating a new deployment after selecting the entry point (on Positron Pro)
description: I haven't been able to get a minimal reprex yet, but don't want to loose this regardless: I'm working from the connect-extensions repo and deploying one of the subdirectories (the quarto-stock-report-r) using Positron Pro on Workbench + the publisher. I'm often seeing significant (a second or two) delays when creating a new deployment, after I select the quarto document before I get to the naming step. There is a working indicator and it always eventually gets there, but it's surprising to me that there is any perceptible pause at that point.

title: Use my currently active Python interpreter to scan for dependencies
description:
## System details

    Publisher Version        : I don't know where to find this, but you may also want to know that I'm using Positron
    Connect Version          : irrelevant
    Your OS                  : macos
    Content Type to Deploy   : irrelevant

I just clicked the "Scan" button under "Python packages" (following #2824), and the requirements.txt it generated starts with this comment:

```
# requirements.txt auto-generated by Posit Publisher
# using /opt/homebrew/bin/python3
```

I know I know, don't use homebrew python. But the thing is, I'm not! I have a `uv` virtualenv active. So I would have expected `.venv/bin/python` to be used instead.

IDK that this would matter in practice, based on what the requirements.txt scanning does, but I wanted to flag it.

title: Generate requirements.txt from pyproject.toml, uv.lock, whatever else
description:
It's fine (in the sense of a dog having coffee surrounded by flames) that Connect requires a requirements.txt file for specifying dependencies and doesn't support the other various Python standards. But just like how Publisher automatically generates a manifest.json based on its TOML, it could generate a requirements.txt from pyproject.toml, uv.lock, and whatever other files we wanted, so that it doesn't just error.

Relatedly, if you're on the Python packages tab, instead of offering to scan the .py files for dependencies, if there is one of these files in the repo, you could generate requirements.txt from it. Though in this case, I'm thinking that requirements.txt could be ephemerally created like manifest.json, we shouldn't need to check in two different ways for specifying deps that could get out of sync with each other.

title: Don't let me deploy if you already know I can't successfully deploy
description: I created a new Python project in Positron, which offers to create a pyproject.toml for me. Cool. So that's where I listed out my dependencies. I created a new deployment or whatever in Publisher, it detected what kind of content I was trying to deploy and generated the publishing toml files. Then the thing in the sidebar gave me the big blue "Deploy your project" button. That was way more prominent than the little caution icon down below in the collapsed parts of the accordion: Clicking the big blue button, the deployment predictably failed because there was no requirements.txt file. But you knew that already, that's why you flagged it below. Why not make me fix that before letting be click deploy?

title: Shiny Express deployments to Connect Cloud don't work
description: Attempting to publish https://github.com/posit-hosted/examples-shiny-python leads to this error (in the PCC UI): Publisher is choosing to set the primary file as `shiny.express.app:app_2e_py` based on this being an Express app, but we expect to receive the actual filename. When publishing to PCC, we should make sure to set the entrypoint to the actual file.

title: Improve Connect Cloud publish failure error messaging
description:
Right now we only display the error code. We need to translate the code into a human-readable error message. There's an error_args field on the response that will be useful for this.

We should be able to use the same logic we have in the UI for translation here. (Hopefully some day in the future there will be a more centralized way to do these translations so that we're not duplicating this.)

Dependency on: Experience team exposing error handling formatting in `vivid-api`

title: Improved logs experience
description:
When something goes wrong the Publisher should get someone to where they need to look to see what's wrong in a quick and straightforward way.

This will contain sub-issues that improve the logs user experience.

Since we want to pull this together for the next release if any of the sub-issues require a significant refactor we can punt them off and address them in the future.

title: Cannot deploy an app when a dependency was installed from r-universe.dev
description:

title: Publisher + Quarto: Rendered document smoothing
description:
[project design document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AF_9QTusq_eON_Vbgf946m2H4P34odw40dkMDngx37c/edit?tab=t.0)

Main issue to track work to enhance the experience when publishing reports with Publisher.

> You can publish the output of quarto docs, but you have to know to go to the html file and then do that there. The publisher should prompt / let you know that you have two options with quarto: send the quarto and have connect render it or you render on your own and then send that to connect.

title: Updating file selection without product_type in file writes invalid data
description:
To reproduce:
1. Create a deployment for Connect
2. Delete the `product_type = 'connect'` line in your config file
3. Add a file in the homeview's project file section - this will add `product_type = ''`, which is invalid

title: Refactor the multi-step extension code to eliminate create credential code duplication
description: Eliminate code duplication for creating a new credential between the `newDeployment.ts` file and the `newCredential.ts` file.

title: Re-introduce the enable Connect Cloud Publisher config
description: Re-introduce the enable Connect Cloud Publisher config and cut a release.

title: Support setting vanity URL & content access through TOML file for Connect Cloud
description: Allow the user to edit the TOML file to add the vanity URL & content access for Connect Cloud and have the schema respect those settings.

title: Verify bundle upload size before upload
description:
Make sure the bundle size does exceed the maximum bundle size allowed by `vivid-intake`. This limit should be exposed by `vivid-api`.

Will likely need the experience team to do the extra work to expose the limit size.

title: Create a local Publisher extension installation file for tech testing
verify Connect Cloud appmode mappings
description:
We have a mapping from app mode to connect cloud content type here: 
https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/aea50a23d859ca2d2d71ab3d1a62c2d321dc58cb/internal/publish/connect_cloud/content_request_base.go#L12-L30

But I'm not sure they're all correct. We need to make sure each type works as intended, or errors properly if they're not supported.

I'm trying to deploy a Shiny app that uses `shinychat`, which is 1) installed from GitHub and 2) installed from a subdirectory in the repo, with

```r
renv::install("posit-dev/shinychat/pkg-r")
