title: Python projects auto-select requirements.txt but it is not visibly checked in the UI
description: ## System details Publisher Version : 1.18.1 Connect Version : 2025.08.0-dev+60-gfac490d2be Your OS : Mac OSX 15.6 (24G84) Content Type to Deploy : Quarto with Python ## Publisher Output and Logs N/A this is a pre-deployment issue ## Problem Statement When creating a new deployment for a Quarto report utilizing Python the `requirements.txt` file appears to be auto-selected but it is not visually checked like my entrypoint file. ## Steps to Reproduce - Clone https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-extensions - Open extensions/content-health-monitor/content-health-monitor.qmd - Setup a new deployment using Publisher - Observe that `requirements.txt` is auto-selected but not visually checked like the entrypoint file - Observe that `requirements.txt` is listed in the `files` array in the toml This does not appear to be related to Quarto and is reproducible with other Python projects such as extensions/stock-api-fastapi/main.py

title: refresh the access token when it expires
description: Right now we store an access token and a refresh token for cloud, but the access token expires somewhat quickly. We need to refresh it when it expires.

title: make creating deployment config file work for connect cloud
description:
Creating a config follows this process:
1. In the extension, call POST /inspect to get the config data
1. Add the product type to the config data
1. In the extension, call PUT /configurations/{name} with the config data
    1. In the agent, validate the config data against the schema
    3. In the agent, write the config to the TOML file

Since we currently use the same Config struct to represent both Connect and Connect Cloud configurations, some fields are only valid for one of the product types. The config returned by `POST /inspect` populates some of those fields, so the validation in 3.i fails. 

We should update `PUT /configurations/{name}` to unset those fields so that the validation can pass and we can write a valid TOML file.

title: feat: Activate deployment target from diff viewer
description:
## Description

If you're working on an app or deploy target inside a git repo, you may open the diff viewer to see changes you've made to your file. You may realize, from those changes, that your app is out of date and click the publisher icon in the toolbar.

When clicked from the diff viewer, the publisher icon does not change the deployment target. This _does work_ when activating Publisher from a normal editor for the target source. So it's easy to think it will also work from the diff viewer and accidentally deploy the wrong app.

title: feat: hide files when including for deployment
description: ## Description This is taken from internal ticket 119662 A minor UX suggestion to benefit Posit Connect users that may alternate between using RStudio and Positron: the screenshot below on the right is from RStudio, showing what the project files deployment window looks like for the exact same app as the Positron screenshots on the left. --- --- You'll notice that the RStudio window automatically hides files/folders that either don't need to be deployed or are required for deployment (e.g. `.Rprofile`, `.posit/`, `renv/`, `renv.lock`, `rsconnect/`). This is a nice feature! Since it probably won't initially be obvious to Posit Connect newbs (like me!) whether these files will have any impact on deployment, it's probably best to hide them (or lock their checkboxes) in the Positron Publisher so users don't have to worry about it.

title: Store each credential as it's own entry in the keychain
description:
Follow on from #2769 

On macOS, keychain items have a maximum capacity of 3,000 bytes. With the addition of token-based auth that is quickly exhausted when we store all credentials in a single keychain file. Instead of serializing all of them into a single keychain entry, we should save each credential to a separate entry and then turn them into a list in our Go code.

title: feat: Change deployment selection on file change
description:
## Description

A feature request that came up while talking to @wch was to change the Deployment selection in the home view sidebar automatically when the opened file in VS Code changes.

We track the active text editor, notebook, or document in `entrypointTracker.ts` we could utilize those same watchers to make selections if a deployment exists for that potential entrypoint.

---

Side note: personally I would want to turn this off as automatic selections would be a bit dizzying to me, but it is easy enough to add a configuration option. We could default it to on if we think my opinion is fringe.

title: Renv automatic setup doesn't use subdirectories
description:
When using the "Setup renv" button in the notification when deploying without an `renv.lock` it does not work if the deployment is inside of a subdirectory of the workspace. Instead the `renv.lock` is created at the root level, the deployment configuration includes `/.renv.lock` but that file doesn't exist inside of that folder.

This leads to a state where users are repeatedly asked to setup `renv` despite clicking the button each time.

title: Connect Cloud device auth polling interval is slow
description: The device auth polling interval, currently five seconds, can create a pretty noticeable gap between clicking authorize and seeing the extension move to the next step. Maybe we could consider reducing it, or ask for the interval returned to us to be reduced.

title: improve Connect Cloud credential conflict error message
description: We should have better messaging when you create a Connect Cloud credential that conflicts with an existing one. Right now we have a popup that just says "Conflict". The Connect flow handles this better:

title: improve messaging for Connect Cloud creation
description: When the extension kicks you over to the UI to create a Connect Cloud account, and the prompt is asking if you want to open the external website (the `/account/done` page), it would be helpful to include a message in the multistepper like "Waiting for account creation..." instead of "Retrieving accounts from Connect Cloud". Otherwise first-time users won't actually know why it's opening a new page. Note this will only apply to VS Code users since Positron trusts our domain already.

title: Generate the dependency portion of R manifests from renv.lock directly
description:
With https://github.com/rstudio/renv/pull/2059 the renv lockfiles should have all the information we need to construct manifests without needing to have a working install of that exact version in an active library. We should update our manifest generation code to do this directly. If we can't, we should raise issues with renv and resolve those too.

Related to (and would likely solve some of the frustration described in) #2646 but the discussion there took a different path (discussion around interpreters) and don't want to overload that issue with this idea.

title: feat: add rsconnect-style token authentication
description:
## Description
Onboarding should be as simple as possible. Though we should pursue a more modern authentication mechanism in Connect (and the publisher), just like Connect Cloud has, we should also make it easy for users of current versions for Connect to authenticate too.

title: feat: add more detail to TOML/JSON schema validation errors
description: ## Description There's two issues I've noticed with our TOML/JSON schema validation: **Case A:** Schema validation errors are very undetailed. This error is due to missing a `[python]` header in the file, which I was only able to discover through using the Even Better TOML extension: We should be able to return a detailed error message including the precise path to the error and why it violated the schema. **Case B:** There's another category of errors that give a line number, but no further information about what's wrong. Here is an example due to a misspelled property: In this case, I think the error is coming from our TOML validation library, which I've heard has limitations on the level of detail it's able to provide. However, we may be able to instead or additionally return a detailed error as is possible in case A.

title: Irrelevant level=ERROR "Error running command" message in logs
description:
## System details

    Publisher Version        : 1.18.1
    Connect Version          : 1.27.0
    Your OS                  : Ubuntu 22.04 (workbench.posit.it)
    Content Type to Deploy   : Quarto doc

## Publisher Output and Logs

```

time=2025-07-31T20:10:58.604Z level=ERROR msg="Error running command" command=/opt/R/4.5.1/bin/R error="exit status 1"
Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called ‘renv’
Calls: loadNamespace -> withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> doWithOneRestart
Execution halted
time=2025-07-31T20:10:58.604Z level=WARN msg="Couldn't detect lockfile path from R executable (renv::paths$lockfile()); is renv installed?"
```

## Problem Statement

When attempting to troubleshoot publishing errors, a `level=ERROR` message can be found in the logs stating that the `renv` package could not be found. While the content of the message is accurate, this is not a fatal error, and if the actual problem is corrected, the publishing process can complete successfully even though this message continues to appear.

In my particular case, there was a TOML schema validation error, but nothing in the logs suggested that this was the problem. This `renv` error was the only `level=ERROR` message in the entire log output.

## Steps to Reproduce

* Start a Positron session in Workbench.
    * The `renv` R package should not be installed; this is true for a fresh user on workbench.posit.it.
* Open a Quarto project that's set up to publish.
* (Optional) Have a schema validation error in your TOML.
    * The "Error running command" appears in the logs during the validation step even if there isn't a validation error.
* Open the Posit Publisher Deployment page in the Output tab.
* Observe the error quoted above in the logs.

title: e2e tests require container restart to reflect code changes
description:
To run the end to end tests, we spin up a vs code container. The container's entrypoint script installs the extension immediately, but never updates the installed extension, even though the current extension file is always visible inside the container through the volume mount. This means if you make changes to the extension code, you also have to restart the container for them to be reflected in the test.

As part of the `just dev` target in `test/e2e`, we should add a step to (re)install the extension once the vs code container is started. We should also probably remove the code from the entrypoint that installs it.

title: Add new credential workflow E2E tests for Connect Cloud
description:
Add E2E tests for the following new Connect Cloud credential flows:
- case 1: there is only one publishable account, use it and create the credential
- case 2: there are multiple publishable accounts, display the account selector so the user can select the account to create the credential
- case 3: there are no publishable accounts, but the user has at least one account, so they could be a guest or viewer on that account, ask if they want to sign up and let them sign up, authenticate them create and create an account to use to create the credential
- case 4: there are zero accounts for the user, so they must be going through the sign up process, open a browser to finish creating the account in Connect Cloud and use it to create the credential

**Note:** New credentials can be created from two places:
1. Create New Credential
2. Create New Deployment

Check that all the other existing create new credential flows (i.e. Posit Connect) are not affected.

## Problem Statement

When using the configuration option to disable keychain usage for credentials, the user is unable to create a deployment if there is not a matching credential already existing within the keychain. New deployment flows of using existing credentials as well as creating new credentials will fail with the error "Failed to create pre-deployment record. cannot get account named 'off-host': no such account" (in this case, the credential account was named "off-host").

Switching the configuration option to enable keychain usage for credentials functions correctly and as expected.

(Window must be reloaded after making the configuration change.)

## Steps to Reproduce

See this video for reproduction. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d62924c-bab3-49a0-b282-8e8c00d26992

The important factors here are:
- Keychain access is disabled and the agent has been initialized with that option. This only occurs when the agent is started initially, so a reload of the VSCode instance is required.
- The name used for the non-keychain credentials must not exist within the keychain credentials
- This does not apply to the workbench environment or one in which the OS does not have a keychain provider active. That will function correctly.

title: feat: Support configuration of client timeout for publishing
description:
## Description

An issue was raised by support that a customer was unable to publisher their app due to a timeout error in the publisher extension. Their app fails to upload when it includes the accompanying dataset that is about 1gb.

After inspecting timeout settings in the repo, we found that the current timeout on the client is hardcoded to [2 minutes](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/internal/publish/publish.go#L199). This should be modified to be configurable in the extension settings by the user in order match the capabilities of rsconnect-python ([line](https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/blob/main/rsconnect/timeouts.py#L15)). It seems that rsconnect has no timeout for publishing apps.

Ideally this value is set to a higher value (10+ minutes) or defaults to unlimited with the ability to change this if necessary in the settings of the extension.

title: Add Connect Cloud support for the Homeview
description:
### Description

title: Update the TOML file schemas
description:
### Description

Update the TOML file schemas to support Connect Cloud.

Create schema v4:

- In the publishing record schema, make the following changes:
  - Allow `server_type` to be set to `connect_cloud`.
- In the publishing schema, make the following changes:
  - Add the `server_type` field that's included in the publishing record schema. Connect-specific fields will be included only when `server_type` is connect, and vice versa with Connect Cloud.
  - Certain root-level fields will move into the connect object:
    - `access`
    - `schedules` (draft)
    - `tags` (draft)
  - Other fields will be conditionally excluded from the schema based on server_type, using JSON Schema `oneOf`:
    - `has_parameters`
    - `python.package_file`
    - `python.package_manager`
    - `python.requires_python`
    - `r.package_file`
    - `r.package_manager`
    - `r.requires_r`
    - `jupyter.hide_all_input`
    - `jupyter.hide_tagged_input`
    - `quarto.version`
    - `quarto.engines`
    - `connect`
  - Add a `connect_cloud` object field with the following subfields:
    - `account_name`
    - `vanity_name`
    - `access.organization_access`
    - `access.public_access`
  - Update the error handling to include field information from JSON Schema validation errors. (nice-to-have)
  - Running the publisher plugin a v3 schema file will automatically convert the schema file to v4.

Note: moving access from the root level into connect is the only breaking change. If we feel this change isn't important enough to warrant a new major schema version, we can keep the current version and conditionally allow the field when server_type is connect.

title: Posit Publisher: Please consider abandoning renv requirement for publishing to Connect
description:
<!--

Take a look at our guidance on feedback and issues:
https://positron.posit.co/feedback.html

-->

## System details:

#### Positron and OS details:

Positron Version: 2025.06.0 (Universal) build 167
Code - OSS Version: 1.100.0
Commit: e7e5d5590adc6bf7b760f837051cd2f57ea9e3dc
Date: 2025-05-29T20:44:08.369Z
Electron: 34.5.1
Chromium: 132.0.6834.210
Node.js: 20.19.0
V8: 13.2.152.41-electron.0
OS: Darwin x64 24.5.0

#### Interpreter details:

R 4.4.0

## Describe the issue:
When deploying a single document to Posit Connect an `renv.lock` is a hard requirement with Posit Publisher. The renv.lock file is folder/repo/project specific, and as such a `renv::init()` function call will create a package list based on all the files within the project folder. That means if a project folder includes any more code than the single document file you want to schedule on Posit Connect, the `renv.lock` will bake in all packages required to run all documents within that folder. This goes in direct contradiction to modern, modular software principles. 

Essentially, the renv requirement means I can't store analysis code that loads the `tidyverse` within the same project folder as scripts for deployment on Posit Connect unless I want all documents that I deploy from that folder to have to install the tidyverse on deployment. This leads to massive bloat being baked in to the default workflow. 

Of course, it is possible to create multiple folders within each project, where each folder only contains the .Rmd to be published and a corresponding `renv.lock` file. But that seems rather non-sensical when an alternative default (mimicking that of publishing in the RStudio IDE) is possible. And my current "workaround" of doing the work in Positron but then opening the RStudio IDE to publish my documents to Connect, isn't great either. The appeal of Posit Connect / RStudio Connect has been the effort put into making it super low-friction to have code running in production while working within your regular data science project workflow. A large part of that is the environment management magic done by Posit Connect, so I feel like this is a super important feature, so that Positron doesn't miss out on that magic that you can still get in the RStudio IDE.

## Steps to reproduce the issue:

<!-- For example, are you using a Jupyter notebook, R script, Quarto document, etc? -->

Press "Deploy Your Project" without having run `renv:init` and you will be greeted with the following error.

```Project requires renv initialization "renv::init()" to be deployed.```


## Expected or desired behavior:

On the `renv` website, on the [Using renv with Posit Connect](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/rsconnect.html) page (which is also the [rsconnect.Rmd](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/vignettes/rsconnect.Rmd) vignette within the `renv` package) it states the following. 

> RStudio Connect uses [packrat](https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/) to restore project environments on the RStudio Connect server. This should have no impact on how the user develops content for RStudio Connect. It is not necessary for the user to use packrat instead of renv when developing content, as the environment management tool used locally has no impact on the tools RStudio Connect uses for environment management. Therefore, there should be no concerns with using renv to develop content that will be deployed to RStudio Connect.

Emphasis on: _**"Therefore, there should be no concerns with using renv to develop content that will be deployed to RStudio Connect."**_

## Were there any error messages in the UI, Output panel, or Developer Tools console?

<!--

- Open the Developer Tools console by running the `Developer: Toggle Developer Tools` command from the Command Palette
- Open the relevant Output Channel logs by utilizing this guide: https://positron.posit.co/troubleshooting.html

-->

UI:
```Project requires renv initialization "renv::init()" to be deployed.```

title: Add schema support for newer Connect Python, Quarto, and R version matching specifiers
description:
## Description

Connect now supports version matching specifiers in the manifest.json However, Publisher does not appear to utilize data from an existing manifest.json if present. There does not appear to be a documented way to present this specific data in the existing [Publisher deployment configuration](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/docs/configuration.md).

This was discovered while attempting deployment of [connect-extensions](https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-extensions) which have been heavily utilizing these new version specifiers.

[Posit Connect 2025.05.0](https://docs.posit.co/connect/news/#posit-connect-2025.05.0)
- Publishers can set version specifiers for Quarto in the manifest.json under environment.quarto.requires (e.g., “>=1.2.0, <2.0.0”). If this field is set, it takes precedence over the Quarto.VersionMatching configuration setting (i.e., nearest, major-minor, and exact). (https://github.com/posit-dev/connect/issues/31234)

[Posit Connect 2025.03.0](https://docs.posit.co/connect/news/#posit-connect-2025.03.0)
- Publishers can set version specifiers (e.g., “>=3.8, <4”) for both R and Python in the manifest.json under environment.r.requires and environment.python.requires, respectively. If these fields are set, they take precedence over the Connect version matching strategies (i.e., nearest, major-minor, and exact). (https://github.com/posit-dev/connect/issues/30062, #30063)

## Problem Statement

I have a project that I've configured to run in R 4.3.3 in positron (though 4.5.0 is on my path as the default). In some portions of the logs, we detect 4.3.3 correctly, but in others (and critically when we call `renv::status()` and then block deploying if that's not clean), we are detecting 4.5.0 and so getting the library(s) wrong and incorrectly saying that there's a package mismatch.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use an interpreter in Positron that is different from the default path. 

And as a note if anyone else is running into this: I ran `rig default 4.3-arm64` to get make that 4.3.3 executable on my path, and that let the deploy go through just fine.

title: Implement flags for targeting an execution environment during deployment
description:
Connect 2025.04 allows setting `environment.identifier` in the bundle's `manifest.json`. This new field allows the content to target a specific execution environment when running on Connect. The existing `environment.image` field remains unchanged however the semantics are slightly different. An `image` selection is now treated the same as any other piece of matching criteria. Connect will choose _any_ execution environment that uses the specified container image.

If not already supported, then we should also ensure that users can set both `app.default_image_name` and `app.default_environment_guid` on the app record from the deployment configuration.

see also: 
- https://github.com/posit-dev/rsconnect-python/issues/652
- https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/issues/1147

'C:\Program' n’est pas reconnu en tant que commande interne
ou externe, un programme exécutable ou un fichier de commandes.

title: Limit impact of R & Python dependency detection to those content types for which it applies.
description:
Our behavior in a multi-type project directory (in which all of the publisher's project files exist in a single subdirectory hiearchy) can lead to some incorrect dependency detection.

The example here is a combination of a python and static-html project. The inspection done for the static-html file, will detect an inaccurate dependency on python, if the developer has created a `requirements.txt` file in that subdirectory. It would likewise also incorrectly detect an R dependency if a file named `renv.lock` was present.

Currently, the inspect functionality does content specific dependency detection, and then falls through a generic check for these two dependency files, adding an R or a Python dependency if they are found. This occurs for all content types, which is incorrect.

To fix this, we need to limit this generic check to only apply to a subset of content types, where R or Python dependencies make sense.

-----

Analysis of issue reported from Tareef:

I had a chance to talk with Tareef and have him show me how he got into the state he did. I now understand it to be a bit different than what was discussed before:

- He was using a single subdirectory with multiple types of projects within it, similar (but different) to our mixed content test case. Within this subdirectory, he had both a Python project and a Quarto project, which he used to output a single HTML page.
- He selected to deploy from his generated HTML file.
- Our inspection correctly created a deployment w/ content type of html,  but incorrectly identified an implicit dependency on Python because his multi-type project subdirectory contained a requirements.txt from his python api app. 
Deploying the project ran into issues during the deployment process w/ Connect. I’m not sure what happened there, but I’m pretty confident it can be reproduced.

I believe the workaround for him is to remove the [python] section from the config file, which will remove the Python dependency and redeploy the project to Connect. (He didn’t get a chance to try this because he wants to actually publish the project as a Quarto project, which would be re-run on a schedule. I’ll update the issue as I try to reproduce it.)

We are currently using `eventsource` `2.0.2` in the extension and homeView code. `3+` is available, but it has breaking changes mentioned in the release: https://github.com/EventSource/eventsource/releases/tag/v3.0.0

This may require some code changes to upgrade.

There is [a migration guide](https://github.com/EventSource/eventsource/blob/main/MIGRATION.md#v2-to-v3).

title: Correctly error when missing required files from bundle
description:
Currently we do not have helpful errors aside from when the `Config.Python.PackageFile` file is missing from the included files list, and that one contains a bug: #2563.

A improvement can be made here. One potential option is to insert the checks in between the create and upload bundle operations in `internal/publish/bundle.go`.

We can utilize the files list inside of the `manifest` and the Config inside of the `defaultPublisher` state to check if the package files, and the entrypoint are included with a helpful error.

## Related Issues

- #1503 
- #1493 
- #2563 (see sub-issues list)

title: Help the user with `renv` issues also from the R packages section
description:
As a follow up to #2543, we should as well help the user from the "R packages" section.

Some latest work on this provides the user with actionable items when attempting to deploy and not having a `lockfile` halts the deployment.

In a similar way, it is possible to have a separate API endpoint that uses the same code already created to evaluate the current `renv` status and report to the "R packages" section if there is something that can be done.

title: Content creation requests happening before pre-flight checks
description: When the following conditions met: 1. Already have credentials registered in Publisher 2. Connect is down or unreachable 3. We already had a nice message but some changes [in commit e162drc](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/commit/e162d4cde56e64931666adddd7253a46dc21c4ba#diff-ce7057dc498c6d64ab8893ac812c640bfd801aa1e0dff85792a9ee9e6a294aeb) changed a bit the order of operations for pre-flight checks. **Previous message shown (the desired message)** **Current message being displayed**

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/a7429cb6124bc786dfabd1d6faa8a3cac7c9b8a7/internal/clients/connect/capabilities.go#L45

The work around currently is to include the package file with `/requirements.txt` for example.

title: Use `.gitattributes` to hide the deployment record in diffs
description:
A `.gitattributes` file has the ability to collapse diffs in GitHub and GitLab when the diff is generated and not really necessary to review. This is common with files like `package-lock.json`.

We can utilize this to help with the generated deployment record file when users use git.

References:
- [Customizing how changed files appear on GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-files/customizing-how-changed-files-appear-on-github)
- [Collapse generated files](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/merge_requests/changes.html#collapse-generated-files)

title: Providing a `type` that isn't mapped in `connectContentTypeMap` sends empty `appMode`
description:
As we learned in https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2476#issuecomment-2605451591 when providing a `type` in the Configuration file that isn't in `connectContentTypeMap` the manifest sent to Connect [provides `""`](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/0b43655aba2281ba17aee425ef39b59a98abb330/internal/clients/connect/apptypes.go#L281) (as it is the `UnknownMode`).

In an effort to better support Publisher working when Connect updates without code changes the `appMode` should be sent using the provided `type` string in the Configuration file rather than falling back to `""` if it is unrecognized.

Reference:

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/0b43655aba2281ba17aee425ef39b59a98abb330/internal/clients/connect/apptypes.go#L258

title: Add descriptions of what versions of R, Python, and Quarto were used during the deployment to the Publisher Log view
description:
Captured from discussion w/ Katie...

The Publisher log should show what versions of the interpreters were used to deploy a project to Connect. The request was to show all three interpreters and indicate if they were a dependency of the deployment as well as the versions being requested in the generated deployment manifest file.

The use case was for a project that had Quarto, R, and Python. Originally, it only had Quarto and R. As the user expanded it to also use Python, their deployments were not successful. In the end, the user saw no indication from the Publisher UX that Python was not configured as part of the project. They were also trying, ahead of adding Python to the project, to use a specific version of Python. 

The user felt there should be better feedback and breadcrumbs around the experience to support self-diagnostics. They suggested that if the publisher log had included some indication of each interpreter's usage and version, then they would have been more self-sufficient in her ability to resolve her issue.

This issue becomes more needed when the versions are not auto-populated into the config file:
- https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2468

title: Accept unknown keys in configurations to pass to the manifest
description:
In an effort to avoiding _always_ needing to make adjustments to Publisher's code and schema to support new Connect features we should allow configurations to accept unknown key value pairs and pass them to the manifest. This will address the question raised in #2510.

Key value pairs in specific sections should be passed to the section they are part of. For example: `python.some_key` should be part of the Python section of the Manifest when it is constructed.

**Trade-offs**
- We will lose the "The selected Configuration has a schema error on line..." warning in the sidebar when an unknown key is used.
- Typos for known, optional keys will no longer show a warning. For example: a user could type `alow_uv` instead of `allow_uv`. The Publisher will have to rely on Connect for any user assistance to understand discrepancies between what is expected and what occurred due to typos like this.

Note: Unknown keys are ignored by Connect servers so supplying configurations with unknown keys will have no effect.

More context for this issue can be found in this Slack thread: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1736434807194889

title: Implement rExecutable discovery to prefer the active version of R within the IDE rather than path
description:
The code needs to identify the same version of R that the users have configured. This is passed in from the extension, but the backend code does not use this value consistently. To solve this, we need to make sure the correct path is identified, following our rules:
 
1. Use the passed-in path for the R interpreter if supplied. It must exist and be validated)
    - If it doesn't exist, fall through to the next option
    - If it does exist but is not a valid R interpreter (use `--version` output to validate), then return an error
 2. Use the first R executable found on PATH; it must exist and be validated.
    - If not valid or doesn't exist, return an error

Once the interpreter is identified, it should be used for creating/retrieving the lock file.

title: Provide ability to re-inspect a project interpreter dependencies
description:
Much of our configuration is based on an initial inspection of the files surrounding the entrypoint file, captured at the time a deployment is created and is not refreshed as changes are made. 

Our assumption within the publisher is that the project is fairly complete, and the user won’t be modifying it much. But the reality is that if they are iterating on it, for example, adding a Python section into their Quarto document, which wasn’t originally there, then we really need the option to detect that requirement and update the configuration and manifest as the updated project is deployed. Right now, we’d continue to deploy it without the Python dependency, and the Quarto doc would never run successfully on Connect.

For example, if the content type does not specifically indicate that R is required, we will not indicate a dependency on it if there is no `renv.lock` file. It seems reasonable that a re-inspect might be useful as the user works on the project, adding functionality. In our current implementation, a user must create a new deployment or manually update the existing configuration. (They could also create a new deployment just to get the config file and then swap the config file to be used with the deployment... but that is pretty complex for a normal workflow.)

I could see us taking a position that we’ll move (or at least re-analyze) the “needsR” and “needsPython” logic, currently done as part of the initial inspection process that creates the config when the user initiates a deployment.

The only way we have to work around this is to suggest that the user create a new deployment, which would perform a new inspection and create a new configuration file. They could then assign the configuration file to the existing deployment or move to a new deployment on the server with the new config/deployment files. The workflow for this common scenario is not great.

title: Update manifest.json Quarto version population
description:
We should update how we decide which Quarto version we specify for running on Connect. This work would update the `Quarto.version` field in the config to be optional, and document what it means to set it. This should also update how we build the `manifest.json` accordingly:

1. From the `Quarto.version` in the config, if set (this field is now optional)
2. From the current active version of Quarto in the IDE, if the `Quarto.version` is not set in config

The answer to this should populate the `quarto.version` field in the `manifest.json`, when we build it.

title: Update manifest.json Python version population
description:
We should update how we decide which Python version we specify for running on Connect. This work would update the the Python.version field in the config to be optional, and document what it means to set it. This should also update how we build the manifest.json accordingly:

From the Python.version in the config, if set (this field is now optional)
From the current active version of Python in the IDE, if the Python.version is not set in config
The answer to this should populate the`python.version` field in the manifest.json, when we build it.

Note that this doesn't lean on the .python-version file written by pyenv ([docs](https://realpython.com/intro-to-pyenv/#specifying-your-python-version)). If we tackle that change, it will be in a follow-on issue.

title: Update manifest.json R version population
description:
We should update how we decide which R version we specify for running on Connect. This work would update the the `R.version` field in the config to be optional, and document what it means to set it. This should also update how we build the `manifest.json` accordingly:

1. From the `R.version` in the config, if set (this field is now optional)
2. From the current active version of R in the IDE, if the `R.version` is not set in config

The answer to this should populate the `platform` field in the `manifest.json`, when we build it.

Note that this doesn't lean on the R version defined in `renv.lock`, which, ultimately, we may want to do. If we tackle that change, it will be in a follow-on issue.

-----

After analyzing feedback from the original PR that was created to address this issue (https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2568), we've decided that the alternative design which was informally discussed would be a better direction to go in.

With the implementation of default values, for R and Python, derived from the active interpreters at the time of deployment, the challenge has been how to keep the concept of a default wanted vs. a locked-in (supplied) value within the extension UX, which depends on values for these fields.

The attributes / responsibility of this alternative design would involve maintaining the internal representation of the configuration objects as they are represented on disk, with the addition of default value fields. The deployment process (in the agent) would be responsible for resolving the defaults, at the time needed when generating the maniftest. The extension UX would be responsible for converting the configuration objects queried from the agent w/ the active "expected" default values. 

Current thoughts on this path: the configuration object can can be extended to include default values inserted during transit. This would maintain being able to identify the difference, but would make the users of this field responsible for looking possibly at both values. (However, this can be done within the existing store, with an explicit computed value.)

title: Project Files checkbox can be inaccurate when collapsing and expanding directories
description:
If the Files API takes awhile due to a very large directory size, and the user clicks a checkbox to include/exclude a item; the checkbox could be inaccurate when the parent directory is then collapsed and re-expanded.

This is due to the item being removed then re-added to the DOM upon collapsing and expanding. We do not store a local state of included/excluded files and instead rely on the API response. This reliance also explains why including/excluding a directory does not change nested files until we hear back from the Files API.

Ideally the expanded state of a directory shouldn't affect the checkbox state prior to the hearing back from the Files API.

This issue does not include handling nested files when a directory is included in the deployment.

title: Update R Inspection to use active R version to populate inspect results rather than renv.lock version
description:
The publisher agent currently populates the `R.version` configuration field with the version found within the `renv.lock` file if it exists. This version is used to target the runtime R version used on Connect.

When a user creates a deployment for a project where the active R version being used within the IDE (VS Code or Positron) matches the version found  in `renv.lock`, all is well.

However, when a user who has configured a specific version of R to be used within VS Code or Positron (which can affect all of the visible and background R processes run within VS Code or Positron), starts interacting with a project who's `renv.lock` file is different, then we are setting up a scenario in which the intended remote execution may not operate as expected. 

To expand upon this scenario, let's suppose that the `renv.lock` file was last used with R version `4.3.3`, but the user has configured their IDE (VS Code or Positron) to use R version `4.4.2`. In this environment, when the user launches an R console, it will be run using the R Version configured (in this case, `4.4.2`). Operations will be run within that environment, including package installation and removal. `renv` will operate in that environment and will detect that having a `renv.lock` file of `4.3.3` but an active running R version of `4.4.2` is an environment which is considered "out-of-sync". `renv` operations will attempt to update the lock file to the same version as the running R console. In almost all cases, to get a successful deployment, the user will migrate the `renv.lock` file to version `4.4.2`.

In addition, the behavior of the Posit publisher will be to use the active version of R to populate the package details needed in the manifest every time the project is deployed. So unless it is caught, package versions of the dependent packages, valid for the active version of R within the IDE, will be used for a runtime time environment on the server that is matched against the incorrect version originally found in the `renv.lock` (`4.3.3`) during inspection. While this might work sometimes, it is not a close representation of the working environment of `4.4.2` running within the IDE.

This issue can easily be fixed by simply eliminating the agent code which attempts to populate the version found in the `renv.lock` file. When a version could not be found (or the `renv.lock` file did not exist), the code already drops down into using the active version of R for the IDE. If not set through an extension, it will fall through and use the first R interpreter it can find on PATH.

description:

title: Reconsider R Package Scan button
description:
We ended up removing the R Package Scan button due to this bug:

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/2403

Further discussion here:
https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1729259573066909

It would be nice to have a button that configures renv for users but the original implementation seemed to only add functionality if the user already had an `renv/activate.R` with either no `renv.lock` or a `renv.lock` file with missing or mismatched packages to the `renv/library`. title: Unable to point deployment to a different content GUID
description:
If the `update previous deployment` option is selected, and that flow followed, the pre-deployment will now be pointing to that content GUID.

However, if the wrong URL / GUID is provided, there is no way to re-run the `update previous deployment` flow to select a new location to deploy.

If a deploy is done it may error due to a different content-type, but if the content type is the same it may override the content as expected.

---

The workaround here is to create a new deployment.

It may be intentional behavior to not allow a deployment pointing to a Content GUID to not re-directed to a different Content GUID. We will need to decide that when picking up this issue.

title: Remove deploy disable state if a deploy is in progress
Remove deploy disable state if configuration is in error
Remove disable states for the Deploy button
description:
We currently have 3 disabled states for the Deploy button in the extension:
1. Resources haven't been selected
2. The selected Configuration is in error
3. There is currently a deploy in progress

---

### 1. Resources haven't been selected

We do not show the deploy button at all when a Content Record has not been selected.

The deploy button is shown if we have a record selected, but can still be disabled in the two possible states past that:
- the user doesn't have a Credential for the Content Record
- the user doesn't have a Configuration for the Content Record

For both states we show warnings to solve this easily.

We cannot easily remove this since the deploy API in our Go binary requires we pass the name of the both the `account` (Credential) and the name of the Configuration.

A decent amount of refactoring could remove the need of requiring a Credential in that API call since it can be derived. Credentials are unique to server URLs and we can attempt to find that Credential during the deploy process and fail if it is not found. This is how the extension is determining the "selected Credential" despite the user never making that selection explicit:

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/7edfbcb66d5a49cd4dff74bf559a00c74f32cf27/extensions/vscode/webviews/homeView/src/stores/home.ts#L93

Removal of the Configuration disabled state could be done in much the same way. We can rely on the selected Content Record to point to a Configuration since that is how we determine the selection in the extension:

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/7edfbcb66d5a49cd4dff74bf559a00c74f32cf27/extensions/vscode/webviews/homeView/src/stores/home.ts#L41

The path forward to remove these disabled states would be to refactor the `POST /api//deployments/$NAME` to not take a `account` (Credential) or `config` and derive them on the Go side.

This would free up the extension to always deploy when a selection of a Content Record is made, and allow errors to bubble up with the derivation goes wrong.

---

### 2. Selected Configuration is in error

We can make the deploy API call to our binary just fine with a Configuration in error since we still have the name of the Configuration. 

It will not ever successfully deploy since we validate the TOML file before sending anything up to Connect: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/7830e62c2bfe119d8d47c3dcc9dce19bacef5371/internal/schema/schema.go#L83

This validation is necessary to get the attributes from a Configuration, but:
- we can allow the pressing of `Deploy`
- the user can get an informative error from our `ValidateTOMLFile` function

That looks like the below, when the notification is expanded:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daf80685-71c8-4ea8-9c57-b87a4e92ac05)

---

### 3. Deploy in progress

Allowing for deploy while another is in progress is possible, but leads to some odd states.

First it allows users to accidentally double click the button sending up two deploys. We would have to introduce some sort of debouncing or something else to avoid this.

Second we start to get errors where builds failed due to being superseded by a more recent deployment.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea447563-6bac-4b2f-b3af-9bfa1eeb096b)

There are questions about how we handle this in our current UX when it comes to logging. Currently our Posit Publisher Logs only track the latest deployment. If multiple deployments are going at once you are either:
- only seeing the logs for the most recent
- seeing multiple logs at once (multiple steps in progress) if you are deploying multiple of the same content ID twice

Even if we get into a bad state where `publishInProgress` remains `true` (for example a Deployment gets stuck) there are few options forward:
- cancelling the in progress deployment - a feature we added in #2057 
- or ultimately reloading / re-opening the VS Code window to reset the state

This will require more thought on how to approach removing this disable state.

title: Import: When deploying to a mismatching content type, metadata is updated but deployment fails
description:
As a test I tried to deploy a bokeh app targeting an already-deployed fastapi app on the dogfood server.

1. The Deployment Status briefly shows the deployment succeeded and then flips to failure:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad257b4a-76d2-448c-8e55-32d9e91a5818

2. The title (and other metadata included in the configuration file) for the content on Connect was updated even though the deployment failed.


I would expect this to fail earlier so we don't update the content on Connect.  Can we detect what target content type is before we even start the deployment? I think we're making the api calls on Connect to update the metadata before the call to do the deployment.  Maybe these should be in the reverse order?

STR:
* Deploy a fastapi app to Connect
* Now deploy a bokeh app using the new `update that previous deployment` link and point to the previous app URL
* I'm allowed to deploy the app
* The Deployment shows Success briefly but then displays the Failure
* The target app's metadata was updated even though the deployment failed.

Expected:
I would expect...
* that we detect a mismatching content type prior to the deployment
OR
* the deployment fails, never shows a success message and the metadata to remain unupdated

title: Exclude sample content from dependabot
Secrets: UX confusion
description: I was a bit confused while testing the Secrets UI. I now understand how to use it, but it did require some tinkering and more advanced configuration usage that we haven't yet introduced. Here are some things I ran into. I'm filing this as an enhancement because these aren't really "bugs" as I think it's working as-designed. 1. nit: the clear button is loaded and active even when there are no secrets to clear: 2. UX: it's not clear _how_ to add a secret. I expected there to be an add button to create one from the UI. This differs from something like `title` because we include `title` in the config by default so users know they can update that. `secrets` are not included and it's also unclear that it takes an array. I think first-time users will have a hard time understanding how to use this feature. Maybe since this is more of a code-first element, we should add an example to the config via a commented out secrets field? 3. When I _do_ add the secret to the configuration file, it's not clear that I then have to edit it to add a value. The edit pencil only appears when you hover over the newly created Secret. My initial thought, is by clicking the edit pencil, it would prompt me to update the title rather than add a value. 4. After I populate my configuration with an array of Secrets, I can click the Clear icon, but I expected it to clear the actual Secrets rather than the values. I think most of the confusion at first blush is due to the field operating differently than other fields available in the interface. The other fields allow interaction with the configuration file, but this is a step in "code-first" that we haven't yet introduced. For example, the Title is created in the UI and adds it to the configuration file. The Project files can be added/removed from the configuration via the UX. Whereas the Secrets field forces the user to first add the secret to the configuration file and any subsequent UI interaction updates the configuration file.

title: Update to go 1.23.1
Agent encountering/responding with Error Code 500 while refreshing files associated with configuration file
description:
From slack thread: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1726068297152959

This might be something specific to my environment, but while editing files in Emacs, the publisher was constantly trying to refresh the project and sometimes produced errors like the following, which are temporary files used while in-flight edits are being performed. I received several of these errors:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28442edd-3d81-4a0b-bc38-86e3beb5b6bd)

Q> How can I get these refresh errors to stop? They are happening even while the publisher view is not open. Do I need to remove the extension?

Unfortunately, there is no specific way to disable them. We rely on them for a large amount of functionality, so a bug in this area is not very mitigable. Without uninstalling the extension, you could disable it (and then enable it back when you want to try its functionality). Otherwise, you could uninstall it until we resolve that issue.

Q> OK. I’ll disable for now. I didn’t expect it to be doing background things while not thinking about publishing.

Looking closer at the error code, it is your symlink `.#bug.py` that is giving the agent problems. This is a good bug and one which we hadn’t seen before. Thanks!
It is an interesting comment to consider: “I didn’t expect it to be doing background things while not thinking about publishing.“. As an extension, part of our functionality is loaded immediately by VSCode, ahead of our activation of our UX. The background functionality supports the command pallet commands and our file-specific entrypoint detection. We have taken a simple path to start with, but could certainly be much more thoughtful about what happens ahead of showing the UX.

title: Quarto Website not deploying as expected
description:
## Update (while trying to reproduce)

While trying to reproduce this issue, found that the work for enabling Quarto scripts (#2424) also helped on Quarto websites, with a couple items still requiring work:
1. Pre and Post render scripts are not automatically picked up to be added to the configuration on project inspection
2. Users selecting `_quarto.yml` as entrypoint would get an undesired outcome (`unknown` type project). This because `quarto inspect` does not work on `_quarto.yml` files but it is understandable that the user picks that file and by doing so the project type is explicit enough already.

## Original

From: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1726064950810009

I have a Quarto website project. I don’t really understand what needs to be considered the “entrypoint” in this context. I’m given my *.qmd files, my *.py pre-render script, and one rendered HTML file, but the _quarto.yml file (which is the closest option in my mental model) isn’t offered.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e89fc199-49f6-4061-ad65-06655cf6c7cf)

I want to deploy this project as source (not rendered) and include the files:
- _quarto.yml
- requirements.txt
- index.qmd, visualize-r.qmd, visualize-py.qmd
- allocation.py
This project has both R and Python package requirements.

Proceeding with the deployment workflow, it missed the pre-render allocation.py script and did not identify that the project requires R as well as Python.
The Quarto inspect output DOES say that knitr is used:
```
  "engines": [
    "jupyter",
    "markdown",
    "knitr"
  ],
```

I tried to guess about the [r] syntax:
```
[r]
version = '4.3.3'
```

 I got an ugly error (attached).
The TOML was updated with placeholders which also violated the configuration:
```
[r]
version = '4.3.3'
package_file = ''
package_manager = ''
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1b647b9-321f-4986-a518-ea2e4cdba9ef)

I tried to `package_manager = 'none'` and got a complaint when trying to deploy; I was trying to use my standard library, not renv.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bcee1db-469f-4dbc-96c1-8f2cc6c11b74)

:cry: The deployed manifest does not indicate that Quarto needs the knitr engine and therefore does not cause Connect to install R packages.

```
	"quarto": {
		"version": "1.5.57",
		"engines": [
			"jupyter",
			"markdown"
		]
	},
```

For those following along, I was able to successfully deploy with:
```
rsconnect::deployApp(server = "rsc.radixu.com", account = "aron", python = file.path(getwd(), "env/bin/python"))
```

This one is a little awkward because it doesn’t use reticulate. Instead, it uses both the knitr and jupyter engines. rsconnect could do better at detecting the need for Python in this situation.

Note: I still have `package_manager = 'none'` but renv was required.

See slack link for archive of project, created with:
```
tar cf mixed.tar --exclude mixed/_site --exclude mixed/env --exclude mixed/renv/library --exclude mixed/.quarto mixed
```

My Python virtual env was in `env`.

Consider having the backend API return JSON on error
description:
Currently we don't send back JSON. We should be returning clean error messages for failure modes. We return specific HTTP codes, but we can be more descriptive with the errors.

All of the responses right now return plaintext responses. Synk does not like when we respond with part of the request in the response, or we can pack an error in JSON.

This is a single file change to change how we pack those errors into the responses.

title: In Python when using a route that's not `app` it fails on Connect
description:
We don't offer a way for the user to set a route in the config file for python apps.  Though it's common to use `app` as the route, in practice a user can set it to whatever they'd like.  

In Connect if a user decided to use a different route, this error is thrown:

> Error while loading Python API: Failed to find an application object (('app', 'application')) or factory function (('create_app', 'make_app')) in module 'app'. You can specify a different entrypoint in the manifest.json file or on the rsconnect-python command line.

We should probably update Connect to throw a new error but also should allow the user to add `route` to the config file.  I think it should be included by default with `app` as the default route.

To reproduce, just change all `app` references to another string in the fastapi-simple app.

title: Create new API which will return both deployments and configurations with one call
description:
This will help optimize the directory scans required for recursive calls.

What we are looking for is that the active configuration that is named within the deployment file be returned with the deployment file.

Since the UX currently always shows data from the configuration file when it displays deployment information, the UX is always calling both of these. It will call them either for a single instance pair or will call them both with the recursive option. The current logic is to retrieve all deployments and retrieve all configurations, but we don't use any of the configurations from this large query except the ones that are named within the deployments.

Perhaps a modification to the GET deployments API, with an option to include the active configuration file as well?

While the UX could eliminate the recursive configurations query, it would have to make a large number of individual configuration API requests instead. We don't know the threshold of when this would be more efficient than recursively requesting all configurations, but since most users will only have a one-to-one relationship of configs to deployments, we think this option wouldn't buy us much (and could actually be slower with the API calling overhead).

title: Add more debug logging in the backend
Move all views into the Home webview
Include attributes for directories in files API if all nested files are included or excluded
description:
For the hierarchical tree view with checkboxes we want to have the folders in the tree view to have an [indeterminate state](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#indeterminate_state_checkboxes) so the three states are:

- Checked if all nested files are included
- Unchecked if all nested files are excluded
- Indeterminate if some nested files are included and some are excluded

To do this we can include attributes if all files are included and another if all files are excluded.

We could collapse these into a single attribute with different enum states as well. As long as we can determine the three states above.

Can we catch that error and throw an error about an invalid configuration file?

title: When redeployment fails we can no longer update existing deployment
description:
I have an existing successfully deployment. If I change my Python version to an invalid one and re-deploy, all Deployment history is lost and I can no longer update my deployment on the server.

STR:
* Create a deployment with a Python app
* Once it succeeds, update the config with an invalid Python version
* Redeploy so a failure occurs

The deployment history is cleared and I now have no way to update the existing deployment.  This seems to occur with any failure.

This instead should keep the Deployment history and allow me to update the existing deployment.

Example:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b7e97d8-7a6c-401e-ac15-fdfa549848d8

title: Bug: File initiated publish not always selecting or recognizing matching deployment
description:
To reproduce:

- Open `connect-content` in VSCode
- activate the Publisher Extension
- Create new deployment with `stock-api-python/app.py` as entrypoint and confirm that the new deployment is selected
- Open `stock-api-python/app.py`
- Click on publish icon for `app.py` file
- BUG: Creates a new deployment
- EXPECTED: Publishes the deployment that was created above
- Create a new deployment for one of the other projects in the repo and confirm that the new deployment is selected
- Click on publish icon for `app.py` file
- BUG: starts deploying, but Deployment selector shows "Select..."
- EXPECTED: the deployment selector is updated to show active deployment

title: Dependency scanning cannot reliably choose packages with different module names
description:
For example:

[`python-dotenv`](https://pypi.org/project/python-dotenv/) has an import like:

```python
from dotenv import load_dotenv
```

and our scan will conclude that the package that should be included in the `requirements.txt` file is `dotenv`.

However the package name itself is `python-dotenv` and [`dotenv`](https://pypi.org/project/dotenv/) is a totally different package.

title: Windows: After a deployment the `A` in Project Files remain for all subdirectory files
description:
After a deployment in Windows, the `A` indicating a new file being added to a Deployment is removed for all files except for those in a subdirectory so it appears all files in a subdirectory are new for subsequent deployments.

This only happens in Windows.


![Screenshot 2024-08-14 103221](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af76ccd0-7c12-4bb4-8b94-8894d33f64a2)

title: Feedback: Move "New" action to top of quick input list choices
description:
We've had internal feedback that having the entry for a "new" config or deployment can be lost at the end, so it should be shown first.

If we do this, we should probably also fix up the consistency with the separators, to include the new / existing within the select configurations quick input list.

PR is already available for this change, creating this issue to collect team feedback. (https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/2111)

title: Bug: API failures when deleting .venv directory - So many API Calls!

title: Eliminate the recursive query required to determine if we have any deployments configured

Let's discuss switching the interface to simply showing something like `Add or Select Deployment`, and updating the deployment selector to also allow a new deployment choice.

description: Put together a brief requirements doc and design propsal for a minimal secrets implementation and review with the team.

title: Requirements scanning detects local imports as package dependencies
description:
If you scan for Python dependencies and your code imports from another local Python file, that will be wrongly detected as a package dependency.

For example, in app.py:
```
from data import get_data
```

in data.py:
```
def get_data(): ...
```

When scanning, we need to see that `data` is a project-local import and not from an installed package.

title: Use file in home directory for a persistent credential in Workbench
description:

We need something persistent that we can fetch when the API call occurs so we are going to have a file to store credentials when there is no keyring to access.

title: Open or activate the appropriate config file when file UX is used to include/exclude files
Add a limit to quick inspection file enumeration, and provide file explorer picker to use when file limits are hit.
description: Add a `limit` parameter to the /api/entrypoints endpoint, and also have it accept the list of open files. Scan the entire tree (as we currently do), and sort preferred / more likely entrypoints to the top of the list before applying the limit. Use th open files and the conept of "preferred filenames" to do the sorting.

title: Files: traverse subdirectories to find included files
description:
The file walker doesn't visit subdirectories unless there's a matching file pattern to include them. But a pattern might match something within the directory, and we won't know until we look.

For example:
```
files = ['dashboard.qmd', 'responses.csv', '_extensions/jmbuhr/qrcode/_extension.yml', '_extensions/jmbuhr/qrcode/assets/qrcode.js', '_extensions/jmbuhr/qrcode/qrcode.lua']
```
will not include any of the files under `_extensions`.

title: Support credential provided through environment variables
description:
To provide initial support for Workbench, we have decided to support the specification of a server credential via environment variables. These are:

CONNECT_SERVER: the URL of the server
CONNECT_API_KEY: the ApliKey for the publisher
CONNECT_SERVER_NAME: <optional> the nickname of the server. If not specified, use the hostname of the server URL.

Do not allow the deletion of a credential specified via the environment variables.

Do not allow overlap of URL or Name with other credentials.

title: Inspection fails on empty `.ipynb` file with 500 status code

annotated-types==0.7.0

anyio==4.4.0
    # via

```

- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv

title: Support a list of known Connect URLs for credential creation
description:
From internal slack conversation: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C06B0UZKT34/p1721311828064789

**Query:**

Workbench has a feature where admins [can set the default Connect server for RStudio sessions](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/rstudio_pro_sessions/rstudio_connect_server.html), but (a) many customers have more than one Connect instance in practice; and (b) this doesn't work for other editors, especially VS Code and soon Positron
we'd like to fix this and make it possible for admins to supply a set of known Connect URLs for VS Code & Positron sessions that would get picked up by the Publisher automatically -- how would y'all like to receive those URLs? config file? environment variable?

Alternatively maybe we could have the Workbench VS Code extension communicate something to the Publisher extension?

**Response:**

It would probably be best if the publisher extension query the workbench extension api for this info when it needs it. We do that for other values across the Position extensions.
If I am understanding correctly, this would be the URLs only and the user would still need to supply their own api key for that server? (confirmed)

------------------------------

Internal discussion:
- Perhaps supporting environment variables as well would be nice, to help customers establish the Connect Server URLs even when they do not have workbench (although we need to acknowledge there are complications of environment variable visibility for launched programs.)

description:
We got this from slack:

When you add the `palm` url (https://pub.palm.ptd.posit.it/) the following error is thrown:

Based on the logs, it looks like we're having trouble parsing the response:

> time=2024-07-16T15:11:34.781-04:00 level=INFO msg="Testing authentication" method="Connect API key" url=https://pub.palm.ptd.posit.it/connect/
> time=2024-07-16T15:11:35.654-04:00 level=DEBUG msg="API request" method=GET path=/__api__/v1/user body="" response="<!DOCTYPE html>\n<!--[if IE 7]><html lang=\"en\" class=\"lt-ie10 lt-ie9 lt-ie8\"><![endif]-->\n<!--[if IE 8]><html lang=\"en\" class=\"lt-ie10 lt-ie9\"> <![endif]-->\n<!--[if IE 9]><html lang=\"en\" class=\"lt-ie10\"><![endif]-->\n<!--[if gt IE 9]><html lang=\"en\"><![endif]-->\n<!--[if !IE]><!--><html lang=\"en\"><!--<![endif]-->\n<head>\n    <meta charset=\"UTF-8\">\n\n    <script type=\"text/javascript\" nonce=\"32Zh1d1fB6Icnylb6KyWqA\">if (typeof module === 'object') {window.module = module; module = undefined;}</script><style type=\"text/css\" nonce=\"32Zh1d1fB6Icnylb6KyWqA\">\n

When we _can_ successfully add a Server we hit (dogfood for reference):

> time=2024-07-16T15:18:37.180-04:00 level=INFO msg="Testing authentication" method="Connect API key" url=https://rsc.radixu.com

> We let certain things through (from history): X-Auth-Token header is present (for IDE access), or Authorization: Key * header for API requests.

title: Optimize recursive scans for large subdirectories

Our operations seem to be taking a long time to update the UX, and this is probably due to the scans. (Only difference between acceptable, near instant response time with a smaller folder hierarchy vs. a large one.)

I would guess that there are some places where the refresh is not taking into account the projectDir, when understanding where to start.

We could also greatly improve this by reducing the number of parallel API calls we are doing since the extension does not have a single store of data.

You can also see that several refreshes are called multiple times very quickly.

title: Use configured R interpreter from VSCode R extension
description:
The VSCode R extension does not appear to allow dynamic selection of which version of R. By default, it uses what is on the path but they do allow these configuration options:

// path of R for background processes
  "r.rpath.mac": "rpathMac",
  "r.rpath.linux": "rpathLinux",
  "r.rpath.windows": "rPathWindows",

// path of R for interactive processes
  "r.rterm.mac": "RtermMac",
  "r.rterm.linux": "RtermLinux",
  "r.rterm.windows": "RtermWindows"

// additional lib paths to be used
  "r.libPaths": ["abc"],
  "r.useRenvLibPath": true,

It should be possible to just query these configuration settings each time we need the values. They all seem to default to blanks.

Here is a thread that supports this approach as the way in which you change or specify R versions: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72707869/changing-r-version-in-vs-code

It is worth noting that publishers may hit this issue (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78027833/vs-code-uses-old-r-version-in-terminal-when-opened-inside-of-folder) when they are changing versions. If we rely upon the config settings as listed above, our agent shouldn't hit the problem, but the publishers may hit it within their own terminal windows.

id = 'simple.py'
isDir = false

title: Investigate Workbench initialization error
Publisher Log tree display is extremely inefficient
description:
The publisher log display is implemented within `extensions/vscode/src/views/logs.ts`. It's approach for displaying the log messages as they are received is very inefficient and should be refactored.

This code performs repetitive, mostly redundant object construction.  As log messages are received, they are appended into an array of other log messages within the stages object, with then the code signalling for a refresh. VSCode then calls GetChildren, which causes every stage and every one of the log messages for each stage to be constructed over and over again.

This reconstruction of the entire set of TreeItems occurs once for every log message received, plus a couple for the stable stages. In my testing for deployment of the `fastapi-simple`, this occurred 720 times. 

I would suggest the code create each TreeItem once, and simply keep passing references back into the VSCode callbacks for getChildren. This would eliminate the redundant construction of objects, which is currently occurring.

title: Make schema validation more flexible?
description:
Our schema validation is strict. When we add fields to the schema, files that contain them will not be usable in older versions of the publisher. Extension auto-updates mitigate the issue, but they're not always enabled. We need a strategy to deal with this.


Some ideas:
* Do nothing - if you're collaborating with or deploying content created by  someone using a newer extension, you need to update. You can work around new fields by dealing with them manually, for example, by removing them.
* Allow extra fields and preserve them when writing config files. This means that field name typos won't be errors (we could warn). Any new deployment features called out in the config file won't be applied as specified, because the older client doesn't understand those fields.
* If the publisher sees a schema that is not built-in, load it from the schema URL and use that for validation. We would also need to preserve the extra values as above.

The strategy might be different for configurations (user opts in to using new fields, and expects them to be honored) vs. content records (Publisher creates them and decides what information to include).

title: Python Scan: imports without a space in a Notebook cell results in an incorrect package being added to requirements.txt
description:
When adding an import to a cell in a notebook _without_ a space, alias or new line after, we get something like this added to the requirements.txt file:
```
requestsimport
```

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/41300090/63f262b8-1ebb-4fca-8a91-b6cfdd593a40

You can reproduce with this example:
https://github.com/rstudio/connect-content/tree/kg-publisher/bundles/cell-import-bug

description:
Some that seem to be affected are:

- scan requirements

Python package sniffer: find all imports in a notebook
description: I believe that we only look in the first code chunk for jupyter notebooks. Observed in user testing: having imports in both a first code chunk and a second code chunk, but packages in the second code chunk didn't seem to be added to `requirements.txt`

title: Document configuring trusted domain in VSCode
description: I'm not sure if this is possible, but could we add server URLs that someone has credentials to to the trusted domains for vscode? That will give us one less modal to click when visiting content.

title: Detecting Python when project is R-only
description:
When inspecting an R project such as rmd-static-1, the publisher returns a configuration containing Python. I think this was introduced with the change to use the selected Python from VSCode/Positron, because the backend interprets "you specified which Python to use" as an indication that the project is using Python.

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/mm-preflight-type-changes/internal/initialize/initialize.go#L80-L83

description: Renaming the Configuration in the UI, requires you to update the Deployment associated with it.  If there is a linked Deployment file, can we offer to update it/them for the user?

title: Renaming Deployment leaves the user in an unexpected state
description:
When you change the Deployment name, we get into an unexpected state where it's unclear what the next steps are. I think we hit an earlier placeholder version of the UI where the Destination is lost and the description is "Get deploying". I saw Julia hit this during user testing during the collaboration section.  The Deployment name was "collab_deployment"   Here I rename the deployment and we can see it gets into the unexpected state:


https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/41300090/637619dc-8672-4aca-97de-3046c7fa4ed7

title: nit: "missing configurations" messaging asks me to "Select a Configuration" even when there isn't one
description:
when there are no configurations for a deployment, there's a `Select a Configuration` link. Should this say `Create a Configuration` when there isn't one to select?

![Screenshot 2024-05-30 at 9 53 59 AM](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/41300090/0a1aae84-f6b3-4b02-b08f-79589f2ab766)

title: nit: order of steps creating api key
description:
This may just be me, but I always want to do:
1. URL
2. API Key
3. Name 

Rather than:
1. URL
2. Name
3. API Key

I keep finding myself naming the API Key with my actual API Key when I'm going quickly.

description: Once this is available, we'll need to update the URL as used within PR: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/1749

title: R Packages text when no renv.lock file exists
description:
I think this was placeholder text when we didn't have a Scan button for the R Packages.

> To deploy R content, you need a package file listing any package dependencies, but the file does not exist or is invalid. Use 'renv::snapshot()' at an R console to create one or edit the current configuration file (configuration-1) to point to an existing valid file.

Should we instead be asking the user to hit the Scan button here?

title: R Scan fails when there is no `renv/activate.R`
description:
The Scan button appears when there's no `renv.lock` file. If you have a `renv/activate.R` file in the project, the Scan button creates a renv.lock file for you.

If there is no `renv/activate.R` file, the Scan button will fail with:
> An error has occurred at homeView::_onScanForRPackageRequirements, Code=ERR_BAD_RESPONSE, Msg=Request failed with status code 500, URL=http://localhost:61514/api/post/packages/r/scan

Logs:
> time=2024-05-29T14:03:37.105-04:00 level=DEBUG msg="Running command" cmd="C:\\Program Files (x86)\\R\\R-4.4.0\\bin\\R.exe" args="-s -e renv::snapshot(lockfile=\"c:\\Users\\kgartland\\publisher-client\\bundles\\mpg-shinyApp\\renv.lock\")"
> time=2024-05-29T14:03:37.298-04:00 level=ERROR msg="Error running command" command="C:\\Program Files (x86)\\R\\R-4.4.0\\bin\\R.exe" error="exit status 1"
> Error in file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) : 
>   cannot open the connection
> Calls: source -> file
> In addition: Warning message:
> In file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) :
>   cannot open file 'renv/activate.R': No such file or directory
> Execution halted
> time=2024-05-29T14:03:37.298-04:00 level=DEBUG msg=renv::snapshot() out="" err="Error in file(filename, \"r\", encoding = encoding) : \r\n  cannot open the connection\r\nCalls: source -> file\r\nIn addition: Warning message:\r\nIn file(filename, \"r\", encoding = encoding) :\r\n  cannot open file 'renv/activate.R': No such file or directory\r\nExecution halted\r\n"
> time=2024-05-29T14:03:37.298-04:00 level=ERROR msg="Internal Server Error" method=POST url=/api/packages/r/scan error="exit status 1"
> time=2024-05-29T14:03:37.298-04:00 level=INFO msg="Access Log" method=POST url=/api/packages/r/scan elapsed_ms=326 status=500 req_size=24 resp_size=21 client_addr=127.0.0.1:61559 req.saveName=renv.lock
> 

If the `Scan` function requires a `renv/activate.R` file, can we hide the Scan button and ask that they run `renv::init()` or  `renv::snapshot()`?  


Additionally, f you _do_ have an renv.lock file but no `renv/activate.R`, and click the eye icon to rewrite the file, it will fail in the same way.

title: Add content type into deployment file, once app GUID is assigned
description:
Needed by issue #1658, which wants to restrict assignment or creation of new configs to the same content type as the deployed app has within Connect.

Without it, we are unable to handle the scenario where the previous config is no longer present, but we need to create a new one which will be compatible (and hopefully successfully deploy).

Resolved by: #1755

Currently we are always running the agent with `-vv` (debug logging enabled). That seems fine for an alpha but not for shipping code.

Should also setup a facility to allow our different debug tracing methods within the UX to be turned on and off via settings in the extension. It would be great if these were dynamically enabled, so restart was not needed.
