title: Add a comment to generated config files
description: When we generate a config file, we open it to give the user a chance to review and make changes. We should add a comment to the file to let them know what it is and what they are supposed to do with it.

title: Quarto projects: pick either static or rendered
description:
Currently if I deploy a quarto project it defaults to rendered (which is the right default IMHO), but the file inclusions then also include the static rendered docs (e.g. under `_site`) by default, so it is a bit confusing which part of the content is actually being used. I can manually exclude the rendered files, but that's an extra step.

But there's an additional thing here of being able to pick either send the rendered stuff (as a static type) or send the quarto docs and render those on connect is helpful, and if we do that each of those should exclude the other's files from uploading by default.

This is probably a mix of other issues we already have, but thought the way it surfaced might be helpful.

Secrets store
description:
Provide a way to deploy with secrets, since we recommend against putting them in the config file as environment variables.

This needs more discussion. One proposal:
* Provide a client-side secret store, using the OS keychain as we do for credentials. 
* Store key/value pairs and provide a CRUD API.
* Create a UI treeview to allow editing the list of secrets.
* Show warning message with "fix me" link in the UI if any secrets in the config are not present in the local store.
* During preflight, ensure that all secrets called out in the config are present in the local store; err if any are missing.
* At deployment time, inject secret values via Connect's environment variables API.

title: Support R Markdown Site. Entrypoint being identified as a single R Markdown Doc.
description:
Example: https://github.com/rstudio/connect-content/tree/main/bundles/rmd-site

This example is getting initialized as an `rmd` and Connect is treating it as an `R Markdown Document`.  It should be an `rmd-site` so Connect will treat it as an `R Markdown Site`.

Since it's an `R Markdown Document` the links are broken in Connect.

Here's the example deployed with publisher client:

title: Refactor inclusion of ConfigurationErrors as separate from Configurations between homeView and webview
description:
PR https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/1640 introduced a separate array of ConfigurationErrors in order to minimize the impact of a blocking bug ahead of a release. 

Original idea was to change the type of the Configuration array to contain both Configurations and ConfigurationErrors. This will require additional checks and typeguards in many places, but it currently feels like the right way to do it.

Second idea may be to continue to offer the choice of being filtered or not, down in the home store. It doesn't makes sense that much of the code would need to filter out the ConfigurationErrors before using the Configurations, when they really only want the valid ones. So perhaps the temporary implementation isn't that far off from what we need? We can certainly clean it up a bit.

title: Use of Title and credentials as primary destination descriptors
description:
We can enforce that a Title is set in configurations by requiring them in the schema, and prompting users for them. Doing this we can always show the title that Connect will have in the UI and remove the need for users to name deployments.

This does introduce a uniqueness problem since Connect doesn't have name uniqueness. So it is possible to have two deployments with two configurations both using a specific name. We will need to show other unique information (like the GUID) to the user so they can distinguish from two destinations in the UI.

Changes will include:

1. Add Title into multi-steps which create configs and remove the prompts for name of deployments and configuration
    - [ ] extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newConfig.ts
    - [ ] extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newDestination.ts
    - [ ] extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/selectConfig.ts
2. Update Select Destination to show Title and summary
3. Update EvenEasierDeploy button to show Title and credential (maybe nickname and host in parenthesis)
4. Add entry point description below button
5. If have multiple configs - show configuration being used. If not, hide it and hide associate with different configuration

title: Don't add repeated include and excludes to configurations
description:

To reproduce do an include or exclude API call 3 times. I'm using [HTTPie](https://httpie.io/) here. 
```
http POST :9001/api/configurations/default/files path="simple.py" action="include"
```

This will produce a configuration with:
```
files = ['*', 'simple.py', 'simple.py', 'simple.py']
```

title: Deploy Your Project vs Redeploying
description:
I hit an issue while revisiting an old app that I had previously deleted from Dogfood and while I figured it out pretty quicky, I think it'll be confusing for users.  It's not clear that `Deploy Your Project` will, by default, target the previously deployed content item (add another layer of confusion, if the target app was deleted).  

When there's already a previously deployed item, the user should have two options:
1. Make a New Deployment
2. Redeploy to exisiting project

I think it's an important distinction because users can overwrite their app without ever considering what they're doing, which could break something in production.  That `Deploy Your Project` button is tempting to _just click_. 

If we can detect when there is an existing deployment, alerting the user in some way that they can deploy to the existing project or create a new one would be useful.

Bonus points if we can check if that project still exists in pre-flight before allowing them to "redeploy".

title: Add popovers for webview components
description:
VSCode uses popovers for hover titles, descriptions, and other elements. Here are some examples

<details>
  <summary>Icon Button</summary>
  
  https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/d63ea25b-7f89-4da0-8358-939f38531cdc

</details> 

<details>
  <summary>Tree item tooltip</summary>

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/f67ab8e8-9c8a-496b-9c76-471d89b19ba7

</details> 

To do this styled exactly like VSCode is not possible. Since we are operating inside of a webview iframe and popovers cannot break past that barrier like VSCode's do.

Our options are:

1. Use generic `title` attributes
 
These are handled at the browser level and can break past the iframe barrier since it isn't the thing presenting them. This is what GitLens does for their hover elements.

<details>
  <summary>GitLents Title Example</summary>
  
  https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/0d9473db-7cc3-42c1-85c2-773039f23394
</details> 

It is also what is suggested by the folks who build the VSCode Toolkit: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/issues/505


2. Use a popover library (like https://floating-ui.com/) and style our popovers

This would allow us to get the exact styling of a VSCode popover/tooltip. However it would have to remain inside of the iframe. So it would be different positionally and with how it was wrapped.

title: Consolidate name validation for configurations
Clicking Back on a Multi-step which occurs after a suppressed step appears to do nothing
description:
There is a problem with how I implemented skipping a multi-step prompt when there was only one choice. The step which is shown immediately afterward is not able to move backward to the previous step shown. Clicking on the left arrow does nothing.

We can skip multi-steps in the following ways:

- **DeployProject**:
  - Select the credential to use, if there is more than one
  - Select the config file to use, if there are more than one

- **InitWorkspace**
  - Name the deployment - if a fixedDeploymentName has not been supplied
  - Select the credential to use, if there is more than one
  - Select the entrypoint, if there is more than one
  - Name the config file to use - if a fixedConfigurationName has not been supplied

- **NewConfig**
  - Select the entrypoint,  if there is more than one
  - Name the config file to use 

- **NewDeployment**
  - Name the deployment
  - Select the credential to use, if there is more than one
  - Select the config file to use, if there are more than one
  - IF parameter 'allowPublish' is true, prompt to deploy

### Test Cases:
- **DeployProject** has none, since if you skip any, there is only one or none
- **InitWorkspace**:
  1. have only one credential and multiple entrypoints, test moving backwards from entrypoint selection
  2. have only one credential, single entrypoint, test moving backwards from config file name
  3. have multiple credentials, single entrypoint, test moving backward from config file name 
- **NewConfig** has none, since if you skip any, there is only one step
- **NewDeployment**:
  1. have only one credential, multiple configs, test moving backwards from config election
  2. have only one credential, one config, test moving backwards from the prompt to deploy
  3. have multiple credential, one config, test moving backwards from the prompt to deploy

What occurs is, when the options are updated in `PSelect` `vscode-dropdown` will select the item at the same index regardless of the `_selection` `:value` prop.

This can be seen by adding a deployment or configuration from their views, and watching the `PSelect` `v-model` value stay the same, but the `vscode-dropdown` changing what is displayed as selected.

The easiest way to is to select the first deployment, and create a new one that is higher in alphabetical order (ie. `default` -> `a`)

- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/issues/486
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/issues/332

title: Create `TreeItem` component for VSCode webviews
description:
Very closely tied to #1333 but can be done in parallel. 

---

The [VSCode Tree View](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/tree-view) and its individual items are a great visual that users expect in VSCode. However the [`vscode-webview-ui-toolkit`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-webview-ui-toolkit/tree/main) does not include an option for a TreeView Item component to use in webview views.

To accomplish the UI's we want inside of a webview we have to implement our own. 

### Example

![Image](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/98dd260b-e6d8-4ed5-9f0a-ba9af0f01dd5)

### Task

Implement a `TreeItem` component that has:

- [x] Title
  - See `package.json` in the example above
- [x] Sub-text
  - See `extension/vscode` in the example above
- [x] Hoverable styling
- [x] Click action to support clicking on the item to trigger an action
- [x] An actions slot for buttons that trigger actions
- [x] Support for icons
- [x] Indent guidelines

title: Create config-based requirements API
description:
Currently we have the `/api/requirements` API endpoint that is hardcoded to support `requirements.txt`, but the configuration allows the customization of the `package-file`. Meaning that `requirements` are dependent on the configuration. To support this we will need a new endpoint based on the configuration.

`/api/requirements/:name/files` will support this allowing us to get the `requirements` for a particular configuration.

---

Following this same model for future non-Python requirements will allow us to more easily handle other languages.

title: Create config-based files API
description:
Currently we have the `/api/files` API endpoint, but with the upcoming "Per-Configuration File Include/Excludes" work the files included / excluded will be dependent on the configuration. To support this we will need a new endpoint based on the configuration.

`/api/configurations/:name/files` will support this allowing us to get the `files` for a particular configuration.

title: Handle scenario where user has no credentials for a deployment.
description:
This may occur initially or because the user has chosen to refresh credentials

Have to handle:

- deployment section:
    - Disabling / removing deploy operation icon
    - Update of the tooltip
- Home View: 
    - Disable entry within dropdown, with some indication of why it is disabled
    - Update deploy button enabled, if the selected entry becomes disabled
    - Update deployment status to indicate they have no credentials that match the URL

We have talked about adding an API that could be called for each deployment, which indicates if there are any known credentials. This was thought of to remove the responsibility of the UX to loop through existing credentials and see if there are any URL matches. Having to make an API call for each of the deployments would be pretty chatty, so I'm not in favor of this alternative API idea, I'd rather just check within the UX.

One possible alternative is then to make it easier to check, so we could add some type of metadata field to the deployment API which would return if there were any credentials for the deployment, thereby eliminating the need for the UX to query all accounts and then do it's own matching. This would be helpful in the future when the backend would also be making sure there are some credentials which have ownership/collaboration access to the content item on the server, as the metadata could be enhanced.

title: Empty entrypoint is accepted but breaks the deployment record
description:
* Config validation requires the `entrypoint` field to be present.
* `entrypoint = ''` is accepted
* Configuration struct declares `Entrypoint` with `toml:"entrypoint,omitempty`
* When this configuration is written out (as a config file or deployment record), `entrypoint` is omitted because it is empty
* Validation of the written file fails.

In this case, deployment was done through the CLI and succeeded (Connect did not need an entrypoint in this case), but an invalid deployment record was written.

title: Consider having per-configuration file inclusion/exclusion
description:
Switch to a model where the configuration specifies the files to include. By default, generated config files will have:

```
files = [
  '/**'
]
```

which will deploy the entire directory tree.

On the UI, show included files to be the ones that match the configuration file list/patterns.

Files in .positignore are omitted from the "Excluded Files List" (or grayed out), making them ineligible to be added. This is similar to how `git add` doesn't show ignored files. We can then also honor a user-level .positignore where users can put things like `.DS_Store`, `.idea/`, etc. similar to `~/.gitignore`.  (see #724).

If a wildcard pattern (like the default one) matches an ignored file, the file is excluded.

From @aronatkins: https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C014UG28GB1/p1711546060484779

> I would like for the publisher to support Quarto projects containing a single rendered script and standalone rendered scripts published as Quarto content. I’ve got Connect Jump Start examples and documentation ready to go, along with rsconnect and rsconnect-python changes which support the content.

> The Connect changes are probably the best resources, along with the Quarto documentation:

>    * https://quarto.org/docs/computations/render-scripts.html
>    * Jump Start and tests: https://github.com/rstudio/connect/pull/26213
>    * Documentation: https://github.com/rstudio/connect/pull/26260

The corresponding rsconnect PR is https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/pull/1055.

Set views' `initialSize` for better initial experience
description:
`initialSize` can help us favor certain views that start open by making them a bit larger initially. 

> Extensions that contribute views in package.json can use the initialSize property to set the initial size of their views. initialSize works similarly to the CSS flex-grow.
There are some restrictions on when initialSize is applied:
It's only an initial size. Once a view has been rendered, the initialSize will not be applied again.
It's only applied when the extension owns both the view and the view container.


### References

- https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_72#_tree-view-initialsize-contribution-finalized
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/flex-grow

title: .python-version use inconsitencies
description:
The requirements Scan function in VSCode uses the `.python-version` file in the parent directory. However the Initialize Project function uses the Python version found on PATH.  

PATH version:`3.11.4`
.python-version: `3.10.0`

File structure:
sample-content/.python-verison
sample-content/fastapi-simple

VSCode has the `fastapi-simple` folder open.

When I intialize the project, it uses the Python version on my PATH (`3.11.4`)
However when I try to scan the requirements file, it uses the `.python-version` file found in the directory outside this project (3.10.0).  Python 3.10.0 is _not_ installed on my system so the failure is expected here.  The bug is the inconsistent way we we use `.python-version`.

https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/41300090/15cf5c25-88ad-4f44-a4d4-59054ff777a5

In default.toml file we see it detected Python 3.11.4:
```
[python]
version = '3.11.4'
package-file = 'requirements.txt'
package-manager = 'pip'
```

However, when clicking the Requirements Scan button,  in the Posit Publisher Output we see it's trying to use 3.10.0:

```
pyenv: version `3.10.0' is not installed (set by /Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/.python-version)
time=2024-03-18T16:02:08.586-04:00 level=ERROR msg="Internal Server Error" method=POST url=/api/requirements error="could not run python executable '/Users/kgartland/.pyenv/shims/python': exit status 1"
```

The only way to `.positignore` files on a path in Windows is to specify `\\` for each directory.

Now that we have the Deployment Files section we can see this in real-time.  Here I exclude the `ingore.txt` file by using `\\` but when I try to use a single `\`, it does not get moved to the exclusion list:


https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/41300090/37ebf382-94c6-4e89-aaa5-bcf51d8195d3

I would expect a single `\` to work in Windows for the .positignore file.

title: Deploying without Quarto config settings gives unhelpful error
description:
When deploying our `quarto-project` sample with this configuration:

```toml
'$schema' = 'https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json'
type = 'quarto'
entrypoint = 'quarto-project.qmd'
validate = true
title = 'quarto-project'
```

I get an unhelpful "Unsupported App Mode" error on publish even though the `type` is supported. To get past this error I needed to include:

```toml
[quarto]
version = '1.3.450'
engines = ['jupyter']
```

title: Redeploying shouldn't prompt for a config file
description:
When redeploying, the extension asks for a credential (if you have more than one) and also prompts for the configuration file. Config files are persistently associated with a deployment and it should be a specific user action to change that. The current behavior makes it too easy to use the wrong configuration (e.g. publishing to production with a staging configuration).

In order for this workflow to be whole, when creating a new deployment, we need to prompt for the configuration before the Yes/No (deploy now) prompt.

Has dependency on #1261 - so that we can save the configuration name within the pre-deployment file.

I have a branch which has most of this in place, just waiting on PR #1261 to finish up.

title: requirements show behavior isn't consistent with the API
description:
Current behavior:
* `requirements create` and `POST /api/requirements` both scan and then create the file
* `requirements show` only scans, and `GET /api/requirements` only reads the file.

Proposal:
* `requirements show` shows you the current requirements (like you will see in the UI)
* `requirements scan` shows you the result of scanning (current `requirements show` behavior)

Alternatively:
* `requirements show` shows you the current requirements (like you will see in the UI)

title: Remove flashing of welcome views with package.json when clauses
description:
In prototyping the single section view initial Welcome vs. the multiple sections shown when the current workspace has been initialized for publishing, I noticed there was often an initial display of one state followed by the correction/display of the desired state.

In `package.json`, the visibility of our specific publisher views is controlled by logical evaluation of context variable values (within `when` attributes), set within the publisher extension. Sometimes these are set within `extension.ts` for our entire extension, and others are set within the `activate` for a particular view. Regardless of where you set the value initially, it is set via this command with the appropriate parameters:

>commands.executeCommand('setContext', initializedContext, 'indeterminate');

What I concluded was that use of boolean values for the context values did not lead to predictable display. I have not looked at the actual source code evaluating it, but it appeared that VSCode was interpreting the absence of the variable when searching the context for the value, as a specific boolean state. So rather than being tri-state: `undefined`, `true` and `false`, it was evaluating into only `true` and `false`, with `undefined` sometimes being `true` and sometimes being `false`. My experiments showed it to be pretty indeterminate. Sections were shown temporarily and then would flip into the desired state after a visible delay.

When I switched over to string comparisons, all of the indeterminate behavior went away. 

My conclusions:

1. BAD:
    a. Setting value: `commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'posit.publisher.initializedContext', false);`
    b. Using it in a when clause: `"when": "posit.publisher.initialized === false"

1. GOOD: 
    a. Setting value: `commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'posit.publisher.initializedContext', 'initialized');`
    b. Using it in a when clause: `"when": "posit.publisher.initialized ==='initialized'"

My conclusion is that we should be using string values to compare against, rather than boolean.

We should also be looking at when we set the initial context values to be evaluated. Waiting until one of our sub-views loads leaves the value undefined for some time, and depending what type of variable and where we need to evaluate it, display visibility can be slow or quick (or indeterminate itself).

Draft PR w/ initial functionality: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/1075

title: requirements: handle model.joblib better
description:
While adding some `requirements create` tests, I noticed our [fastapitableau-example](https://github.com/rstudio/connect-content/tree/main/bundles/fastapitableau-example) jumpstart was failing with:
```No module named 'sklearn'```

The `requirements create` command adds `fastapitableau`, `joblib` and `pandas` but this app also requires `scikit-learn`.  It seems that`model.joblib` file in the app directory is closely associated with the `scikit-learn` package but can also dynamically add other imports to the app.  

Can we do the following when we find a `model.joblib`?

1. add `scikit-learn` to the requirements.txt file
2. emit a warning informing the customer that this file was found in their directory and they may need to add other packages to their requirements.txt file manually.

Possile wording:
> We've created a requirements.txt for you however we detected a `model.joblib` in your project directory which may dynamically import other packages in your app.  You may need to manually add those packages to your requirements.txt file prior to deploying.

title: Add docs + other helpers for (re)installing alphas
description:
In a chat with @dotNomad I was remarking how much I liked [Positron's updating docs + helpers](https://connect.posit.it/positron-wiki/updating-positron.html). title: Epic: Deployments view
description:
**Ideas from UX Document:**

DEPLOYMENTS

- [x] When no deployments exist, display a welcome message to prompt them to start the new deployment flow
    - New deployment flow: Use Multi-step interface to:
    - Name the deployment
    - Select the credential to use
    - Generate configuration? (if none exist)

  - [x] Refresh list
  - [x] New deployment

  - [x] Mouse-over displays multi-line info that we’re now showing on deployment card
- View/item/context operations:
  - [x] Delete
  - [x] Deploy 
  - [x] View deployment file
- [x] File watching: Update list when underlying files change (so all related commands automatically update the view)

### Tasks
- [x] https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/1008
- [x] https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/1010
- [x] https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/1027
- [x] https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/1017
- [x] https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/issues/1026


### Thoughts

#### Publishing flow from top-level extension

#####  If there is one deployment, one matching credential, one config, we'll start deployment on click

#####  If there are no deployments present
1. Prompt for name
2. Prompt for credential, if there are more than one
3. Prompt for config, if there are more than one

##### If there is more than one deployment
1. Prompt for which deployment
2. If there are multiple credentials that match, then prompt
3. If there are multiple configurations, then prompt

#### Publishing flow from item/context of a deployment

1. If there are multiple credentials which match, then prompt
2. If there are multiple configurations, then prompt

title: Python package status is not informative
description:
The python package status during construction of a virtualenv isn't very informative.

Pip does not indicate when it is installing a package. We can see downloads and download cache hits, and can see when a package is installed over a version present in the base environment. But after the download phase, all new packages are installed and there is a single log line for all.

Between the known events, there can be significant elapsed time that (from our messaging) looks like it was spent downloading or installing a specific package, when in fact pip has moved on.

Proposal:
* Include download cache hits, with status = "checking"
* Include the "installing all packages" event with a status = "installing", name = "packages", version=""

title: Create better success and failure Deployment TypeScript types
description: Currently we have a `Deployment`, `PreDeployment`, and `DeploymentError`. However we want to know more about the error states in some of our components. We can make those `isSuccessful` and `isUnsuccessful` functions type predicates informing us that `deploymentError` is not `null`, for example, making them easier to use across the frontend.

title: Refactor Deployment Status to be more slot based
description:
Currently our `DeploymentStatus` component is heavily based on the type of Deployment we are looking and its success/failure status. However this is difficult to maintain and keep consistent. After a discussion with @sagerb we thought a refactor to make the card and header details more "slot based" (date slot, server slot, dashboard link slot, etc) which would make it much easier to maintain.

Reference to discussion: https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/864#pullrequestreview-1844656324

title: DeploymentPage 404s due to store race condition
description:
Going to a Deployment details page at `/deployments/:name` and reloading will cause a fatal error to occur due to a race condition.

The issue is on https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/cb7699d74fe6190c5d4f95607dd97a261bfe32cb/web/src/views/deployment/DeploymentPage.vue#L69
where we attempt to get the deployment from the store which is still being initialized. The deployment will never be in the store until the API call completes. This means every time, on reload, we will get an error "Invalid Value for Deployment Object".

description: In the frontend we are frequently using `saveName` if looking at a `Deployment` or `PreDeployment` and using `deploymentName` if looking at a `DeploymentError`. Ideally this should be the same attribute and we can reference it on any Deployment type.

title: Refactor ConfigSettings to programmatically show settings
description:
Currently the `ConfigSettings.vue` component is heavily templated and requires a lot of boilerplate. In the future we can be better about programmatically showing the settings and having exceptions for settings that need special rendering - like those with Array types.

This is on hold until we are pulling down information from stores and file watching.

title: feat(vscode): enable user to choose project directory on startup
description:
Currently, the extension provides the workspace directory as the project directory when starting the publisher.  https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/blob/main/extensions/vscode/src/services.ts#L96

In some cases, this is appropriate, but it is often not. A better approach would...

- Allow the user to configure the project directory.
- Scan the file tree for any .posit directories and prompt the user to choose.

title: feat(vscode): move publish icon to activity bar
description:
Currently, the publish icon is displayed in the editor toolbar. The editor toolbar implies a file-level context. Since the publisher intuitively exists in a project-level context, moving the launch icon to the activity bar seems appropriate.

https://code.visualstudio.com/api/ux-guidelines/overview

title: feat(vscode): improve extension's time-to-first-render
description:
There is a delay when starting the extension. This delay waits for the server to start before revealing the UI to the user.

Modify the startup process to launch the server as part of the VSCode startup sequence. The current implementation launches the first execution of any command.

title: Normalize URLs across sources
Update style for anchors in dark mode
description:
Currently the default styling for visited anchors is very hard to read in dark mode, and the normal styling isn't that much better. We need to improve this.

![Image](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/09804f7c-cad2-4e85-8c03-c287a4a2f875)

title: Remove visited style from links
description:
Visited style links don't make a lot of sense inside of an app dashboard like this. Perhaps styling for external links could still have a `:visited`.

VSCode also resets the `<a>` styling defaults for Chrome and doesn't have a `:visited` styling so this makes the app more consistent between the two.

title: Improve colors and use VSCode colors in DiffTag
description:
Currently the `DiffTag` component which is used to enable the Configuration Diff view is only using simple `red` and `green` borders. This works for light and dark mode but can be improved. Additionally it can use VSCode colors with a fallback in the `var()` CSS function.

This was separated from #783 to potentially remove this bit of work from the Alpha 2 milestone since it is difficult to select what VSCode colors to use, have fallbacks if the theme is using borders vs backgrounds, etc.

title: bug: recover state if agent process terminates unexpectedly
description:
The extension is not aware of the process that is launched via the terminal. It only knows of the terminal, not the process running inside of it. 

Therefore, if the agent process is killed by another process (or by the user) then the extension enters an unknown state that it can't recover from.

A potential solution is to check if the API responds to a request. If it doesn't, then the agent needs to be relaunched.

title: Support copy from my env workflow for environment variables
description:
We should support copying environment variables from the machine that is initiating the deploy similar to `rsconnect:deployApp()` as a way to:
- ease migration to the new tool by making it familiar
- provide a way to pass encrypted data to Connect to be used in environment variable values

### References

- [Slack discussion](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C05D7NZD52S/p1705441548870119)
- https://rstudio.github.io/rsconnect/reference/deployApp.html

title: Create alpha2 changelog
Support Quarto inspection during project init
description:
The `init` command does not recognize and configure Quarto projects. For this, we need:
* recognize the entrypoint .qmd file (preferring the one that matches the project directory name)
* run `quarto inspect` to determine the quarto version and engines
* capture Python dependencies if needed (configuration includes jupyter engine, or a pre-render or post-render .py script)

The first iteration will only support the `jupyter` engine, and will err if the `knitr` engine is configured.

title: More specific language when using environment variables for server
description:
when deploying with the account specified in Environment Variables we say "using account env". Will users know what that means?

```
> publisher deploy test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/
Deploy to server https://rsc.radixu.com using account env and configuration default, creating deployment Untitled-10
```

Instead can we specifically say we're using the Environment Variables CONNECT_SERVER and CONNECT_API_KEY to determine server and api keys?

title: Remove theme setting buttons in VSCode
description:
With #356 and #796 work we will be inheriting the CSS that VSCode injects into the webview panel. That will make our UI match the theme selected in VSCode proper. However we have a theme setting in the UI that allows us to select Dark, Light, or System (your computers color preference). This will need to be removed since VSCode CSS variables will not be adjusted based on the UI level theme.

The theme setting in the UI can stay in the non-VSCode UI.

title: Conditional display of progress steps
description:
Display only the the steps that will occur in the deployment that is being started. Return this from the `POST /api/deployments/:name` endpoint.

We may want to show the steps grayed out, like we do now, but it is still helpful to have the frontend know which steps are expected.

title: Refresh button does not function in VSCode Webview

title: Use HTML5 mode vue-router history
description:
If we do not use [HTML5 mode for the `vue-router` history](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/history-mode.html#HTML5-Mode) we get errors in VSCode:

![Image](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/assets/19917631/69c3acba-8484-461c-a144-ae2790b3a66b)

We have to configure our Go web server to fallback to point to our web app though when the server receives requests to endpoints too:

> Here comes a problem, though: Since our app is a single page client side app, without a proper server configuration, the users will get a 404 error if they access https://example.com/user/id directly in their browser. Now that's ugly.
> Not to worry: To fix the issue, all you need to do is add a simple catch-all fallback route to your server. If the URL doesn't match any static assets, it should serve the same index.html page that your app lives in. Beautiful, again!

description:
When reviewing this [PR](https://github.com/posit-dev/publisher/pull/756), it occurred to me the error state isn't very clear.  In the scenario when a deployment cannot be made (for example,  undetected Content Type), we don't explicitly warn the user anywhere in the app without some action required.

Suggestions:

* Disable `Add a New Deployment` button with an error message being displayed on click or hover.
* Make the `!` icon in the Configuration card red so it stands out
* Explicitly state what the error is on the page somewhere so it can't be missed.

We already have all we need to do this in the UI since the deployment records have the previously used configuration details and we have all of the new details for the default configuration.

title: Deployment Error from Non-Current Deployment not shown
description:
Errors on Project Page and Deployment page are not showing correctly.

To reproduce:

1. Clean out deployments
2. Create a new deployment that is successful
3. Redeploy that deployment, but cause it to fail. (I had two credentials for same server, and tried to redeploy without that second user being a collaborator)
4. Project page shows the error correctly, as does the deployment page.
5. Create a new deployment that is successful
6. Return to the project page and you will see that the earlier deployment, which was in error, is now showing success.

Base Issue:
Error is being displayed by looking at the last deployment results built up by the event stream, which only handles one result.

Error should be populated out of the deployment object, where it is now being populated.

Needs to be implemented after #786

title: Move `/progress` page to `/deployments/:name/progress`
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

With the new Predeployment Records and all publishing moving under the `/deployments/:name` page in the UI we can move the progress page underneath the deployment details pages. This:

> simplifies how we retrieve the progress logs for previous deployments
> simplifies the history and makes navigation (and breadcrumbs) make more sense

title: Remove `localId` from progress events
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> Since all deploying in the UI occurs with a named deployment or pre-deployment record in this model the progress events can be tied to that unique identifier instead of a `localId`.

title: Add Predeployment Records support to Deployment Details page
Create Predeployment Record with `/add-new-deployment` form
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> When filling out the “New Deployment” form we can create a “Pre-deployment Record” on completion based on the Deployment Name and selected server details.

Instead of using the form to navigate to the New Deployment page with URL query params, we can instead submit and `POST /api/deployments` to create a Predeployment Record. On success we can navigate to the new Deployment Details page.

title: Remove `/new-deployment` page
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> Instead of having a `/new-deployment page` there would only be the “Deployment Details pages” at `/deployments/:name`

The `/new-deployment` page and related components can be removed from the UI with the addition of Predeployment Records. Once those are supported we can go directly from the `/add-new-deployment` form to the (Pre)Deployment Details page.

title: Add API endpoint `POST /api/deployments/:name` to publish
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> Publishing via the UI would always use the `/api/deployments/:name` endpoint which would handle the initial deployment for a “Pre-deployment Record” or a redeployment if that record has already been deployed before.

title: Add API support for Predeployment Records
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> Getting deployments via `/api/deployments` or `/api/deployments/:name` will return `Deployment`, `DeploymentError` and/or one additional type `PreDeployment`.
The PreDeployment will not have a `ContentID` since it has never been deployed, but it will have the file name, server details, etc.

title: Add API to create Predeployment Records
description:
Part of the [Deployment Rework in the UI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hrxe6MtMdQup6OC0FMIm1Leprcz22DXx4lcPwm6cqc/edit)

> `POST /api/deployments` would create a “Pre-deployment Record” rather than publishing

title: Rename CLI commands
description:
Rename the `create` and `update` commands.

Decide on CLI structure. Options that have been discussed:
* Current structure. Rename `create` and `update` to `deploy` and `redeploy`.
* (Re)Combine into a single command that accepts an `--update` or similar option:
```
publisher deploy -a dogfood -n staging           # creates staging deployment
publisher deploy -a dogfood -n production        # creates production deployment
publisher deploy                                 # creates another (unnamed) deployment
publisher deploy --update staging                # updates staging deployment
```

* (Re)Combine into a single command that accepts a `--new` or similar option. Default would be to create a deployment if there aren't any, or update your last deployment (maybe err if there are more than one and you don't say which one?). Seems like we'd still need `--update` here?
```
publisher deploy -a dogfood -n staging           # creates staging deployment
publisher deploy                                 # updates staging deployment
publisher deploy --new -a dogfood -n production  # creates production deployment
publisher deploy                                 # updates production deployment, or is an error
publisher deploy --update staging                # updates staging deployment
```

* Consider shipping a separate `publish` binary, so in the above, `publisher deploy ...` can just be `publish ...`

description:

![Image](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/assets/17675905/ec0a6aa4-1a94-4b12-867f-312a0f8e859c)

title: Deletion of `.positignore` or removal of rules aren't reflected in API
description:
This seems to be a problem no matter how `.positignore` is updated.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the UI / API with `just run ui test/sample-content/fastapi-simple --listen=127.0.0.1:9001`
2. Grab the response of `GET /api/files` I used [httpie](https://httpie.io/): `http :9001/api/files`
3. Create a `.positignore` and add `.gitignore` to the exclusions. See that reflected in the API response

From here there are a few ways to see this problem:
- delete `.positignore` entirely
- Remove all contents `.positignore`
- Remove `.gitignore` and add another file
  
No matter what was done above `.gitignore` will still be excluded siting the `.positignore` file as the reason.

Added files seem to be reflected but removal of exclusions do not.

title: kubernetes: publishing-schema: Validation Issues
description:
https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json

Looks like the schema wants `memory-request` and `memory-limit` to be a string but we validate them at pre-flight as an int.

`py-environment-management` doesn't seem to be a valid option at pre-flight but it's in the schema as a boolean.


* **memory-request**
Error:
```
error in file 'stock-api-fastapi\.posit\publish\default.toml'. Keyword 'connect/kubernetes/memory-request' expected integer, but got string.
```

Schema:
```
            "memory-request": {
              "type": "string",
              "minimum": 0,
              "description": "The minimum amount of RAM this content needs when executing or rendering, expressed in bytes.",
              "examples": [
                "20000000"
              ]
```

* **memory-limit**
Error:
```
error in file 'stock-api-fastapi\.posit\publish\default.toml'. Keyword 'connect/kubernetes/memory-limit' expected integer, but got string.
```

Schema:
```
            "memory-limit": {
              "type": "string",
              "minimum": 0,
              "description": "The maximum amount of RAM this content will be allowed to consume when executing or rendering, expressed in bytes. If the process tries to use more memory than allowed, it will be terminated",
              "examples": [
                "100000000"
              ]
```

* **py-environment-management**

Schema:
```
            "py-environment-management": {
              "type": "boolean",
              "description": "Enables or disables Python environment management. When false, Posit Connect will not install Python packages and instead assume that all required packages are present in the container image.",
              "examples": [
                true
              ]
```

Error:
```
> publisher create .\stock-api-fastapi\ -a colorado
time=2023-12-15T16:04:26.345-05:00 level=ERROR msg="Error running command" error="can't load file 'stock-api-fastapi\\.posit\\publish\\default.toml': \n27| memory-limit = 10000\n28| memory-request = 5000\n29| nvidia-gpu-limit = 1\n30| py-environment-management = true\n  | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ missing field"

can't load file 'stock-api-fastapi\.posit\publish\default.toml':
27| memory-limit = 10000
28| memory-request = 5000
29| nvidia-gpu-limit = 1
30| py-environment-management = true
  | ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ missing field.
```

title: CLI: UX: update without a name throws confusing error
description:
```
> publisher update .\
time=2023-12-15T10:30:25.889-05:00 level=ERROR msg="Error running command" error="can't find deployment at '.posit\\publish\\deployments\\.toml': open .posit\\publish\\deployments\\.toml: The system cannot find the file specified."

can't find deployment at '.posit\publish\deployments\.toml': open .posit\publish\deployments\.toml: The system cannot find the file specified..
```

If you don't specify a name to update, that error message is returned. Since the `update` command expects a positional argument it's using the target directory, `.\`, as the `name`. 

Since we know we're missing a positional argument (`name` and `target`) maybe we can provide a better error to ensure they're giving us both `name` and `target` argument.  Or maybe going back to a named argument for `name` would work better here?


We throw the same error when there's only a single deployment too.  If there's only a single Deployment record, can we use that by default if a `name` isn't given?

title: `init` when no `requirements.txt` exist we create one semi-silently
description:
Since we want customers to create their own `requirements.txt` file to avoid unnecessary deployment delays and bloat on their Connect server, we should proactively tell them when we're creating requirements files for them.

Currently we don't print anything about it when not in `-v` mode:

```
> publisher init ./
Created config file "/Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/.posit/publish/default.toml"
```

verbose mode:
```
> publisher init ./
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.573-05:00 level=INFO msg="Client version" version=0.0.dev5-30-g15f64cd6
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.573-05:00 level=INFO msg="Development mode" mode=dev
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.573-05:00 level=INFO msg="Development build" DevelopmentBuild=true
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.573-05:00 level=INFO msg="Detecting deployment type and entrypoint..."
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.574-05:00 level=INFO msg="Deployment type" Entrypoint=app.py Type=python-shiny
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.574-05:00 level=INFO msg="Running Python" python=/Users/kgartland/.pyenv/versions/3.9.15/bin/python
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.598-05:00 level=INFO msg="Detected Python" version=3.9.15
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.598-05:00 level=INFO msg="Running Python" python=/Users/kgartland/.pyenv/versions/3.9.15/bin/python
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.598-05:00 level=INFO msg="Using Python packages" source="/Users/kgartland/.pyenv/versions/3.9.15/bin/python -m pip freeze"
time=2023-12-14T12:14:03.893-05:00 level=INFO msg="Wrote requirements file" path=/Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/requirements.txt
Created config file "/Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/.posit/publish/default.toml"
```



Suggestion:
 
In non-verbose mode we could tell the customer we're creating the requirements file for them:
```
> publisher init ./
A requirements.txt file was not found so we're creating one for you with `pip freeze`. Please review before publishing and omit any unnecessary packages or create your own manually.

Created requirements file "/Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/requirements.txt"
Created config file "/Users/kgartland/work/publishing-client/test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/.posit/publish/default.toml"
``` 

Additionally in `rsconnect-python` we print a comment in the requirements file so we know it was generated by us, which could be a helpful troubleshooting tool.

i.e.
```
# requirements.txt generated by rsconnect-python on 2023-12-14 17:04:15.470311
```

description: Similar to #541 the `filePath` supplied in the `Match` for file ignores should be relative to the passed directory to the CLI.

title: Config schema incorrect sets `memory-request` and `memory-limit` as strings
description:
`MemoryRequest` and `MemoryLimit` in `ConnectKubernetes` are [set as numbers in the Go struct](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/blob/883605ba4d7072ddc322407deda21418fd936e55/internal/config/types.go#L179).

Our frontend type [mirrors this](https://github.com/rstudio/publishing-client/blob/055f0eea1b7fda39184e5428112cf73964ab59dc/web/src/api/types/connect.ts#L26). 

However the schema has it as type `string`:

```
"memory-limit": {
  "type": "string",
  "minimum": 0,
  "description": "The maximum amount of RAM this content will be allowed to consume when executing or rendering, expressed in bytes. If the process tries to use more memory than allowed, it will be terminated",
  "examples": [
    "100000000"
  ]
}
```

https://cdn.posit.co/publisher/schemas/posit-publishing-schema-v3.json

description:
Each API has a list of possible errors which may be returned within a response.

The UX needs to differentiate and handle these differently than the fatal errors it receives.

The hope is that these errors can be displayed in a way in which the user can correct the issue and continue forward.

Fixed by: #635

title: Config path is based on run directory not passed directory
description:
When fetching a Configuration via `GET /api/configurations` the `configurationPath` is relative to the location the binary is run from.

For example when running:
```

```
from `~/dev/publishing-client` the `configurationPath` is `test/sample-content/fastapi-simple/.posit/publish/default.toml` 

I would expect that this would be a relative path to the directory provided to the publisher command.

title: Entrypoint considerations: commonly used filenames
description:
The current Entrypoint rules are:
* if there is one .py file, that is the entrypoint
* if there are multiple .py files, and one of them is app.py, then app.py is the entrypoint
* otherwise we fail to determine the entrypoint

Given that the use of multiple python files can be prevalent, we should expand on the default app.py entrypoint.

I went through the example sites for each of our supported content types and found commonly used filenames (not exhaustive):

Seems like we should include `api.py`, `main.py` and for streamlit case maybe `*app*.py`

dash:
app.py

flask:
app.py
api.py

fastapi:
main.py

streamlit:
app.py
streamlit_app.py

shiny:
app.py

bokeh:
main.py


voila and jupyter: 
.ipynb

title: Configuration file validation
description:
We need to validate config files when we load them.

Currently, we set `DisallowUnknownFields` on the TOML decoder, which ensures that all field names in the file are valid. The decoding process also ensures that data types match.

We should validate against the jsonschema, which is somewhat stricter (and would also verify that our code matches the schema). Additionally, we can check cross-field constraints (e.g. min processes cannot be > max processes).

title: Deployment record isn't in the bundle that gets deployed
description:
The deployment process currently follows these steps:
* create bundle
* create deployment on Connect (obtain the ID)
* write deployment record (contains the ID)
* upload bundle
* deploy bundle

So, the deployment record is not contained in the bundled files. We need that for the Collaborate Through Connect use case, where a collaborator downloads a bundle from Connect, makes a change, and wants to redeploy.

Confusingly, it will (sort of) work if you've deployed more than once, because all but the latest record will be included, allowing the client to identify the target server and deployment ID.

title: Modify CI to push archives (.tar.gz, .zip) to GitHub Release artifacts
description:
The current build process produces executables and uploads them to GitHub's release artifacts. These executables have unique names since GitHub does not allow multiple artifacts with the same name. GitHub also does not support directories as release artifacts.

The VSCode extension expects the executable name to be `publisher.` Therefore, the user must complete a manual rename of the executable downloaded from GitHub Releases before adding it to `PATH.`

Modify the build process to produce packaged archives that contain the executable. Each archive should contain the executable (`publisher,` `publisher.exe` on Windows) when extracted. The archive name should include the name, version, operating system, and architecture. 

As an example, reference the archives produced for Go: https://go.dev/dl/

Related to #388

title: Epic: Agent and UI lifecycle
description:
### Current Behavior / Mechanisms Available:

1. When Agent dies while UX is running, UX will receive the event (generated internally).
```
{ "type": "errors/open", "time": "Tue Sep 26 2023 09:24:16 GMT-0700 (Pacific Daylight Time)", "data": { "msg": "unknown error with connection 1695745456694" } }
```
2. When UX closes (after having opened the SSE channel), the agent could detect clients going away, but it is a question if this works if the browser process is terminated or has a happy exit path. From the SSE documentation (https://github.com/r3labs/sse):
```
A way to detect disconnected clients:

func main() {
	server := sse.New()

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		go func() {
			// Received Browser Disconnection
			<-r.Context().Done()
			println("The client is disconnected here")
			return
		}()

		server.ServeHTTP(w, r)
	})

	http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)
}
```

3. The UX could detect failure when unable to access the agent during any of its API calls and determine it is now disconnected (or never could get connected).

4. It would also be possible to implement a heartbeat API between the UX and the agent, which would help deterministically determine if either side has gone away. While this is basically what the SSE channel event on the client provides to the UX, there is the question if the other side of the connection, within the agent, is dependent on network transport timeouts in order to determine that the connection is "done". If it is, then it may not be as timely as we would want. In this case, an explicit application layer heartbeat would provide the simplest solution to meet expectations.

### Behavior once disconnect has been detected

Once we can detect that the other side is no longer there, then we need to address the expected behavior.

1. If the UX is launched without an agent, then the browser interface will indicate that it is unable to connect. Nothing we can do here.
2. If the UX is launched with the agent:
    a. but the agent dies, then the UX should display an error and indicate that it needs to be closed. No recovery is possible.
    b. but the UX is disconnected, then it is a question of what the agent was in the middle of:
        - configuration of publishing: the agent should exit with an error immediately.
        - publishing in progress: complete the publishing process (successful or error) and then exit.

title: Remove Quasar CLI and use our own tooling
description:
Quasar CLI "takes care of all the tooling" and has extensions for testing (we are using Cypress and Vitest extensions). However this has a handful of issues that we have run into:
- `quasar upgrade` failed with dependency resolution errors in #173 
- Upgrading Quasar extensions requires removing and re-adding them which:
  - Also hit dependency resolution errors and did not work
  - Requires manually handling overwritten files in git
- Quasar and Quasar's extensions especially are using older packages or causing dependency collisions (like with Vite requiring both 2.9 and 3/4)
- The Quasar extensions for testing are in Alpha / Beta states.

All of these combined cause issues maintaining and enabling different tooling. After @sagerb and I discussed this an option is to use Quasar's Vite plugin which injects Quasar into Vite so we can still use their components and configure Quasar.

We can maintain our own tooling separate from Quasar to enable everything ourselves without needing to use Quasar's extensions or configuration which have caused problems without much benefit - Quasar CLI gives features that we don't plan to use.

title: File Selector shows 3 files selected by default
description:
Description for the issue.

File Selector shows "3 files selected..." by default even when no files are selected.  When selecting actual files, it then adds those files to the total (i.e. "7 files selected" when there are a total of 4 files)

title: Configure default reviewers
Implement SSE channel from Agent to UX
description:
Following the decisions made in #139 and the implementation in #187.

This issue will cover the UX changes. It will include the receipt and display of existing events being published from the agent.

DoD:
- Events are received at the UX
- Components within the UX are able to subscribe to messages
- Messages will be displayed in a simple scrolling window within the publishing view (as basic as it can be, since we will replace the event's presentation with the work in #198.
- Unhandled events are displayed in the console of the UX

title: Add UX logger and method response method
description:
UX development needs a basic logger that can be optionally activated. 
- It should be simple and lightweight. 
- It should suppress logging when not activated.
- It should be able to be activated via a query parameter in the URL

In order to support logging results, we also need a standard response method object, which can wrap both success and an error object when failing. 

DoD:
- The two facilities are in place and are able to be used within the codebase.

title: Determine Interface Needs for Logging w/ SSE events on agent.
description:
The POC on branch `sagerb-POC-event-stream-for-realtime-logs` demonstrated the plumbing necessary to have server-side-events sent autonomously from the agent up to the UX. This facility is expected to be used to communicate autonomous errors, log message dispatch and general status from the agent up to the UX.

What this POC also demonstrated was the need for establishing the right data structures to accompany the events, which will allow the UX to minimize the amount of business logic it needs to implement (and allow us to centralize that logic in a common location for both the CLI and the UX).

This issue will be considered DONE when a document outlining the event data structures is reviewed and approved. This issue does not include implementation.

title: Use relative or full file path consistently across APIs
description:
The `GET /api/deployment` `manifest.files` initalized with relative paths (for the project to publish) for the files' keys.

If running the server with a relative path with the CLI command the `GET /api/files` will return relative paths. When running with an absolute path with the CLI command the `GET /api/files` will instead return a full, absolute path.

Either option de-syncs the keys for the File Tree causing everything to be unchecked initially since the key (`pathname`) don't match between the two API responses and therefor don't have a connection in the UI.

The workaround here to select files to get the agent and client back in sync. This does leave the old, initial files in the `manifest.files` list as there isn't a way to clear those out.

### Tasks
- [ ] The APIs use the same path naming for files
```

title: Create API endpoint for triggering publish action (initial)
description:
API endpoint will trigger the publish workflow that is currently implemented within the agent, using the parameters specified via the agent's CLI. No parameters need to be passed through w/ the API call, as we're currently going to simply hook it up to be triggered by the changes in the related issue: #93

Note: `connect-client` currently supports deployment via the command line w/ an action of `publish`. The intention overall is to be able to launch the `connect-client` with a similar command line but with an action of 'publish-ui', and have the UX displayed. When the UX calls the new publish API endpoint, the same behavior that the `publish` command would have automatically started, will occur (with the output being displayed in the terminal where the `connect-client` was run from.

DoD:
- Able to launch the `connect-client` with an appropriate set of CLI parameters w/ the 'publish-ui' target, and have the project deployed to a server that has been set up w/ an account, when the publish API is called. For example:

```
./bin/darwin-amd64/connect-client publish-ui \
test/sample-content/fastapi-simple \
 --account-name=dogfood \
 --title="First Connect-Client Test"
```

Then an appropriate curl command sent (API endpoint TBD):

```
curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/__api__/publish

```

Should result in a successful deployment.

This will affect our TypeScript typing, our Go JSON serialization, and will inform if we need/want any middleware to do conversions to match language standards (like camel case in JavaScript/TypeScript).

### Things to Consider
- Connect dashboard does [a transformation to and from camelCase and snake_case](https://github.com/rstudio/connect/blob/be3b4969a2791ba9ba1cc8daa745d97de7e31584/ui/dashboard/src/api/transform.js#L13C23-L13C23)

```[tasklist]
### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Create documentation formalizing the decision of the team
- [x] Determine why ESLint hasn't complained about snake_case
- [x] Convert TypeScript typing in the API module to match the decision
- [x] Implement Axios interceptors
- [x] Search for ESLint camelcase disabled rules and remove them
```

title: File list: add reason for exclusions to Files API
description:
File exclusion is done using a fork of a 3rd-party .gitignore package for Go (our modifications so far were to make it access the filesystem through an interface from the `afero` package). That code accepts exclusion patterns from the CLI (we pass them in directly), from .gitignore files (where the library seeks out all the .gitignore files in the directory tree), and from .rscignore files (where we tell the library to load them as we encounter them).

We need to:
* Make the gitignore library keep a record of where each exclusion pattern originated.
* Make the match function return that record (or nil) rather than just a boolean.
* Annotate the returned file list with the exclusion reason.

title: File list: restructure bundling code
description:
The same code should serve the bundle/manifest creation path and the file listing path. But there are some differences:
* Bundle/manifest code skips excluded files and directories. File listing visits them (with some exceptions) and annotates excluded files with the reason for exclusion.
* Bundle creation packs the files into a tarball. Manifest creation computes a hash for every file and lists the files and hashes in the manifest. File listing should accumulate files into a tree-structured payload for the frontend.
* The bundle and manifest code reads .rscignore files it finds while traversing directories, and adds the exclusion patterns to the ignore list for the current directory tree walk in progress. When listing files, .rscignore files should be loaded into the ignore list that is being used to annotate excluded files, not the one controlling the FS walk.

So, we need to factor the filesystem iteration code out of the bundle creation (in bundle.go) and make it accept either a function or interface that handles all of the visited files. Directory walking is already based on functions (as in the standard library) so maybe that's cleaner, but these functions accumulate significant state so an interface might be better.

Done: code is refactored, same level of test coverage, tests pass.

description:
### Problem Statement

We need to select a stack that will allow us to move forward quickly, leverage much of the experience the team has but also support the open source status of this project. It would be beneficial if it were to move in the future direction of the Connect dashboard, but is not required.

### Conclusion

Notes can be found below from the investigation.

For everything but the UI Component Library, there were very little doubt in the direction we wanted to go with.

For the UI Component Library, I came up with these requirements:

- Must:
    - Vue 3 compliant
    - Be releasing/maintaining actively
    - Have good help docs
    - Have a rich set of easy-to-use components
    - Have a stepper (wizard)
    - Tree-shakable
    - Have an acceptable security analysis (including dependencies)
    - Support an efficient developer workflow
- Should:
    - Be fixing bugs regarding accessibility
    - Written in Typescript
    - Promote Composition API
    - Theme-able

After my investigations, I chose to move forward with Quasar. It shined above the others in documentation, completeness, security analysis, and community support.

We'll use this choice within the initial stack for prototyping the WebUI client. We'll re-evaluate the choices after we have built up some experience in actually using the technologies (as many of these are new to us - but do represent the communities best/current practices)

- Quasar CLI using pnpm (https://quasar.dev/)

    - Typescript

description:
## Context

#4336 exposes the existing `troubleshootDeploymentFailure` diagnostic as a Positron agent-compatible command. That tool returns the current Publisher logs and is intentionally scoped to deployment-failure troubleshooting.

We should circle back and determine whether agents need a more general, purpose-built way to inspect Publisher logs rather than continuing to reuse a narrowly named diagnostic tool for broader questions. Related UI/error-surfacing work exists in #4203 and #3879, but neither tracks the agent-tool API.

## Questions to investigate

- Which log sources should an agent be able to inspect: the current Publisher log buffer, a specific deployment, Connect/Connect Cloud build or validation logs, or historical runs?
- Should the API support filtering by deployment, time range, severity, operation, or source?
- What structured result would be more useful than returning one unbounded text blob?
- What limits, truncation, redaction, and sensitive-data handling are required before logs enter model context?
- Should generic log inspection be separate from higher-level diagnostic tools that interpret a known failure mode?
- Which capabilities belong in `vscode.lm`, Positron agent-compatible commands, or both?

## Acceptance criteria

- Inventory the log data currently available to the extension and the existing diagnostic/log-related tools.
- Define the intended agent use cases and boundaries for generic log inspection.
- Propose a small, composable tool surface with structured inputs and results, including redaction and output-size behavior.
- Identify overlap or dependencies with #4203 and #3879.
- Create implementation follow-ups once the API shape is agreed.

Related: #4336, #4304, #4305

title: Expose additional Publisher configuration workflows as agent tools
description:
## Context

The current Publisher agent tools cover planning a deployment, deploying content, and opening the credential workflow. Agents still cannot perform many common Publisher configuration tasks that are available through the extension UI, so users must switch contexts to finish preparing a deployment.

## Proposal

Expose a broader, intentional set of Publisher operations through both VS Code Language Model Tools and Positron agent-compatible commands. Initial workflows should include:

- Inspecting and updating the files included in or excluded from a deployment bundle
- Adding and removing secret names from a deployment configuration
- Securely collecting or updating secret values without placing values in tool arguments, model context, logs, or tool results
- Listing, adding, and removing integration requests
- Reading and updating other supported deployment configuration fields where an agent workflow is useful

Prefer small, composable tools with structured inputs and results over a single general-purpose configuration mutation tool. Read operations should be clearly separated from mutations, and destructive or deployment-affecting changes should require explicit user confirmation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and document the initial supported operation set, including which actions are read-only, mutating, or require UI interaction.
- Tools are exposed through both vscode.lm and contributes.commands[].agent, with both paths sharing the same implementation.
- File include/exclude operations use Publisher configuration semantics and validate paths before modifying configuration.
- Secret values are never accepted or returned as agent tool arguments; secure UI or secret storage workflows are used when values are required.
- Integration request operations validate the supported request schema and return actionable errors.
- Mutating operations return structured summaries of what changed.
- Tests cover successful operations, invalid input, cancellation, unsupported configurations, and sensitive-data redaction.
- Tool descriptions tell the agent when user confirmation is required.

Related: #4304, #4305

title: Expose existing diagnostic tools as positronCommands
description:
Publisher already provides these two diagnostic Language Model Tools:

- troubleshootDeploymentFailure
- troubleshootConfigurationError

Expose both as positronCommands, following the same pattern used for the existing deployment tools. The commands should delegate to the existing tool implementations; no new diagnostic behavior is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both existing diagnostic tools are contributed as agent-compatible commands.
- Both commands are registered during extension activation and call the corresponding existing tool implementation.
- The existing vscode.lm tool registrations remain unchanged.
- Tests cover registration and command dispatch.

Related: #4304, #4305

title: Fall back to legacy token auth when OAuth device flow is unavailable
description:
## Summary

Publisher browser sign-in fails against Connect versions that advertise OAuth but do not support RFC 8628 device authorization. Instead of falling back to the existing browser-based token claim flow, Publisher reports:

> OAuth sign-in did not complete: This Connect server does not advertise the OAuth device flow. You can use an API key instead.

This affected a workshop using Publisher v2.9.17. Upgrading Connect to a version with device-flow support made sign-in work, but the upgrade masked a Publisher backward-compatibility regression.

## What happened

1. Publisher discovers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, available on Connect 2026.02.0 and later.
2. Any successful OAuth discovery causes **Sign in with a browser** to select the OAuth path unconditionally.
3. In a web/remote Positron environment, Publisher cannot use the local loopback callback. If no usable Workbench redirect relay is detected, or that relay cannot be used, Publisher selects the device-code flow.
4. Connect 2026.02.0 through 2026.05.x advertise OAuth but do not advertise `device_authorization_endpoint`; device flow requires Connect 2026.06.0 or later.
5. `OAuthClient.startDeviceAuth()` throws because the endpoint is absent. The credential flow then returns to the auth picker with API key as the only functioning alternative.

The legacy token claim flow is currently selected only when OAuth discovery returns no metadata. It is not reconsidered when the available OAuth transports are incompatible with the current editor environment and Connect version.

## Expected behavior

Browser authentication should preserve this compatibility cascade:

1. OAuth authorization code using a viable callback transport
2. OAuth device flow, only when `device_authorization_endpoint` is advertised
3. Legacy browser token claim
4. Manual API key

A Connect server advertising OAuth should not by itself make the legacy token flow unreachable.

## Relevant code

- `extensions/vscode/src/multiStepInputs/newConnectCredential.ts`: `dispatchAuthMethod()` routes browser sign-in to OAuth whenever `oauthMetadata` is non-null.
- `extensions/vscode/src/auth/oauth/activator.ts`: `authorize()` falls back to `deviceCodeFlow()` for web/remote environments and after unsuccessful Workbench/loopback transports without first checking device-flow capability.
- `extensions/vscode/src/auth/oauth/client.ts`: `startDeviceAuth()` correctly rejects metadata without `device_authorization_endpoint`, producing the observed error.

## Test gap

Activator tests use OAuth metadata that always contains `device_authorization_endpoint`. Client tests separately confirm that an absent device endpoint throws, but there is no cross-layer test covering:

- OAuth metadata present
- `device_authorization_endpoint` absent
- web/remote environment, unavailable Workbench relay, rejected Workbench redirect URI, or failed loopback transport

Add coverage for that compatibility matrix and assert that the credential flow proceeds to legacy browser token authentication rather than API-key-only recovery.

## Version context

- Last known-good workshop: July 28, before the OAuth Publisher change shipped.
- OAuth implementation merged July 30 and shipped beginning with Publisher v2.9.14.
- Failure reproduced with Publisher v2.9.17.
- Upgrading Connect to a release supporting the device endpoint allowed the same Publisher flow to complete.

title: set the user-agent header when calling backend apis
description:
## Description

I would like to see the Publisher set a user agent when making http calls to the backend (in particular, Connect Cloud). Currently the user agent looks like this:

```
axios/1.19.0
```

which comes from the client library being used. Contrast this with what `rsconnect` sets:
```
RSConnect/1.11.0
```
